title: fix(sim): a shipped build ignores CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE; a field-engine verdict names its engine
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 0757563d).

## What changed
- **A shipped build ignores `CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE`.** The switch (#637) is honoured only where `CARRY_ENGINE_SWITCH_HONOURED = cfg!(debug_assertions)` holds (dev and test profiles); a release build never reads the variable and always carries stock on the column engine. The read is now the pure `engine_from_switch(value, honoured)` (`crates/app/src/stock_sim_held.rs`, re-exported as `stock_sim::carry_engine_from_switch`). This was the only reader of the variable.
- **A field-engine verdict names its engine, never silently.** New `stock_sim::carry_engine_note()`: `None` on the column engine, else "carried stock judged by the field engine (band N, development switch CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE), not the shipped column engine". It rides the post gate's visible, non-blocking line (`posting::sim_clause` -> post result, status line, G-code header), the setup sheet's `SIM:` line (`setup_sheet::simulate_verdict`) and the GUI Deviate readout (`crates/ui/src/actions.rs`).
- On the column engine nothing changes: no golden, no shipped verdict text moves.
- Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/1168-carry-engine-switch.md`: `debug_assertions` chosen over `cfg(test)` (integration tests link the lib without it, so the carried suites could no longer be run whole on the field arm) and over a cargo feature (a build change, plus `--features` on every field-arm run). No Cargo.toml change. The agreement lane is unaffected: it selects engines per call tree with `with_carry_engine`, in release too.

## Tests
Pinning tests (`crates/app/tests/carried_engine_agreement.rs`, default lane):
- `a_shipped_build_ignores_the_carry_engine_switch` - `engine_from_switch(_, honoured = false)` is the column engine for `field`, ` FIELD `, `column`, empty and unset; honoured, `field` selects the field engine; `CARRY_ENGINE_SWITCH_HONOURED == cfg!(debug_assertions)`.
- `a_verdict_the_field_engine_judged_names_the_engine` - on a carried two-setup document, `sim_clause` and `simulate_verdict` name the field engine (and the switch) under `with_carry_engine(FIELD)`, and add nothing on the column engine.

Gate on the final head (f8a8ff8d), Linux:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: app suites + ui suites ok, 949 passed, 0 failed (4.1 min).
- `carried_engine_agreement` 3 passed, 1 ignored (heavy lane, untouched); `setup_carry` 9/9, `rest_across_setups` 7/7, `carried_verify` 8/8, `carried_fixtures_cache` 6/6.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Not exercised: a real `--release` build run with the variable set (the release behaviour is pinned through the pure gate function and the `cfg!` constant); the heavy `--ignored` agreement lane; macOS/Windows; the GUI readout by hand. `crates/ui/src/actions.rs` is now 403 lines (was 400).

Changelog: A release build no longer reads CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE (always the column carry engine); where the field engine judges, the verdict says so

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1168

title: fix(thread): start the thread mill's feed at the operation's R plane
body:
Stacked on #1219 (on #1137, #1045, #1005). Retarget to `main` before #1219 merges.

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

- **Kernel** (`camcraft-motion`, `machining2d::thread_mill`): `ThreadParams` gains `r_z: Option<f64>`, the R plane. Each feature's rapid stops at `max(R, the ride's run-out)` and the feed down the axis (or beside the boss) starts there; the ride climbs back to it at feed before the link rapid. `None` is the #894 ride, so every existing kernel golden is byte-identical. An R plane below a feature's top, above the link plane, or not finite is refused by name.
- **App** (`thread_op::kernel_params`): passes the resolved `top_z` ("R plane (feed starts here)") as `r_z`, for internal and external threads.
- **Door** (new `operation::thread_r_plane`): a fixed `top_z` below a listed hole's or boss's top is refused when the operation is created, edited or re-tooled. A referenced height resolves at generate, where the kernel asks. The door's R check runs after the tool and feature laws, so their refusals keep their own wording.
- **Stock law** (`thread_r_plane::judge`, called at generate before the #992/#985 way-in laws): every vertical rapid down is read in the prior grid over the mill's full disc. Stock above the rapid's end is refused by name with the stock height and the fix ("raise the R plane (feed starts here) to z ... or above, or machine that stock away"). An unknown prior or an unreadable disc is left to the way-in laws, which already refuse both by name.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1212-thread-r-plane.md`. It covers how the default is seeded: unchanged, Top of Model, and every golden fixture already states R on the feature top.

## Tests (pinning)

- Kernel: `machining2d::thread_tests::the_ride_rapids_to_the_r_plane_and_starts_its_feed_there` (internal and external; an R on the top equals the #894 ride move for move), `an_r_plane_under_a_top_or_over_the_link_plane_is_refused_by_name`.
- Golden (new): `golden_cl::thread_mill_raised_r_plane_matches_golden` -> `tests/golden/thread_mill_raised_r_plane.cl` (R 2 mm over the tops of two holes). **No existing golden moved.**
- App: `thread_entry::the_operations_r_plane_is_where_the_rapid_stops_and_the_feed_starts` (generates, verifies clean, posts through the gate), `an_r_plane_under_the_holes_top_is_refused_when_the_operation_is_made`, `an_r_plane_that_ends_the_rapid_in_the_stock_left_ahead_is_refused_by_name`. Unit: `operation::thread_r_plane::tests::*` (door, stock law).
- Fixture changes: two MCP tests (`mcp::thread_milling_over_the_tools`, `external_thread_milling_over_the_tools`) typed a mouth at z 20 above a 15 mm block, under the default R (top of model). They now sit on the block's top, and the #992/#985 refusals they pin are unchanged. `thread_boss::impossible_bosses_are_refused_when_the_operation_is_made` states R on its 25 mm boss so that the reach refusal it pins is still the one reported.

Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/988-thread-pass-control` on the final head: green (2 steps, 0 failed, 4.1 min) on cfb25dd2. Clippy `-D warnings` on camcraft-motion and camcraft-app: clean.

## Not exercised

- Through the UI page: the Heights tab already shows the R plane, and no UI code changed.
- Posted NC golden with a raised R plane: the CL golden pins the moves, and the post is unchanged.

Changelog: Thread milling rapids to and starts its feed at the operation's R plane (top_z) instead of each hole's or boss's top; an R plane below a feature's top, or one whose rapid would end in stock left by the program ahead, is refused by name.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1212

## What changed

The creation-time family refusal (`family_gate` in `crates/app/src/commands/operation/gates.rs`) said "the setup's machine is a mill" when no machine was mounted. An unmounted setup reads as a mill by default (the kind_of law), so the words misstated it. Verdict unchanged; only the clause differs:

- no machine mounted: `... the setup has no machine mounted - mount a lathe (or a mill-turn) first` (turning), `... the setup has no machine mounted - mount a plasma table first` (plasma)
- machine mounted: unchanged, e.g. `... the setup's machine is a mill - mount a lathe (or a mill-turn) first`

The "milling work ... is a lathe" sibling has no no-machine case (an unmounted setup is judged as a mill, so milling ops are never refused there), so it is untouched.

title: fix(app): judge a tap's cutting moves at its thread's core in the op verify
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 0757563d).

### What changed

The second half of #266. @austin62jake's PR #713 (merged) made the program sim sweep a Tap-kind tool at its thread's core (`tool_law::cutting_radius`, ISO 724 basic minor diameter, `d/2 - 0.5413 p`). As their PR noted, a tap on a tap-drill hole still did not post: the op's own verify convicted the tap's feed in and out (`move 1/2 cuts past the finish surface`) because its tangency and solid laws read the full major diameter against the hole wall.

- New `operation::tap_core` (`acquit`, `core_tool`): for a Z drill cycle with a Tap-kind tool, generate re-runs the same cutting laws (`verify_bodies` + the containment solid law) with the tap cut to its core, and drops each `Gouge` that the core run does not also raise.
- Only `Gouge` is re-read. Rapids, shank, holder and fixture verdicts keep the full diameter (a tap must never rapid into its thread band). It can only remove convictions, never add one; a pitch with no core leaves the full verdict standing.
- Out of scope, unchanged (full diameter, over-reports only): the helical thread mill (`Thread` op), cross holes, tilted (3+2) taps.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/266-tap-core-verify.md`.

title: feat(finish3d): land model - fill closed openings on the drive surface
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 37482923).

## What changed

A 3D Finish option, **Fill openings** (`fill_openings`, mm, off by default), for the land case in #1196: the finish flies over bolt holes and small pockets at their rim instead of diving down their walls.

**The fill rule** (`crates/motion/src/finishing3d/fill.rs`, new):
- Sample the model's top-down height field on a grid (cell = width/12, coarsened to at most 4M cells; a width too fine for the model at that cap is refused by name). Cells over no facet read as the model's lowest Z.
- Grey-scale morphological closing with a flat disk of the stated diameter (Serra 1982; Soille 2003). A cell raised by more than the finish tolerance is an opening cell.
- A connected group is filled only when it is **closed**: none of it on the grid border, and every bordering cell is material standing at the lid's level (within one cell's 45-degree rise + tol). Slots or valleys that run out to an edge, or a lid that would spill over a lower rim, are never filled.
- Lids (horizontal rectangles at the closed height, never below the surface) cover the group plus its neighbour ring.

**Safety:** the drive facets are the model's facets, unchanged and first, plus lids, so a path planned on them can rise but never bite the model deeper. Only the path is planned on the lids. The verifier still gets `material.facets` (the real model), so a gouge under a lid is still caught. The path gets a `land: N closed opening(s) narrower than W mm filled at their rim and flown over, not cut ...` note.

**Plumbing:** `OpParams::Finish3D.fill_openings: Option<f64>` (undoable through `EditOperationParams`; sanity refuses a non-finite or non-positive width at the door). The optional `fill_openings` file key is absent when None. The MCP params door carries it (`edit_operation {"fill_openings": 5.0}`). The stamp digest gets bytes only when a width is set. There's a "Fill openings" field on the 3D Finish page. Geodesic + fill is refused by name, because the lids would be new open boundary for its march. There's no project-file version bump: an older reader ignores the key and cuts the model itself, which is a valid finish, not an unsafe one. The reasoning is in `docs/decisions/1196-finish3d-land-fill.md`.

**Option off is byte-identical:** no file key, no digest bytes, and the generators get `&material.facets` as before. No goldens moved.

## Tests
- `crates/motion/tests/finish3d_land.rs` (new):
  - `land_finish_flies_over_the_bolt_holes_and_verifies_on_the_real_plate`: a 40x20x8 plate with two 3.4 mm through holes and a 3 mm ball. Waterline and Parallel with fill on: no tip inside a hole below the top. The deepest ball bite measured on the REAL plate is within tol. The same path sunk 0.5 mm is caught on the real plate. The raster crosses the mouths at the top with fill on and doesn't with it off.
  - `a_blind_pocket_is_lidded_and_a_gouge_into_its_floor_is_convicted`: off dives to the pocket floor and on never does. A plunge planted through the lid into the pocket floor is caught on the real model.
  - `an_opening_wider_than_the_width_or_open_to_the_edge_is_not_filled`: a 3 mm width doesn't fill a 3.4 mm hole (output is exactly the model), and an edge-to-edge slot stays open.
  - `nonsense_widths_are_refused_by_name`: 0, negative, NaN, inf, a too-fine width and an empty model.
- `crates/app/tests/operations.rs` `finish3d_fill_openings_lands_over_a_pocket_and_verifies_on_the_model`: end to end through `GenerateOperation`. Off rides the pocket floor. On never descends, status Ok (the real-model verify is clean), and the land note is present. A negative width is refused at `CreateOperation`.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp.rs` `fill_openings_rides_the_params_door_and_undoes`: off by default, set over MCP, 0 refused, generate ok, and undo restores off.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`) on the final head: green on 0754f88c (motion 190 s, app 599 s, ui 74 s; 0 failed). Clippy `-D warnings` is clean on motion, app and ui.

## Not exercised
- The reporter's STEP part (not attached). The fixtures are square-hole plates.
- The finish3d heavy (`--ignored`) envelope lane: no existing generator changed, and the fill is opt-in.
- The UI field is only compile-checked. No snapshot PNGs changed.

Changelog: 3D Finish can fill closed holes and pockets narrower than a stated width on the planned surface ("Fill openings"), flying over them as a land finish while the verifier still judges the real model (#1196)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1196

- `site/README.md`: a short note on search and `vendor/`.

No `.github/` change: the existing `zola build` in the `site` job picks up the config, so the maintainer does not need to touch the workflow.

title: feat(vise): self-centering grip jaw - a step the stock sits on
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 37482923).

## What changed
- `vise::SelfCentering` gains `grip_depth` / `grip_width` (mm, 0 = off): a grip jaw, a step cut into each jaw's inside top edge. The jaw profile walks down the face to the ledge, in along it, down to the floor; the frame's z = 0 is the ledge (the floor the part sits on), so the vise body drops by `jaw_height - grip_depth`. Fit and an in-place `SetVise` edit both keep the stock seated on the ledge; the fixture/collision laws, stock simulation and the post gate read the stepped mesh.
- Law (`check_grip`, refused by name at command creation): both figures or neither; finite, non-negative; depth < jaw height; width < jaw thickness; opening > 2 x width (ledges would meet under the stock); dovetail lip and grip step not both ("a dovetail or a grip jaw, not both").
- `ViseParams::seat_height()` / `SelfCentering::seat()`.
- Project: two optional keys on the `self_centering` object, written only when non-zero; older files read as no step and a stepless vise writes byte for byte as before. No project version move.
- Dialog: "Grip step depth" / "Grip step width" rows with tooltips (dovetail rows get one too); the fit line says the stock sits on the grip steps and how far above the vise floor.
- MCP: `add_builtin_vise` / `set_vise` `dimensions` take `grip_depth` / `grip_width`; the vise view reports them.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1274-grip-jaw.md`.

## Tests
- `crates/app/tests/self_centering_grip_jaw.rs` (new): `the_grip_jaw_carries_the_step_and_its_seat_is_the_frame_origin` (volume, bounds, steel/air at ledge and jaw), `bad_grip_figures_are_refused_by_name`, `a_grip_vise_seats_the_stock_on_the_ledge` (vise sits 12 mm lower than bed-seated for a 3 mm step on a 15 mm jaw), `the_fixture_law_judges_the_stepped_jaw` (face pass at z 9.5 struck by bed-seated jaws, clear on the grip step; pass at z 1 into the step blocks the post), `an_older_vise_key_reads_and_writes_unchanged_and_a_grip_round_trips` (old key byte for byte; save/reload; undo/redo).
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_self_centering_vise.rs`: grip dims through `set_vise`, refusals named, undo count.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/fixture_self_centering_tests.rs`: grip rows present for self-centering only; `a_grip_jaw_seats_the_stock_on_its_steps_and_places_in_one_step` (structural; no snapshot PNGs).
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`) and clippy `-D warnings` on app/ui on the final head f0e63454: green (app suites 18 s, ui suites 83 s; 0 failed); clippy clean.

## Not exercised
- Posed (tilted) grip vises in the 5-axis fixture laws beyond the shared mesh path; setup sheet (it does not state jaw forms).
- An older build re-editing a grip vise would drop the step (it keeps the saved facets until edited) - noted in the decision file.

title: docs(site): keyboard shortcut and mouse reference
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 37482923fc858b4ba3c4c600504020ef2489f1b0).

## What changed

- New guide page `site/content/guide/keyboard-and-mouse.md` (weight 7): every keyboard shortcut and mouse gesture bound in `crates/ui`, with Windows/Linux and macOS columns. Egui's `command` modifier is Cmd on macOS. Pick modifiers use the physical Control key on every platform.
- `site/content/guide/first-run.md`: one paragraph linking to the new page.
- Docs only. No Rust, no snapshot, no test changes.

## Verified rows (source)

Keyboard, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/panes.rs` `shortcuts()`:
- New Ctrl/Cmd+N, Open model Ctrl/Cmd+O, Open project Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+O, Save +S, Save As +Shift+S, Post +P: gated by `cmd && !typing`.
- Quit Ctrl/Cmd+Q (same block). macOS Cmd+Q also via `egui_app/os_quit.rs`.
- Undo Ctrl/Cmd+Z (no shift/alt). Redo Ctrl/Cmd+Y or +Shift+Y. Not gated by typing.
- Copy operation Ctrl/Cmd+C (needs a selected operation), Paste Ctrl/Cmd+V: `cmd && !typing`.
- Delete key (`Key::Delete`), gated by `!typing`. On a Mac this is Fn+Delete (forward delete) - not checked on hardware.
- F frames all (`!typing && !cmd && !alt`). Bare P toggles perspective/ortho (same guard).
- Enter commits a typed value: `egui_app/op_page.rs:83`, `egui_app/step_budget_row.rs:24`.

Viewport mouse, `egui_app/shell.rs` (~L415-520) and `interact.rs`:
- Left drag past `CLICK_TRAVEL_PX` (4 px) orbits; middle drag orbits.
- Right drag pans. Right click with no movement does nothing; the viewport has no context menu.
- Mouse wheel and `smooth_scroll_delta` dolly toward the cursor (`cam.dolly_cursor`). Two-finger scroll is the same path on a trackpad.
- Pinch (`zoom_delta`) is read only in `egui_app/tool_body_page.rs`, not in the viewport: listed under Not bound yet.
- Left click (release within 4 px) picks through `interact::pick_at`; a miss clears the model selection (`pick_model`).
- ViewCube: `egui_app/viewcube.rs` `click()` orients the view on a cube hit, and runs nav buttons.

Picking modifiers, `interact.rs` `Mods` (`ctrl` = physical Control), `edge_pick.rs`, `feature_click.rs`, `boundary_draft.rs`:
- Feature pick: plain replaces; Ctrl or Shift appends (`feature_click.rs:191`). Adding an already-picked face or vertex is refused with "already selected" (`interact.rs` `queue_feature_pick`).
- Edge mode: Ctrl toggles one edge (removes it when already picked), Shift takes the whole face loop, Alt one segment (`feature_click.rs` `ask`, `edge_pick.rs`).
- Boundary: Ctrl toggles, Shift closes around the face loop, plain replaces (`boundary_draft::PickMods`).

title: test(machine): pin that a machine switch is judged again at the post
body:
## What changed

This PR adds tests and a decision record. It changes no product code.

Issue #1241 asked whether a toolpath generated and cleared on machine A can post on machine B without being checked against B. A remount happens two ways: through the setup's own machine (`SetSetupMachine`) or through the document's machine (`LoadMachine`), which the setup follows. The new suite `crates/app/tests/machine_switch.rs` traces both.

**Result: only the display is stale. No path posts on B without being checked.** For every law the post checks the cached path again, against the machine the op's setup mounts now:

| Law (path made on A, mounted on B) | Op status after the switch | Gate / post on B |
|---|---|---|
| Travel (B: +/-10 mm) | Ok | refused: `machine TightMill: ... Face1: move N reaches ... the stroke is -10.000..10.000` |
| Spindle max rpm (B: 1000) | Ok | refused: `Face1: tool EM-0400-2FL runs ... above the machine's 1000` |
| Rotary (tilt-head to VMC 3-axis, leaning pocket) | Ok | refused: `P: move N tilts the tool; ... states no tilting rotary` |
| Machine kind (mill to Lathe) | Ok | refused: `Face1: a ... operation cannot run on its setup's ... machine` |

Every refusal writes no file. The same results hold through each switch route (setup and document), after undo (A is back and the program posts), after redo, and after save and reopen.

The op still reads Ok after a switch on purpose. This is the M2.3 "roomy-one" law: machine limits and workholding feed the post's live gate and are never part of the op stamp. It is pinned by `fixtures.rs::workholding_never_stales_a_fresh_toolpath` ("loading a machine must not re-generate the program"). M3.2 B once tried a machine digest term in the stamp and reverted it. So the issue's "Done means" is met by its "or the issue records why it need not" branch. `docs/decisions/1241-machine-switch-live-gate.md` records the decision, the options I dropped (stamping the machine identity, or only the fields generation reads), and what it would cost to change if the maintainer wants a switch to show ops as stale.

## How tested

- Pinning tests, `crates/app/tests/machine_switch.rs` (6):
  - `a_setups_new_machine_judges_stroke_and_spindle_at_the_post`
  - `the_documents_new_machine_judges_stroke_and_spindle_at_the_post`
  - `a_setups_new_machine_without_the_rotary_refuses_the_lean`
  - `the_documents_new_machine_without_the_rotary_refuses_the_lean`
  - `a_setups_new_machine_of_another_kind_refuses_the_family`
  - `the_documents_new_machine_of_another_kind_refuses_the_family`
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, 6 of 6.
- Neighbouring suites: `setup_mount`, `fixtures`, `post_not_judged` and `machine` all green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --tests -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The per-mount post (`post_mounts`), where setups run on different machines. It uses the same `machine_problems` gate.
- The spindle-body and table steel after a switch. These are checked by the live fixture gate (`fixture_struck` reads the setup's current machine), and the existing fixture suites pin that.
- The UI. The UI test comment the issue quotes (`setup_mount_pages.rs`) is not on upstream main.

Edge and feature picks added to the selection on Ctrl. On macOS Control is the secondary (right) click, so a Mac user could not Ctrl+click to add an edge chain to an operation's picks, while the keyboard shortcuts already use the command modifier.

- `interact::Mods.ctrl` is renamed to `Mods.command`. It is built from egui's `modifiers.command` (Cmd on macOS, Ctrl elsewhere) through a new `From<egui::Modifiers>` impl, which the shell now uses.

title: fix(verify): a polygon declared at its corner circle earns no full rim credit
body:
Stacked on #1228 (base it on main once #1228 merges; this branch carries #1228's two commits).
Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
- #1228 credits a facet edge its whole chord dip when both of its ends lie on a declared hole rim. That left a gap: a hole that is really a coarse polygon, declared or recognized at its corner circle, kept the full credit on its flats. A drill cycle's own rim (tool diameter / 2) left the same gap.
- `crates/sim/src/verify/solid_index.rs` (`on_rim`): a rim chord now also has to dip at most `RIM_SAG_MAX` (0.05 mm) inside its circle, `r - sqrt(r^2 - l^2/4)`.
  - A deeper chord counts as a polygon's flat. It gets the 0.01 mm mesh credit, like every off-rim edge.
  - An octagon on r 5 (flats 0.38 mm deep) or a 16-gon on r 5 (0.096 mm) now convicts against a drill, bore or thread of the corner-circle size.
- The fix sits in the verifier rather than the recognizer. The hole list is editable data, and the drill's own rim bypasses the recognizer, so the verifier is the one gate every path goes through.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1231-rim-sagitta-bound.md` (it also lists what was dropped: inscribed-radius declaration, the STEP `ReducedFidelity` chord, the surface type, a segment-count rule).

## Tests
- New in `crates/app/tests/hole_wall_chord.rs`:
  - `a_polygon_declared_at_its_corner_circle_still_convicts_on_its_flats`: 8-gon and 16-gon on r 5, rim declared at r 5; a drill, bore orbit and thread helix each convict. It fails with the bound removed (checked).
  - `a_small_tessellated_round_hole_keeps_its_rim_credit`: 16-gon r 2 (0.038 mm), a matched 4 mm drill on its rim is clean.
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/1217-chord-dip-excuse` on the final head: green (sim lib, midmove_pose, posed_rapids, motion solid_law, app hole_wall_chord, probe_reach, real_tip_contour, tool_body_drill_probe).
- Also run by hand, all green:
  - app `solid_law_goldens` (drill_plate, tap_plate), `golden_cl`, `bore_facet_sagitta`, `solid_law`, `conformance`, `fanuc_post`;
  - `operations` drill tests, including `drill_op_recognizes_from_the_model_then_machines_clean`.
- Clippy `-D warnings` on camcraft-sim and camcraft-app (all targets): clean.
- No golden or snapshot changed.

## Not exercised
- Real coarse STL exports: any round hole that dips more than 0.05 mm is now judged as a polygon. That is a refusal, not a pass.
- The batch and release tiers.

Changelog: Verify: a polygonal hole declared or drilled at its corner circle no longer has its flats excused; a chord counts as round-hole tessellation only when it dips at most 0.05 mm (#1231)

title: fix(verify): hole-wall chord-dip excuse only on a declared rim, never a polygon's flats
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (cut from upstream/main 12a6dcbf).

## What changed
The containment kinds' hole-wall excuse (`swept::chord_dip`, read by `solid_index` under `SolidLaw::hole_walls`) used to credit every facet chord's full dip into the swept disc. That let a coarse polygon hole's flats be cut silently. It now judges each facet edge on its own:
- **An edge with both ends on a declared rim circle** (within `RIM_TOL` = `DEV_TOL`, 0.01 mm, in XY, on an upright move) is a chord of the round wall that the region judges exactly. It keeps its whole dip.
- **Any other edge** is credited at most `HOLE_CHORD_CREDIT` = `DEV_TOL`, 0.01 mm. That is the mesh tolerance, and the same value #1099 uses for its thread grant.
- **Where the rims come from:** `generate::contain_into` builds them from the op's `holes` (Drill, Bore, Thread), using each hole's circle. A drill cycle also gets its own diameter at the hole centre, because a drill or tap cuts its own size there (the `tap_plate` case). They are passed through the new `verify::solid_hits_rims` and `verify::HoleRim`.
- **Callers without rims:** `solid_hits` keeps its signature and passes no rims, so the cross-drill and probe laws get only the 0.01 mm credit. Their suites are green.
- **The issue's case now convicts:** the octagon's corners at r 5 are on no declared rim (the thread was declared at r 4.4), so its flats are judged and the cut is a Gouge.

**Why not a bare 0.01 mm cap.** That was the first commit on this branch. It false-gouged pinned round holes: `drill_op_recognizes_from_the_model_then_machines_clean` (a 16-gon r 2 that dips 0.038 mm), plus the `drill_plate` and `tap_plate` goldens (32-gons). It would have done the same on every coarse STL drilled hole.

**Residual, stated in `docs/decisions/1217-chord-dip-credit.md`.** A hole declared or recognized at a polygon's own corner circle is still excused on its flats, because the declaration says it is round. Only the recognizer could tell the two apart.

**Interaction with #1099 (open, #1071):** the two PRs touch different files and both use the 0.01 mm credit. This PR's constant is private and named `HOLE_CHORD_CREDIT`, so it does not collide with #1099's `verify::CHORD_CREDIT`.

## Tests
- New `crates/app/tests/hole_wall_chord.rs` (the first and third fail under the old full credit; the second passes both before and after):
  - `a_coarse_polygon_holes_flats_cut_by_a_containment_kind_convict`: an octagon and a 16-gon (corners on r 5), cut out to r 5 by a bore orbit and a thread-mill helix with the rim declared at r 4.4 or with no rim, and by a drill with no rim. Each is a Gouge.
  - `a_full_fidelity_round_hole_stays_clean_for_every_containment_kind`: a 96-gon hole stays clean for the drill, bore and helix, with or without its rim.
  - `a_coarse_round_hole_is_excused_only_on_its_declared_rim`: a 32-gon at r 5 stays clean on its declared rim (drill and bore). A drill gouges when the rim is declared at r 4.4.
- `solid_law_goldens`: its `contain_law` harness now passes the drill cycle's rims, as `contain_into` does. **No golden files changed.**
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`) on the final head: **green** (sim 12 s, motion 4 s, 76 app suites 334 s).
- Also run by hand on the final head: 32 containment-related app suites, including `golden_cl`, `solid_law`, `solid_law_goldens`, `operations`, `coarse_contain`, `drilling_cross*` and `tap_sim`. All green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No snapshot PNGs changed.

## Not exercised
- The release-lane `--ignored` heavy suites.
- The issue's Thread reproduction through the full op path (`#1071`'s `thread_mill_rim` fixture lives on #1099's branch). It is pinned at the `solid_hits_rims` seam with the same declared-r 4.4 octagon geometry.
- Tilted (non-upright) containment moves: they read no world-XY rim and get only the capped credit. That is stricter, never looser.

Changelog: The containment kinds' (drill, bore, thread) solid law no longer excuses a cut into a polygonal hole's flats: a hole-wall chord's full dip is excused only on a declared hole rim, any other at most 0.01 mm (#1217)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1217

title: build(process): refresh a conflicting PR only at merge time; merge-plan planner
body:
Process change (#1221, P4, effort:high). Branch synced from `origin/main` at 7a5816cf. The five points of the issue, in order.

## What changed

1. **Refresh only at merge time.** AGENTS.md: new rule "Refresh only at merge time" (the maintainer's words quoted, 2026-11-12). A conflicting PR carries `conflicts` and is otherwise left alone. The start-of-session contributor refresh is marked superseded (quote kept). `resolve-conflicts` contributor mode is the merge-time tool; its maintainer `check` asks an author only for a PR in the batch about to merge, and never for others. `review-prs` 2b and `PR-reviewer` follow.
2. **Planner in the repo.** `cargo xtask merge-plan <PR>...`, `--label <name>`, `--delta <PR> --reviewed <sha>` (plus `--repo`, `--remote`, `--base`). Pure ordering in `xtask/src/merge_plan.rs` (waves, stacks, shared history, the trial callback); pure delta classes in `xtask/src/merge_delta.rs`; git/gh side in `xtask/src/merge_plan_git.rs` (`gh pr list`, `git fetch`, `git merge-tree --write-tree`, `git commit-tree`, `git show --remerge-diff`; nothing checked out, built or pushed). Unit tests in `xtask/src/merge_plan_tests.rs`. One deliberate difference from the reference script: a child whose parent was deferred in wave 1 is deferred too (the reference would have merged it and pulled the parent's changes in silently). Pinned by `three_way_clash_defers_the_merge_and_its_child`.
3. **A clean merge of main keeps its review.** AGENTS.md section of that name. `--delta` says SAME (only merges of main, empty remerge-diff: review and `merge-ready` stand, no agent) or MECHANICAL (hand edits only in settled files: read by the merging session); DELTA gets a delta review, NEW CODE/Rewritten a full one. The draft rule in AGENTS.md gets the one exception: a clean merge of main keeps the ready flag; any other merge still turns it back into a draft. `review-prs` step 1 skips a head whose new commits are SAME; `PR-reviewer` skip check does the same.
4. **Only the owner's reviews count** (#1207, "No, only ours count"). `review-prs` step 1 query reads markers only from comments/reviews whose author is the owner (`gh repo view NeoTech/Camcraft --json owner`). `merge-ready` without an owner marker for the PR (current head, or an earlier head that `--delta` says SAME/MECHANICAL) is removed with a one-line comment. `PR-reviewer` skip check and `resolve-conflicts check` filter on the author too. AGENTS.md "Outside PRs are reviewed" names the rule.
5. **One gate per batch.** AGENTS.md "Fixes are tested in the background": one batch-tier gate per merge batch, not per merge.

Also: `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` 30 to 31. Decision note: `docs/decisions/1221-merge-time-refresh.md`.

**PROCESS_VERSION 31** - what changed: refresh of conflicting PRs only at merge time (no start-of-session refreshes); the merge-order planner (`cargo xtask merge-plan`); clean merges of main keep their review; only the owner's markers and `merge-ready` count.
What a fork must do: stop the start-of-session contributor refreshes; stop marking and labelling your own PRs (the owner's account does that); pull the process files:
`git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION xtask .cargo/config.toml scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh scripts/release.ps1 scripts/collect-decisions.ps1 scripts/collect-decisions.sh`
(the announcement on #681 is made by the merging session when this merges.)

## How tested

- `cargo test -p xtask --bin xtask merge` : 16 passed, 0 failed. Names: `independent_prs_form_one_wave_docs_first_then_cool_then_hot`, `base_conflict_is_refreshed_after_wave_one_and_is_clean_then`, `pair_clash_on_mechanical_files_is_a_mechanical_refresh`, `code_conflict_after_wave_one_is_by_hand`, `stacked_child_merges_after_its_parent_even_when_it_is_docs_only`, `child_of_a_deferred_parent_is_deferred_too`, `shared_history_puts_the_side_with_fewer_own_commits_first`, `three_way_clash_defers_the_merge_and_its_child`, `render_names_both_waves`, `mechanical_is_the_settled_files_and_snapshots`, and the six `delta_*` tests.
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: green on the first run (xtask unit tests, 6 s).
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Live, read-only, from the worktree (outputs below): `merge-plan 1211 1216 1203`, `merge-plan --delta 1131 --reviewed 05a44be7`, and `merge-plan --label merge-ready`. The owner lookup and the owner-filtered review query in `review-prs` step 1 were also run live.

```
$ cargo xtask merge-plan 1211 1216 1203
base 7a5816cf

WAVE 1 - merge in this order; no head moves, so no refresh and no delta review (2):
  #1211  fix(ui): workholding lives under Fixtures in every state
  #1216  feat(ui): tool kind glyphs on the Tool library catalog rows and the tool picker

WAVE 2 - one at a time: refresh against the main of that moment, check, merge, THEN the next (1):
  #1203  [by hand] conflicts with main now: crates/ui/src/egui_app/viewcube.rs
         feat(ui): viewport bottom control bar holds the view buttons (#1198 slice a)

$ cargo xtask merge-plan --delta 1131 --reviewed 05a44be7
NEW CODE: new commits since the review: a review of `git diff <reviewed>..<head>` for those commits
  c6091eca merge of main, no hand edits
  2c1efae9 commit: test(lathe_voice): SinkerBurn is a refused kind on the lathe (#541 wit

$ cargo xtask merge-plan --label merge-ready

  #1216  feat(ui): tool kind glyphs on the Tool library catalog rows and the tool picker
```

## Not exercised

- Windows only: built and run on Windows here. macOS and Linux are not built in this session (the code uses only `std`, `git` and `gh`; no platform paths).
- The skills are instructions: the `/resolve-conflicts` and `/review-prs` flows were not run end to end on a real conflicting PR (no PR was refreshed or labelled by this change).
- Wave 2 with several deferred PRs and a long simulated chain (the commit cache past one or two prefixes) was covered by unit tests with a fake merge oracle, not by a live run.
- The `--delta` path on a real merge of main with an empty remerge-diff was not run live (no such PR among the three above; the classification is unit-tested).

title: test: trace a setup's own machine and post to the posted files
body:
## What changed

This PR is test-only. It traces a setup's own machine and post from the pick to the bytes in the posted files (#1224), on top of the #1206 UI pins already in this PR. No product code changed.

Fixture (app): Setup1 follows the document, which mounts **machine A** (the shipped VMC 3-axis) and **post A** (the built-in Fanuc). Setup2 owns **machine B** (the shipped Tormach 770M, a 10000 rpm spindle) and **post B** (Siemens 840D). Each setup cuts its own box: Setup1 has Face1a then Face1b at G54, Setup2 has Face2 at G55. The tests check dialect markers, not only file counts. Fanuc files carry `%`, `O0001 (<machine>)` and `M30`. Siemens files carry `; <machine>`, `N10 G17 G710` and `M2`. Each header names its own machine.

- `crates/app/tests/setup_mount_trace.rs` (new, 6 tests)
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_setup_mount_trace.rs` (new, 1 test)
- `crates/app/tests/setup_mounts_post.rs`: two edge tests. One is `#[ignore = "#1232: ..."]`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/setup_mount_pages.rs`: the #1206 two-mount pin now also posts through the shell's own `PostProgramFile` command. It reads both files from disk and checks Fanuc on the VMC and Haas on the tilt head, each holding only its own setup's work.
- `docs/decisions/1224-setup-mount-trace.md`

## Failing rows (filed, not fixed here)

- **#1232 (P1)**, row 7: a lathe setup's turning operation, posted through the setup's own milling post (Haas), is written as a milling program (`G17`, `T2 M6`, `G43 H2`, `S3000 M3`, facing as `Y` moves at `X0`). It should be refused. Pinned by `an_own_milling_post_on_a_lathe_setup_is_refused_by_name` (ignored).
- **#1233 (P5)**, the MCP half of row 1: no MCP tool sets a setup's own post, so the MCP leg covers the machine pick only. The post pick is pinned app-side.

## Trace table

| Row | Test (path) | Result |
|---|---|---|
| 1 Stored | `each_mount_file_is_its_own_post_machine_ops_and_work_offset` (app `setup_mount_trace.rs`, new): the document, Setup1 and Setup2 each hold their own machine and post. UI: `the_setup_machine_page_takes_its_own_machine`, `the_setup_post_page_takes_its_own_post_through_the_picker`, `the_setup_machine_page_picks_its_own_machine_from_the_library` (ui `setup_mount_pages.rs`, #1206). MCP: `a_setups_own_machine_picked_over_mcp_reaches_its_own_posted_file_and_undoes` (app `mcp_setup_mount_trace.rs`, new) and existing `setups_declare_activate_and_post_their_own_word` (app `mcp_setup.rs`) | pass. The MCP post pick has no tool: #1233 |
| 2 Generated (other setup active) | `each_mount_file_is_its_own_post_machine_ops_and_work_offset` (new: Setup1's operations are generated with Setup2 active, and the reverse). Existing: `an_inactive_setups_op_generates_on_its_own_machine_without_activation` (mill/lathe kind law, `setup_mounts_post.rs`), `two_setups_on_different_machines_are_judged_on_their_own_and_the_ribbon_follows_the_active` (`setup_mount.rs`), `the_z_stroke_cap_reads_the_ops_own_setups_machine_not_the_active_one` (`fixture_route.rs`) | pass |
| 3 Verified / simulated | New: `a_spindle_limit_is_judged_on_each_ops_own_machine_from_either_active_setup` (12000 rpm refused on machine B only, naming Face2, nothing written) and `a_rotary_index_swing_is_judged_on_each_ops_own_machine` (a work-turning A with no nose height refuses only the ops of the setup that mounts it). Existing: `a_travel_limit_is_judged_on_the_ops_own_machine_only` (`setup_mounts_post.rs`), `the_struck_check_judges_each_op_on_its_own_setups_spindle` (`fixture_ux.rs`), the lathe file's `G50 S12000` from its own machine (`a_mill_and_a_lathe_post_two_files_each_byte_identical_to_posting_it_alone`), workholding rpm per setup (`lathe_workholding_rpm.rs`) | pass |
| 4 Posted | `each_mount_file_is_its_own_post_machine_ops_and_work_offset` (new): two files `_01_Setup1.nc` and `_02_Setup2.nc`. Each is in its own dialect and names its own machine. Each holds only its own operations in order (Face1a before Face1b) at its own work offset (G54 / G55). The bytes are the same whichever setup is active. UI: `each_setup_picks_its_own_machine_and_post_and_posts_one_file_per_mount` (extended: shell Post command, dialect asserts) | pass |
| 5 Follow the document | `the_document_mount_moves_only_the_following_setup_and_untick_follows_again` (new): a new document machine and post (Tilt-head 5-axis, Haas) change Setup1's file and leave every byte of Setup2's. Unticking Setup2's own post, then its own machine, makes it follow the document (one file at the end). Each untick is one undo step back to the earlier output | pass |
| 6 Round trip | `two_mounts_round_trip_byte_identical_and_undo_redo_restores_each_output` (new): save, reopen, post gives byte-identical files. Undo and redo of the machine pick and of the post pick each restore the earlier output. Existing: `a_setups_own_machine_and_post_round_trip_and_undo` (`setup_mount.rs`), `the_script_post_writes_one_file_per_mount` (`setup_mounts_post.rs`) | pass |
| 7 Edges | `the_same_own_mount_is_one_file_and_half_a_mount_is_two` (new): both setups owning machine B and post B give one file through Siemens for machine B with G54 and G55, as `program_mounts` groups. An own machine with a followed post gives two Fanuc files. The reverse gives one machine in two dialects. `an_own_lathe_post_on_a_mill_setup_is_refused_by_name` (new, `setup_mounts_post.rs`): refused (#1190 door), nothing written. `an_own_milling_post_on_a_lathe_setup_is_refused_by_name` (new, ignored) | **lathe setup + milling post: FAILS, #1232**. The rest pass |

## How tested

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: green on the first run. It ran app `mcp_setup_mount_trace` and `setup_mount_trace` (new suites), `setup_mounts_post::an_own_lathe_post_on_a_mill_setup_is_refused_by_name`, the ui lib unit tests, and ui `boundary`, `boundary_picks` and `theme_files`.
- Each new test was also run by name: `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test setup_mount_trace` (6 passed), `--test mcp_setup_mount_trace` (1 passed), `--test setup_mounts_post -- an_own_ --include-ignored` (the #1232 pin fails as filed), and `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- setup_mount_pages` (4 passed).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test setup_mount_trace --test mcp_setup_mount_trace --test setup_mounts_post -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --lib --tests -- -D warnings`: clean.

## What was not exercised

- No posted file was run on a real control or a control simulator. The dialect checks are text markers.
- Nothing was looked at on screen. The UI leg drives clicks headlessly.
- The single-file post of a lathe document whose document post is a milling dialect was not run. #1232 says it is very likely the same path.
- A user's own `.cps` as a setup's own post was not traced.

title: fix(sim): the hole-wall excuse measures a facet about its hole's axis, so a tool cutting into a flat is a gouge
body:
## What changed

The containment kinds' hole-wall excuse in the solid law (drill, bore, thread mill, cross drill) read a facet by its **corners** against the **tool's own disc** (`swept.rs` `chord_dip`). If every vertex stood outside the tool, the facet was forgiven its edges' dip into it. That bound grows as the tool shrinks against the hole. Every flat whose corners lie on the hole circle (an octagon, a D-bore, a square) passes inside that circle along its middle, and a cut there got no blocking warning.

Now:
- The operation names its holes' axes: `verify::solid_hits_walled(path, facets, cutter, law, &[HoleAxis])`. `generate::contain_into` passes the op's Drill/Bore/Thread holes, and `cross_part` passes the cross holes' lines. `solid_hits` is unchanged for every other caller. With no holes named, nothing is excused.
- New `crates/sim/src/verify/hole_wall.rs`. A facet is excused only when it is a **round wall** of one of those holes. Its sagitta about the hole axis must be at most `WALL_SAG` = 0.05 mm. The sagitta is the nearest vertex's radius less the facet's **nearest approach** to the axis (point-to-segment, or point-in-triangle, in the plane square to the axis).
- The excuse granted is the smaller of that sagitta and the old edge-dip bound, so the law can only convict more than before, never less.
- A facet with any non-finite coordinate excuses nothing. So does a facet over the axis, or a hole axis that is not along the move's tool axis (`Frame::axis_xy`).
- `chord_dip` is removed. The decisions are in `docs/decisions/1205-hole-wall-nearest-point.md`: why a cap is needed on top of the nearest-point reading, why 0.05 mm, and what was dropped.

Why there is a cap: an octagon *is* an inscribed polygon of its corners' circle, with a 0.38 mm sagitta on r 5. So a nearest-point measurement alone still excuses a cut to its corners. Only a stated bound on what counts as tessellation tells a coarse circle from a flat. That is the issue's "passes inside the circle by more than the stated tolerance convicts".

## Probe readings (before = main's rule, after = this PR; the same build with the old rule toggled by a throwaway switch, since removed)

| Case (plate, blind hole, corners on the circle) | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Thread mill 6 mm p1, declared r 4.4 (major 4.94), octagon on r 5: solid law | **0** gouges | 38 |
| same, D-bore (96-gon r 5, flat chord at Y 4) | **0** | 22 |
| same, 32-gon at the major circle (the thread's own round wall) | 0 | 0 |
| Bore EM-0600 at r 5, octagon on r 5 (0.38 mm into each flat): op verdict | **0** | 10 |
| Bore at r 5, D-bore | **0** | 4 |
| Bore at r 5, 32-gon on r 5 (0.024 mm sagitta, past the 0.01 tolerance) | 0 | 0 |
| Bore at r 4.6, octagon on r 5 (inside the 4.62 flats) | 0 | 0 |
| Bore at r 5, 23-gon (sagitta 0.0466, under the cap) | 0 | 0 |
| Bore at r 5, 22-gon (sagitta 0.0509, over the cap) | 0 | 10 |
| Drill DR-0600, octagon on r 3 (flats at 2.77) | **0** | 1 |
| Drill DR-0600, 32-gon on r 3 | 0 | 0 |

Thread note: on main, a model-sourced **Thread op** is already refused by its region law (the helix cuts past the declared minor circle by design; that is #1071, which PR #1099 grants). So the op-level probe gives 52 blocking warnings before and after. The reviewer's 0 was read on #1099's tree. The thread rows above therefore judge the generator's own helix with the solid law alone, as `contain_into` runs it. That is the verdict that stands once #1099 lifts the region law.

## Tests

- New `crates/app/tests/hole_wall_flats.rs` (4 tests):
  - `a_thread_mill_cutting_into_an_octagons_flats_is_a_gouge`: the reviewer's probe, plus the D-bore and the round-wall control.
  - `a_bore_or_drill_into_an_octagons_flats_is_a_gouge`
  - `a_round_tool_in_a_finely_faceted_round_hole_still_verifies_clean`
  - `the_wall_excuse_ends_at_its_stated_sagitta`: the boundary pin, 23-gon clean / 22-gon convicts on r 5.
- New unit tests in `hole_wall.rs`: `a_chord_reads_its_own_sagitta_about_the_axis` and `a_facet_over_the_axis_or_unreadable_is_never_round` (NaN and infinite input excuse nothing).
- `solid_law_goldens`' `contain_law` now names the holes it drills (it called the law with `hole_walls: true` and no holes, which now excuses nothing). Its verdicts are unchanged: all 14 goldens clean, and the drill/peck/tap 32-gon goldens still need, and keep, the excuse.
- Kept green without loosening anything: `bore_facet_sagitta` (2/2) and `bore_entry`.
- Full `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head 6637e92c: green, 8.1 min. The sim lib plus 19 sim suites, motion `real_tip`/`solid_law`, the app lib plus 75 app suites: 950 passed, 0 failed, 12 ignored.
- By hand on the same head: `bore_facet_sagitta`, `golden_cl`, `conformance`, `tap_sim`, `mill2d_c`, `drill_prior_kinds`, `drilling_cross_box`, `drilling_cross_holder`: 57 passed, 0 failed. Before cleanup I also ran `bore_entry`, `verify`, `solid_law`, `solid_law_goldens`, `coarse_contain`, `drilling_*`, `operations` and more on identical logic, all green. (There is no `coarse_rims` suite on main.)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -D warnings` is clean. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib --test hole_wall_flats --test solid_law_goldens -D warnings` is clean.

## Goldens

No golden file moves: no `.cl`, `.nc` or snapshot PNG is touched, and `golden_cl` is green. I instrumented the old rule over the touched suites (throwaway, removed). Every excuse the old rule granted in `solid_law_goldens` (3326), `drilling_cross` (15595) and `operations` (574) is still granted.

The one newly convicted fixture is `tap_sim::a_tap_in_a_hole_modelled_at_tap_drill_size_is_not_a_gouge`:
- Its hole is a **square** of half-width 2.5 under an M6 tap.
- The generator's contain law sweeps the tap at its full r 3, which is 0.5 mm into each flat. The old rule excused that only because the square's corners (r 3.54) stand outside the tap.
- The test asserts only the program sim's verdict (core-radius tap, #266), so it still passes. The op's generator verdict now carries a blocking Gouge.
- This matches main on a *round* tap-drill hole, where the contain law already convicts the tap's full radius (the hole's vertices are inside the tap, so no excuse applied). The square was the bug's case, not a different law.

## Not exercised

- A tilted cross hole through a coarse wall: `drilling_cross*` suites pass, and the axis-in-frame mapping is covered only by them.
- A 4th/5th-axis posed Drill/Bore whose tool axis is not the hole axis: there the excuse now stands down (stricter).
- Real STEP/STL parts beyond `Milling-test.step`. A hole imported coarser than 0.05 mm sagitta (e.g. a 16-gon on r 5) now convicts as a false gouge, which is the safe side, as with #864.

## Overlap with PR #1099

This PR changes `solid.rs`, `solid_index.rs`, `mod.rs`, `contact.rs` and `rapids_posed.rs` (the `hits` signature: the `hole_walls: bool` parameter became the hole-axis slice `walls`). PR #1099 also changes them: it adds a `bores` parameter to the same `hits` and a `solid_hits_threaded` beside `solid_hits`, and `generate.rs` `contain_into`. Whichever merges second needs a careful keep-both on those lines. `swept.rs` `chord_dip` is gone: #1099's call to it becomes `hole_wall::wall_excuse`. #1099's own vertex-based measurements (`thread_bore.rs` `wall_radius`, `material_source.rs` `major_rims`) are left to that PR's review, which asks for this same nearest-point rule.

title: feat(thread): thread-milling pass control - decreasing passes, finish and spring passes, depth allowance, M4 cutters
body:
Stacked on #1137 (on #1045, #1005). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

Thread milling (internal and external) gains pass control, one value `ThreadPasses` on the kernel's `ThreadParams` and on `OpParams::Thread`:

- **Decreasing pass depths (constant chip area)**: `pass_schedule: constant_area` - cumulative depth after pass i of n is `D x sqrt(i/n)`, the infeed is the first (largest) pass, `n = ceil((D/infeed)^2)`, capped at 64 (refused by name past that). The last roughing pass lands exactly on D.
- **Finishing pass** of its own radial depth (`finish_depth`) and **spring passes** (`spring_passes`, at most 4) on the final radius.
- **Depth allowance** (`depth_allowance`, radial): the last pass lands on standard depth - allowance. A negative allowance (past the major diameter of a hole / the design root of a boss) and one over a quarter of the thread depth are refused by name.
- **Spindle and cutter hand** (`spindle_reverse` = M4, `cutter_left_hand`): climb sense flips under M4 (the helix keeps the drawing's hand); a right-hand-cut mill under M4 or a left-hand-cut one under M3 is refused by name. M4 reaches the post via a new `PARAM MillSpindle reverse` (`post::ask_reverse_spindle`) and manifest flag `millSpindleReverse`; `fanuc.cps` declares it and writes `M4`; the engine refuses such a section by name for every other script (the lathe's #629 `SpindleDirection`/`threadHands` is deliberately not reused).
- Gated at the door (create, edit, retool via `thread_op::door`) and again in the kernel. File/MCP keys flattened into the Thread params, additive, written only when not default; the digest clause appears only when not default. Page: Passes tab (schedule, finish, spring, allowance), Feeds tab (spindle, cutter hand).

Defaults are the #894 ride: every existing thread golden (`.cl` and `.nc`) is byte-identical.

## Sources

Smid, "CNC Programming Handbook" (thread cutting: constant-area pass depths, spring pass); Machinery's Handbook ("Thread milling", "Thread cutting": finish pass, climb vs cutter rotation, cutter hand vs spindle); ISO 724 / ISO 965-1 (depths, tolerance scale). No HSMWorks / Fusion material. Decisions in `docs/decisions/988-thread-pass-control.md`.

## How tested

- Kernel (`camcraft-motion`, `machining2d::thread_pass_tests`): `constant_area_passes_decrease_and_each_takes_the_same_chip_area`, `a_finishing_pass_and_spring_passes_land_on_the_final_radius`, `an_allowance_leaves_the_stated_depth_uncut_and_is_refused_past_its_tolerance`, `an_m4_spindle_with_a_left_hand_cut_mill_flips_the_orbit_and_keeps_the_hand`, `a_cutter_hand_against_the_spindle_and_other_nonsense_are_refused_by_name`.
- App (`tests/thread_passes.rs`): clean verify + Fanuc post for decreasing/finish/spring/allowance; M4 left-hand ride posts `M4` on Fanuc and is refused by name on Haas; door refusals at creation; edit gated, undo, project-file round trip.
- Golden: `thread_mill_constant_area_spring_pass.cl` (`golden_cl::thread_mill_constant_area_spring_pass_matches_golden`).
- MCP: `mcp::thread_pass_control_over_the_params_door`.
- UI: `thread_mill_page_tests::the_pass_control_rows_edit_the_draft_and_apply_undoes`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/985-external-threads`: green on the final head (post, motion, app, ui suites; 13.5 min); clippy -D warnings on motion/app/post/ui.

## Not exercised

- M4 on posts other than Fanuc (they refuse by name). No machine run.
- The issue's last bullet (feed starts at the op's `top_z` R plane rather than each hole's entry) is split out to #1212.

Changelog: Thread milling: decreasing (constant chip area) pass depths, a finishing pass, spring passes, a depth allowance and M4 / left-hand-cut thread mills, internal and external (#988)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #988

title: feat(edm): wire taper by angle word - the control's corner rule as machine data
body:
Stacked on #1181 (on #1163, #1144, #1139, #1123, #560, #551)

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

A wire EDM can now state an **angle-word taper dialect** in place of U/V moves. The control's behaviour goes in the machine file as data, so the verify can judge the lean the control will actually cut.

- **Machine data** (`post::machine::edm_taper`, new): `edm.taper_angle { positive: top_left|top_right, corner: mitre|cone }`. Both values are enumerated words with no default. A garbled word refuses the file. An unstated one is refused by name at generation. The angle code is `edm.codes.taper_angle`, a template with `{angle}`.
- **Generator** (`motion::wire_edm::taper`): a `WireCorner` rule.
  - `Mitre` is #536's path. On the fixture its CL equals #536's golden byte for byte (pinned).
  - `Cone` pivots the wire about each top-plane corner and holds the lean at the angle. The lower end runs on an arc of radius `H tan a`, laid as posed moves at most 2 degrees apart.
  - Under `cone`, a lead-in that meets a corner is refused by name.
- **Door** (`app::operation::wire_op::corner_rule`): a U/V machine keeps the mitre. An angle-word machine uses its stated rule. An incomplete rule is refused by name, and so is a 4-axis cut, because one angle cannot state two profiles. The rule is stamped only for angle-word machines, so U/V stamps do not change.
- **Post** (`app::posting_wire::angled`, `wire-iso.cps`):
  - Each move's X Y is written on the programmed plane, which is the work's top. The angle word is passed as `PARAM WireAngle`, signed by the side rule and computed from the path. No U/V words are written.
  - The cone's turning moves are not sent, because the control makes them itself.
  - `taper_on` and the angle word are written before the lead-in, and `taper_off` before the lead-out.
  - A machine that states neither `uv` nor `edm.taper_angle` is refused by name.
  - The new PARAMs are listed in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md`.
- The decision record is `docs/decisions/1164-wire-taper-angle-word.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/wire_taper_angle.rs` (new):
  - `an_angle_word_punch_posts_its_golden_with_the_mitre_rule`: new NC golden `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_taper_angle_punch.nc`; the CL equals `wire_taper_punch.cl`; the sign flips under `top_right`.
  - `the_cone_rule_turns_the_wire_about_each_corner`: the lean is held at 3 degrees through every corner, and the NC equals the mitre golden except for the note line.
  - `a_corner_the_stated_rule_gouges_blocks_the_post`: on a 3-degree drafted punch with sharp corners, the mitre rule verifies clean and posts. The cone rule's rounded lower corners gouge it, so the post is blocked with `wire gouge`.
  - `an_incomplete_dialect_and_a_four_axis_angle_cut_are_refused_by_name`: a missing corner rule, a missing side rule, neither uv nor angle, and 4-axis on an angle machine.
- `motion` unit test `the_cone_rule_holds_the_lean_and_refuses_a_lead_into_a_corner`; `post` unit test `taper_angle_words_parse_and_garbled_ones_refuse_the_file`.
- U/V goldens: `wire_taper`, `wire_4axis`, `wire_post`, `wire_contour` and `wire_verify` pass with their goldens unedited.
- Gate on the final head 39d014d8: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/537-wire-4axis` green (3 steps, 0 failed, 11.2 min); the wire suites by hand (wire_taper 5, wire_4axis 6, wire_post 5, wire_contour 7, wire_verify 3, wire_taper_angle 4: all pass); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- No real EDM control (D10). The angle code and dialect words are invented on the synthetic fixture.
- How a real control ramps the lean over the lead-in and lead-out is modelled as a linear ramp, the same as #536. The decision record states this.
- The `arc` corner rule (lean change rounded over a stated radius) is not offered.
- No UI page field for `edm.taper_angle`. It is machine-file data only, like `edm.codes`.

Changelog: Wire EDM: a machine can state an angle-word taper dialect (edm.taper_angle: side rule and mitre/cone corner rule). The wire post writes the angle word, and the verify judges the lean the stated corner rule cuts.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1164

title: fix(build): the gate reports VOID when the checkout moves during a run
body:
## What changed

- `cargo xtask gate` (every tier, and the release gate in process) records HEAD and `git --no-optional-locks status --porcelain` at start, before each step, and at the end. A change prints `VOID: ... during the gate (<where>) - this run is void, not a verdict on any commit`, stops, and exits 1. The summary ends `== gate VOID`, never a green table.
- Detection only, no lock and no hook: a `.git/index.lock` leaked by Ctrl-C would block all git work in the checkout. Decision in `docs/decisions/1201-gate-checkout-guard.md`.
- AGENTS.md ("Start from the latest main") and the `work-issue` skill: a worktree agent never switches, pulls, merges, resets, checks out or stashes in the main checkout; its only git there is `fetch` and `worktree add`. The maintainer's quoted sentences are untouched.
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` 29 -> 30.

PROCESS_VERSION 30: a fork must take the process files from upstream (`git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION xtask`). A fork's own gate then reports VOID on a moved checkout instead of a verdict; nothing else changes for it.

## How tested

- Pinning tests (`xtask/src/checkout_tests.rs`, pure function on fake readings, no git): `unchanged_checkout_has_no_void_message`, `head_moved_with_clean_tree_names_both_commits`, `half_moved_checkout_is_caught_with_head_unchanged` (the #1201 case: HEAD unchanged, index and tree rewritten), `head_and_tree_both_moved_say_so`, `long_diffs_are_capped_at_five_named_entries`, `short_sha_is_safe_on_short_input`.
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: xtask unit tests green (54 + 6 new). First run was red on one assertion (singular "1 entry differs" wording); fixed and re-run green. Clippy `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## What was not exercised

- The VOID path end to end: no real gate was run while a pull moved a checkout. The comparison is covered by unit tests; the `Run` wiring (`check` calls in `plan`, the summary) was only exercised by a dry run in this checkout.
- Non-Windows hosts: the code uses only `git` and `cargo` through `Command`; not run on macOS or Linux here.

Changelog: none

Effort: medium

Fixes #1201

title: fix(post): hold an undeclared post script to the lathe door on a lathe or mill-turn
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
- `post::dialect::declared_turning(cps) -> Result<Option<bool>, PostError>`: `Some(true/false)` for a declared `capabilities` mask, `None` when the script states no usable mask (absent, a string, negative, non-finite). `speaks_turning` keeps its meaning and is now `declared_turning(..)?.unwrap_or(false)`.
- `app::lathe_voice::at_post` (the #1190 door) reads the tri-state: a declared turning script fires the door as before; a declared non-turning script passes as before; an **undeclared** script is held to the door for every operation whose setup mounts a machine with a work spindle (lathe or mill-turn, via `machine::kind_of_setup`), and the refusal adds that the script has no `capabilities` line and what to add (`capabilities = 1;` mill, `= 2;` turning). On a mill, plasma table or EDM (no work spindle) an undeclared script passes as before.
- Decision recorded in `docs/decisions/1199-undeclared-dialect.md`: option (b) of the issue; (a) refuse-everywhere and (c) warn-only considered and dropped, with reasons.

Behaviour change for users: a user's own *milling* script without `capabilities`, posting a milling op on a lathe or mill-turn setup, is now refused by name with the one-line fix. Every shipped post states its mask, so no shipped post, golden or registry pairing changes.

## How tested
Pinning tests:
- `camcraft-app` lib `lathe_voice::tests::an_undeclared_script_is_held_to_the_door_on_a_machine_with_a_work_spindle`: an inline undeclared lathe script (also `capabilities = "2"` and `-1`) on a lathe and on a mill-turn refuses a Face op and an off-centre Drill by name (names the missing line, the machine, the fix), still passes Facing / on-centre Drill / C-stating live tool; declared `1` / `2` on the same machines behave as before; on a mill and with no machine loaded it passes. Fails on main (the door returned Ok).
- `camcraft-post` lib `post::dialect::tests::an_undeclared_mask_is_none_never_a_guess`.
- Unchanged and green: `lathe_voice::tests::the_door_refuses_on_every_turning_dialect_and_passes_every_milling_one` (every shipped post, every kind) and the other lathe_voice unit tests.

Suites run (debug, all green): camcraft-app `posting`, `conformance`, `golden_cl`, `lathe_post`, `lathe_post_css`, `lathe_post_g76`, `lathe_post_refusals`, `lathe_post_tormach`, `lathe_post_tormach_thread`, `lathe_work_spindle`, `lathe_workholding_rpm`, `lathe_spindle_law`, `lathe_cross_drill`, `control_comp`, `drill_prior`, `per_op_files`, `setup_mount`, `setup_mounts_post`, `wear_comp`, `edm_machine`; the whole `camcraft-post` crate; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

- The rest of the app suites (batch tier).

title: fix(motion): land a rapid only on swept stock; hold the developed band's bore exit and lap kinks to the bar's laws
body:
Stacked on #1138 (on #1080, #1007). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

**#1169 - a rapid landed on a wall strip thinner than a planner cell (safety floor).**
The microlift plan read its landings on the planner's cell bitmap (D/120 = 0.083 mm). A wall strip thinner than a cell that falls between two rows of cell centers is invisible there: the easing laps drop it as "air" and it stands until the last lap. On the narrow slot 14x60 the return over the retract plane (`LinkLaw::high`) rapided to 0.3 mm over the floor at (17.407, 8.956) with a 0.075 mm strip under its rim - the verifier's `RapidInStock`.

- New `adaptive::lift_swept::Swept`: the segments the plan's pieces have cut so far, exactly. `high` lands only where the whole footprint (r - 10 um, the verifier's own footprint) is within r - 12.5 um of a cut segment (2.5 um arc fit + the 10 um chords the verifier reads a posted arc on). The proof is a quadtree over the disc on exact segment distances (1-Lipschitz bound per square, divided to 1 um); where it does not close the landing is refused. Nothing is sampled. The cell test stays as the cheap first reading. The verifier is untouched.
- The hop's landing (`lift_link::landing`) takes a lead point the pieces swept before one only the cells read clear. The hop comes down at plunge feed from over the stock, never in rapid, so with no point proved the cells' choice stands.
- A piece starting exactly where the tool stands is ridden on to at the floor (`lift::ride`) instead of a retract and plunge on one spot. That hop, not the strip, was the slot's "4 descents for 2 levels" (the growth's last piece handing over to the first easing lap at (5.135, 7.312), both in cut).

**#1050 - the held fix (16e129bb), now landable.** `adaptive::conform`: the disc phase out of the entry bore is held on the planner's rim and on a rim twice as coarse (the worse kept); the closing laps' fillet kinks are spread at 4 degrees. The measured pins `R62_LOAD_FACTOR`, `R62_BREAKS` and `BAR_50_BREAKS` are removed; the pins hold the whole bar's laws. No law and no bound loosened.

## Readings (release, Linux x86-64)

Narrow slot 14x60, with #1050's change:

| | verifier | descents (2 levels) | returns | over the retract plane | rides | hops |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| before | 1 `RapidInStock` | 4 | 200 | 3 | 0 | 1 |
| after | silent | 2 | 199 (1365 mm lifted) | 0 | 2 | 0 |

Out of cut 0.88x the cut (law 1.5), load 15.4 % D, 0 breaks, 14262 moves.

Rotary bars (0.1 mm dexel, law 19.8 % D, no break past 5 deg):

| level | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| r6.2 / 5.7 | 20.3 % D, 0 breaks | 17.3 % D, 0 breaks |
| r6.2 / 5.2 | 20.3 % D, 3 breaks | 17.7 % D, 0 breaks |
| r7 / 6.5, 6.0 | - | 19.5 % D, 0 breaks |
| r7 / 5.5, 5.0 | - | 17.3 %, 18.4 % D, 0 breaks |

Other `adaptive_hsm` fixtures: bore 15.4 % D, rectangle 15.4, L-pocket 15.7, 0 breaks, 2 descents each; island and channel fall back to Offset rings as before.

## Verdict moves

- Narrow slot: `RapidInStock` -> silent; its three returns over the retract plane (leads along the walls, not provable at 12.5 um) became routed lifted returns; one retract hop became a ride.
- r6.2 neck levels and r7 level 5.0: measured pins removed, now under the whole bar's laws.
- App `pocket3d_hsm::the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` (the STEP bore's per-platform exact triple, moves / planar feeds / arcs): the plan moved, as the pin says a planner change will. Linux x86-64 had no triple of its own (it rode the band of the other two, 16100-16260 moves); it now reads **(15561, 14837, 1561)**, two release runs identical, added as its own exact arm. Every level still verifies clean and none falls back (Z 20: 56 microlift returns, 7 rides, 1 retract hop). **The Windows (16197, 15458, 1581) and macOS (16160, 15432, 1571) triples were measured before these changes and could not be re-measured here; they are left as measured, not widened, and will fail on those platforms until re-measured there.** That re-measure is owed before this merges or at the latest at the cut (release tier).
- No golden file and no snapshot changed.

## Tests

New: `lift_swept::tests::a_rapid_landing_on_a_sub_cell_wall_strip_is_refused` (a 0.04 mm strip the cells read clear: `high` refused, allowed once the strip is cut; the hop landing's preference), `lift_swept::tests::a_disc_is_covered_on_the_cut_and_not_a_hair_past_it`, `lift_tests::a_piece_starting_where_the_tool_stands_is_ridden_on_to`.

Run on the final planner code (ba3cdd8e; the commits after it change only docs and the app pin's Linux arm), release, `--include-ignored`:
- motion `adaptive_hsm` 6/6 (`hsm_report_full_resolution` green), `adaptive_band` 2/2, `rotary_adaptive` 6/6, `level_links` 12/12, `pocket3d_hsm` 4/4, `adaptive_orbit_seam` 1/1
- motion lib `adaptive` filter 35/35 (both #1051 budget twins, the slot sweep, the new unit tests)
- app `shoulder_adaptive` 3/3, `roughing2d` 7/7, `pocket_overhead` 2/2, `whole_model_pocket` 5/5 (release, default lane)
- app `pocket3d_hsm` 2/2 (with the Linux triple added; first run red on the band, see Verdict moves)
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/1051-planning-budget-edge`: green (motion lib + 5 suites, debug)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean

## Not exercised

- The batch and release gate tiers; app suites other than `pocket3d_hsm`; the UI.
- Windows and macOS: nothing was run there, and the bore pin's triples for both are stale (Verdict moves).
- Which of the two changes moved the bore's triple was not separated (the held #1050 commit was never run against that suite on its own).
- The hop landing's swept preference on a real plan: no fixture run here posts a hop after this change (unit-tested only).

title: feat(ui): WCS page applies its origin from the footer beside Close, and says where the origin is
body:
#870: a Makera Z1 user cut air on their first program because they hadn't understood where the origin was. Then it "took a while to find out how to actually save the setting, as the 'set origin' button is crammed next to a lot of other options".

Fork synced at v0.18.0, PROCESS_VERSION 29; merged with upstream main at 62a2c93a.

## What changed

- **Set origin in the footer.** The WCS page's apply button leaves the page body (where it shared a row with *Level*, among the quarter turns) and moves into the property pane's fixed footer, beside *Close* (`egui_app::wcs_footer`). Every other page keeps its plain *Close*.
- **Pending edits are flagged.** While the typed X/Y/Z or angles differ from the placed WCS, the footer shows **Origin not applied** in the warning ink.
  - The position is compared to 1e-9 mm. The angles are compared as rotations, so yaw 360 is not an edit. A non-finite field reads as pending.
  - The drafts survive a close and reopen, so closing loses nothing silently. Closing does not apply them either.
- **The origin in words.** A new pure module, `app::setup_origin`, places the origin against the box the page anchors on (the stock box, else the model's bounds).
  - A point on one of the 27 anchor points is named, e.g. `top of stock, front-left corner`, `top of stock, centre` or `mid-height of stock, front edge, centred`.
  - Any other point is given as signed distances from the box's left side, front and top, so it never claims a corner it is not on.
  - The WCS page states it under its heading: `G54 origin: top of stock, front-left corner (X0 Y0 Z0)`. The setup sheet gains an `origin:` line under the WCS numbers.
- **Viewport marker:** the WCS axis triad already marks the origin; nothing was added.
- **Docs:** `docs/user-guide/work-origin.md`, a short page on where the origin is shown and how to change it.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/870-wcs-set-origin-footer.md`.

**Overlap with #759** (@mkinney, open draft, `conflicts`): it splits the WCS page body out of `pages.rs` into `wcs_page.rs` and keeps its own *Set Origin* in the quarter-turn rows. This PR touches the page body in one place only, removing that button. The new code lives in its own files (`wcs_footer.rs`, `setup_origin.rs`). Whichever lands second drops the body button and calls `wcs_footer::origin_line` from the page.

## How it was tested

New pinning tests:
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/wcs_footer.rs` (structural: painted text, AccessKit labels, coarse placement):
  - `the_page_says_where_the_origin_is_in_words`
  - `set_origin_sits_in_the_footer_beside_close_and_nowhere_else`: one row, Set origin before Close, below the page body, exactly one apply button, no flag on a fresh page.
  - `a_typed_origin_is_flagged_until_set_origin_applies_it`: the flag appears, a click on Set origin places the typed X and clears it, and yaw 360 does not raise it.
- `app::setup_origin` unit tests: `every_anchor_point_is_named`, `a_point_off_the_anchors_is_given_as_distances_never_as_a_corner`, `a_non_finite_origin_or_box_says_so`.
- `crates/app/tests/setup_wcs.rs`: `the_setup_sheet_says_where_the_origin_is_in_words` (corner, centre, off-anchor).

Two existing ui tests got a taller window, 1280 x 900 instead of 720. The new origin line makes the WCS page one to two rows taller, and at 720 px the bottom of the page scrolls under the footer. The page scrolls; nothing is lost.
- `one_wcs::the_wcs_page_shows_the_work_offset_dropdown_and_no_setups_page_pointer`: its bottom note was out of view.
- `origin_page_shows_the_anchor_grid_and_arms_pick_mode`: its SE cell click missed.

Gates on 8b850a18:
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui` (CWD `crates/ui`): all green. The lib has 596 passed and 5 ignored; every integration binary passes.
- App suites that read the setup sheet or the WCS: `setup_wcs`, `setup_sheet`, `rotated_wcs`, `setup_align`, `program_entry`, `inverted_axis_display`, `setup_stock_source`: all pass. `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib setup_origin`: 3 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No snapshot PNG touched.

## Not exercised

- Not looked at in the running app. The layout is pinned structurally only.
- On a rotated or aligned setup (#326), "left" and "front" are the world box's, as the anchor grid's compass names already are.
- The release-lane pixel snapshots were not run. If one frames the WCS page, it moves at the cut's regeneration.

Changelog: WCS page: Set origin sits in the footer beside Close, unapplied edits are flagged, and the page and setup sheet say where the origin is in words ("top of stock, front-left corner") (#870)

Effort: medium (the issue's label). Not escalated.

Fixes #870
