title: feat(edm): sinker side burn - a lateral electrode move that burns one wall out by a stated amount
body:
**Stacked on #1166** (#544, `issue/544-sinker-orbits`), which stacks on #1131 (#541) → #560 (#531) → #551 (#530). Retarget it to `main` once its parents merge. Fork synced at v0.18.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 17).

## What changed
- **New op kind, Sinker Side Burn** (`OpType::SinkerSideBurn`, stored id 42, appended; file key `sinker_side_burn`). Its params are `SinkerSideBurnOp { burn: SinkerBurnOp, direction, amount, undersize }`:
  - The burn's plunge is #541's struct, embedded whole, with the op's **own** condition. It takes no orbit; an orbit is refused by name.
  - Then one lateral Feed of `amount` along +X, -X, +Y or -Y at the floor, the same Feed back to the burn point, and the rapid retract.
  - #541's door (`sinker::check`) and condition read (`sinker_op::condition_gap_as`) are reused, not copied.
- **Allowance law** (`motion::sinker_side`): `allowance = undersize - gap`. Refused by name:
  - a move past the allowance ("... toward +X burns into the part - the side's allowance is 0.150 (undersize 0.200 less spark gap 0.050)");
  - a gap the undersize can't honour;
  - a non-finite, zero or negative amount;
  - a bad undersize;
  - an orbit.
- **Validated at command creation** (`gates::sinker_gate`, on CreateOperation, PasteOperation, EditOperationParams and ChangeOperationKind, ahead of `is_sane` so the refusal is by name):
  - always: the structural refusals above;
  - once a condition is named on a sinker EDM: an unknown condition, the gap against the undersize, and the allowance.

  An unnamed condition stays a draft (the ribbon's seed) and is refused at generation. Generation, the staleness stamp and the sim plan re-run the whole law (`sinker_side_op::side_gap`). A machine that later re-states a wider gap therefore refuses the stored op by name.
- The stock sim sweeps every move with the existing box atom. No new sim law.
- **MCP:** through the params JSON door (`add_operation` / `edit_operation` with `direction` / `amount` / `undersize`). `list_operation_types` lists the kind. No new command, so no new MCP tool.
- **UI:** only the minimal rows on the existing sinker page's Passes tab (wall, amount, undersize, in place of the orbit rows), plus the contour glyph for its row. The full pages are #548's. No snapshot PNG was touched.
- **Files:** an appended DTO variant (the burn's keys flattened, plus the three side keys). Old files load unchanged.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/545-sinker-side-burn.md`.

## How tested
- `crates/app/tests/sinker_side.rs` (new):
  - `a_side_burn_moves_the_faced_wall_by_its_amount_in_the_sim`: for each of the four directions, at a 0.05 column grid:
    - the faced wall stands at electrode + gap + amount: the column centre just inside it is burned to the floor and **the next column out is untouched**;
    - the far wall and the walls across the move stay at the plunge's gap;
    - the program verdict reports 0 gouge cells.
  - `a_lateral_move_past_the_allowance_is_refused_by_name`:
    - refused at creation: a move past the allowance, past the undersize, a gap past the undersize, an unknown condition, a NaN/inf/negative/zero amount, a bad undersize;
    - at the allowance exactly, the op is admitted; an edit past it is refused;
    - after a remount with a wider gap, generation refuses by name and the op is left unchanged.
  - `an_undersize_overstated_against_the_part_is_convicted_by_the_stock_sim`: the part's cavity lacks the claimed undersize, so the sim reports a gouge.
  - `the_side_burn_round_trips_the_file_and_rides_the_mcp_params_door`: save and load, then `list_operation_types`, add, generate, an edit past the allowance refused, edit, undo.
  - `sinker_side_burn_matches_golden`: new golden `crates/app/tests/golden/sinker_side_burn.cl`, read by hand. Rapid to (12.5, -7.5, 25), plunge to Z 14.05 (floor 14 + gap 0.05), lateral -Y 0.15 to Y -7.65, back to -7.5, rapid to Z 25. Five moves.
- Unit tests in `motion::sinker_side`: `sinker_side_moves_along_its_axis_by_the_amount_and_back` and `sinker_side_refuses_past_the_allowance_by_name`.
- `ribbon` (the last kind is now SinkerSideBurn) and `coarse_laws` (SinkerSideBurn is a stated refusal on a reduced model, like SinkerBurn).
- Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on 7bdd2505. Tools, post, sim, motion and ui suites, and every app integration binary, were green. That includes coarse_laws, sinker_burn, sinker_orbit, sinker_side, edm_machine, edm_conditions, golden_cl, project_roundtrip, operations, ribbon and mcp. The app lib's `operation::tests::stamp_follows_every_input` failed on the kind count (42 -> 43); b8191744 bumps the pin, and `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` is green on the final head (138 passed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
- Not exercised on a real EDM control: the conditions are synthetic.
- Posting waits on #542 (the sinker post). This PR emits no new PARAM.
- No wear compensation (#546) and no electrode generation (#547).

Changelog: Sinker EDM side burn: a lateral electrode move burns one wall out by a stated amount, bounded by the op's own undersize less its condition's spark gap; a move into the part is refused by name (#545)
Effort: high

Fixes #545

title: fix(post): a milling operation is never posted on a lathe's work spindle
body:
## What changed

A lathe post opens every section that states no C angle with the WORK spindle (`G97 S M03`). The stream names no operation family, so a milling pass that stays on one meridian read to `fanuc-lathe.cps` and `tormach-lathe.cps` exactly like a turning pass, and posted the work spindle at the cutter's rpm with the cutter standing still.

The program gate now decides it before a line is written, from what it already holds (the operation's kind, its cached path, its work offset). Through a turning dialect a section passes only as live-tool work (its path states C), a turning-family kind, or a Drill whose every cutting move and cycle is on the spindle axis with the tool along +Z. Every other operation is refused by name.

- `crates/app/src/lathe_voice.rs` (new): `voice(params, path, origin) -> LatheVoice { WorkSpindle, LiveTool, Refused(why) }` is the one derivation; `voice_of(world, entity)` reads it from the document; `at_post(world, ops, cps)` is the door.
- The door is called where a script is known: `post_script_body` (so `post_script`, `post_setup`, one-mount `post_mounts`), `post_each` (several mounts, each with its own script) and `post_per_op_with`. It runs before the verification report in all three, so the user reads this refusal first.
- `crates/post/src/post/dialect.rs` (new): `speaks_turning(cps)` reads the script's own manifest (`capabilities`, the mask every shipped post already states: 2 for the two lathe posts, 1 for the rest); `states_live_tool(path)` is the one "does the path state C?" test, and the stream's `PARAM LiveTool` is now written from it.
- No change to the stream format, the CL spec or any post script. A mill post is untouched: there `M03` is the cutter's own spindle.

## Reproductions (both re-verified on main before the fix)

Mill-turn bench (spindle as C, live-tool words stated, spindle maximum 15000 so the machine's rpm limit masks nothing), through `fanuc-lathe.cps`.

**(a) Drill DR-0400, one hole at X0 Y0** - correct voicing, unchanged, still posts:

```
G97 S10000 M03
M8
G00 X0 Z20
G83 Z10 Q12000 F0.008
```

**(b) Face, flat end mill EM-0400-2FL, one pass along Y = 0** - before, no refusal from either lathe script:

```
(OPERATION: F1 - FACE - G54)
G54
(T0202 EM-0400-2FL - FLAT END MILL D4)
T0202
G50 S15000
G97 S12000 M03
M8
G00 X-24 Z30
G01 X-24 Z4 F0.0083
G01 X24 Z4 F0.025
```

After, from every post entry point, nothing written:

```
F1: a Face operation would be posted on the work spindle - a lathe post turns the work at the tool's speed while the cutter stands still, so nothing is milled; cut it as C-axis live tooling (a rotary operation), or move it to a setup that posts through a mill post, or suppress the operation
```

Through `fanuc.cps` the same document posts as before.

## Per-kind table (all 41 kinds, on a path that stays on the meridian and on one that stays on the axis)

| Kinds | Through a lathe post |
|---|---|
| Turning family (12): Facing, Profile Rough, Profile Finish, Groove Rough, Groove Finish, Parting, Threading, Chamfering, Taper Turning, Multi-Pass Turning, Form Turning, Boring | posts on the work spindle |
| Any kind whose path states C (in practice Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset on the spindle's C) | posts with the live-tool voicing |
| Drill, every cutting move and cycle on the spindle axis, tool along +Z (drill, centre drill, tap cycle, reamer) | posts on the work spindle, as (a) |
| Drill with a hole off the axis (on the meridian or not), or a tilted (cross) drill | refused, naming the hole: `D2: a Drill operation would be posted on the work spindle with a hole off the spindle axis (X6.000 Y0.000 from the work offset) - ...` |
| Face, 2D Contour, 2D Pocket, Slot, Trace, 2D Adaptive, 2D Offset, Engrave, 2D Chamfer, Circular, Thread (thread mill), Bore (helical), Trochoidal slot, 3D Pocket, 3D Finish, Deburr, 5-Axis Contour, 5-Axis Parallel, Swarf, Advanced Swarf, Multi-Axis Rough, 5-Axis Flow, Multi-Axis Contour, and the three rotary kinds when their path states no C | refused by name, on the meridian and on centre |
| Probe | refused by name ("cannot be posted through a lathe post - it would open the section on the work spindle and writes no probing") |
| Plasma Profile | refused by name |

Decided one by one: a tap on centre is a Drill with the tap cycle and is admitted (the work turns, the tap stands still - lathe practice); Bore is refused (its cutter orbits the hole); the thread-mill Thread is refused (the cutter must turn). On-centre is exact because tool and work then share one axis, so it makes no difference to the cut which of the two turns; off the axis that is gone. Tolerance: `spindle_law::SPINDLE_TOL`, 0.0005 mm, the lathe scripts' own `EPS`. Rapids are not judged.

## The route, and why

The smaller route: a law at the program gate, no stream parameter. The gate already holds everything the law needs, so the refusal is made before the stream exists; a stream parameter would only let the *script* say the same thing, at the cost of a format change and goldens moving in every dialect. No case defeated the smaller route. The parameter becomes worth it when a lathe post should *voice* a milling section with a driven tool and no C move (new behaviour, not this fix). Recorded in `docs/decisions/1190-mill-op-on-lathe-post.md`.

## The shared predicate (for PR #1191)

"Is this section voiced on the work spindle?" is `camcraft_app::lathe_voice::on_work_spindle(world, &entity)`, and the full answer is `lathe_voice::voice_of(world, &entity) -> Option<LatheVoice>`: `WorkSpindle` is the section whose stated rpm turns the work, `LiveTool` the one whose work turns on C, `Refused` one that never reaches a lathe post. `setup_workholding::work_speed` can map those three onto its `Stated` / `OnC` / `Not` instead of keeping its own reading. One difference it would pick up: a mill-turn's on-centre Drill is `WorkSpindle` here, and today's `spindle_law::turns` leaves it out, so it is not held to the chuck limit. `setup_workholding.rs` is not touched by this PR.

## Entry points

GUI Post (`posting::post_mounts`), GUI Post per operation (`posting::post_per_op`), the script verb and the MCP `post` tool (`api::v_post` -> `post_mounts` / `post_mounts_script`), and the CLI through those. All go through `op_streams` and then one of the three bodies that hold the script. `posting::stream_records` (the gate-free stream the test suites hand to `engine::run`) is not gated: it holds no script.

## Goldens

Byte-identical; no golden file is in the diff. The lathe goldens hold only Drill (three, all on X0), Facing, Groove Finish, Parting, Profile Rough, Profile Finish and Threading sections, plus two synthetic C-axis streams: no mill-family section on the work spindle, so nothing to list as a finding.

## Pinning tests

- `lathe_voice::tests::every_kind_is_work_spindle_live_tool_or_refused_by_name` (the table over `KindInfo::ALL`; the expectation is an exhaustive match, so a new kind does not compile until it is decided)
- `lathe_voice::tests::a_drill_is_admitted_only_with_every_cut_on_the_spindle_axis_along_z`
- `lathe_voice::tests::the_door_refuses_on_every_turning_dialect_and_passes_every_milling_one` (every kind against every built-in post; registry list and manifests agree)
- `lathe_work_spindle::a_drill_on_centre_posts_on_the_work_spindle_as_a_lathe_drills` (reproduction a)
- `lathe_work_spindle::a_face_pass_on_the_meridian_is_refused_by_name_never_posted_on_the_work_spindle` (reproduction b, both lathe dialects)
- `lathe_work_spindle::every_post_entry_point_refuses_it` (`post_script`, `post_setup`, `post_mounts`, `post_mounts_script`, `post_per_op`, `post_per_op_script`, MCP `post` with and without a named post)
- `lathe_work_spindle::a_drill_off_centre_on_the_meridian_is_refused_by_name`
- `lathe_work_spindle::live_tool_and_turning_sections_pass_the_lathe_door`
- `post::dialect::tests::the_turning_bit_is_read_from_the_manifest_mask`, `a_path_is_live_tool_work_only_when_a_move_states_c`

## How tested

On the final head `50c0bea7` (the fix `ee8423cd` plus a merge of `origin/main` at `d7e9a807`, which had moved under the branch):

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: green on the first run - post suites (19 binaries) and app suites (the lib plus 125 suites it mapped from `app::posting` / `post::post`), 1259 tests passed, 0 failed, 8.0 min wall.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Before the merge, on `ee8423cd`: `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (all green) and the app suites `lathe_post`, `lathe_post_css`, `lathe_post_refusals`, `lathe_workholding_rpm`, `c_axis_live`, `c_axis_unwind`, `edm_machine`, `conformance`, `operations` (117), `golden_cl` (25), `solid_law_goldens`, plus every other suite that posts through a lathe dialect at the real gate (`lathe_cross_drill`, `drilling_axial`, `drilling_cross_box`, `drilling_cross_holder`, `drilling_cross_stock`, `lathe_post_g76`, `lathe_post_tormach`, `lathe_post_tormach_thread`, `lathe_stroke`, `lathe_cycle_exit`, `per_op_files`, `post_not_judged`, `setup_mount`, `setup_mounts_post`, `coolant_followups`): all green, no existing assertion changed.

## Not exercised

- Not run on a real control.

body:
Adds the `set_workholding_max_rpm` row to the camcraft-mcp skill's Setups section, and a note on `get_job`'s per-setup `workholding_max_rpm` field. Text only.

**Row added** (after `load_machine`):

> `set_workholding_max_rpm { "max_rpm": number | null, "setup"?: string }`: State the rated maximum rpm of a setup's chuck or collet; `null` clears it. Refused with a named error: a missing or non-numeric value, zero, negative or non-finite numbers, anything under 1 rpm or over 100000 rpm, an unknown setup, and a value the setup already states. `setup` defaults to the active one. One undo step. At post time, a constant-rpm (G97) turning operation faster than the limit is refused by name, and a constant-surface-speed (G96) section's rpm ceiling is capped at it (Fanuc `G50 S`, Tormach `G96 D`).

**get_job note:** the description now ends "... status), and each setup's `workholding_max_rpm` (its stated limit, or `null`)."

**Where each fact was read (main at 0fc30b65):**
- Name, description, parameter schema (`max_rpm` required, `number|null`; `setup` optional string, defaults to active): `crates/app/src/mcp/workholding_tools.rs` lines 15-20 and 36-44.
- Registration: `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` line 69 (`super::workholding_tools::TOOLS`).
- Missing / non-numeric `max_rpm` refusals and the one-step history call: `workholding_tools.rs` lines 23-31.
- Active-setup default and unknown-setup refusal: `crates/app/src/mcp/setup_tools.rs` lines 66-72 (`setup_or_active`); no-declared-setup error at `workholding_tools.rs` line 29.
- Zero / negative / non-finite / under 1 / over 100000 refusals: `crates/app/src/setup_workholding.rs` lines 31-45 (`MAX_STATED_RPM`, `invalid`).
- Not-a-setup, no-op refusal, one undoable write with `invert`: `crates/app/src/commands/setup_workholding.rs` lines 28-43 and 63-70.
- `null` clears (stated as `None`): `workholding_tools.rs` line 25; `commands/setup_workholding.rs` line 20-25.
- Post time, G97 refusal by name: `crates/app/src/setup_workholding.rs` lines 68-105 (`program_problems`); G96 cap: lines 56-66 (`css_of`, min of tool and workholding, posts take min with machine).

title: docs(process): a P1-P9 priority scale replaces P0/P1/P2; PROCESS_VERSION 27
body:
Process change: the P0/P1/P2 scale becomes P1-P9 (lower number is picked first). **PROCESS_VERSION 29** (another process PR takes 28 and merges first; the merger renumbers if needed).

## Scale (AGENTS.md "Priorities")
| Label | Means | Was |
|---|---|---|
| `P1` | Unsafe or wrong output, crash, data loss | `P0` |
| `P2` | Main broken / regression with no workaround | red-gate `P1` |
| `P3` | Wrong behaviour a user hits, with a workaround | `P1` bugs |
| `P4` | Work the maintainer asked for | `P1` enhancements he opened |
| `P5` | Agent surface and tooling (MCP, process) | `P1` MCP / process |
| `P6` | Accepted enhancements, not scheduled | other `P1` enhancements |
| `P7` | Owed polish, small fixes | `P2` bugs and polish |
| `P8` | Ideas needing design/research | `P2` enhancements, `effort:max` |
| `P9` | Someday | - |

Only `P1` and `P2` block a release cut (maintainer's later choice); `P3` is worked ahead of planned work but never holds a cut.

## Rules changed (old -> new)
- Pick: "`P0` before `P1` before `P2`, then the oldest" -> lowest number first, then the oldest.
- `P?`: "instead of a `P0`/`P1`/`P2` label" / "picks `P0`/`P1`/`P2`" -> `P1`..`P9`.
- Enhancement lane: "then `P1` before `P2`" -> "then the lower number".
- Safety floor: "every `P0`" -> "every `P1`" is at least `effort:high`.
- MCP issues: `P1` -> `P5` (the 2026-11-10 quote kept, dated).
- Red batch gate: "`P0` if wrong output or gouge, else `P1`" -> `P1` / `P2`; cut blocker "a `P0` it opened" -> any open `P1` or `P2` (wide reading, per the maintainer; a `P3` never) - superseded the first draft, which kept "it opened".
- New filing rules: `P1`-`P3` defects only; `P4` only with the maintainer's words quoted; follow-ups are `P7` unless a defect; never `P?`.

## Files
`AGENTS.md`, `README.md`, `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`, `.claude/skills/{gh-issues (SKILL, claim-workflow, both evals), classify-effort, camcraft-mcp}`, `docs/decisions/1189-p1-p9-scale.md` (decision + migration script). work-issue, review-prs, resolve-conflicts, agents, issue templates, CONTRIBUTING (absent), docs/ and `xtask/src` name no priority level (xtask reads no priority labels; no xtask test run needed). The pick-next jq `test("^P[0-9]$")` already matches P1..P9; its default for unlabelled became `PZ` so it does not tie with `P9`.

## Grep
`grep -rn "P0" AGENTS.md .claude .github README.md`: only AGENTS.md:93 and :100 (the quoted maintainer words and the "Was" column) and two Stripe URLs containing `P0F...`. Evals parse as YAML.

## No label or issue was changed by this PR
The migration script is in the decision file; the merging session runs it once (`--dry-run` first) right after the merge, then comments on #681 with the mapping. The "main is broken" `P2` set is an explicit `--main-broken` list, not guessed from labels.

**Fork:** pull the process files, create the same labels, relabel its own issues with the same mapping (old `P1` first, then `P0` -> `P1`).

Changelog: none
Effort: medium

Fixes #1189

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)



## Rework after review (head after this push)
1. Cut rule: one sentence, same words in "Priorities" and "Fixes are tested in the background": a minor/major cut does not start while any `P1` or `P2` issue is open (a `P3` or lower never holds one). Decision file corrected.
2. MCP: `P5` is owed agent-surface work; a defect in MCP code is rated `P1`-`P3`.
3. No priority = untriaged: triaged by the first agent that reads it, before any pick; both gh-issues Pick snippets list such issues first under "TRIAGE THESE FIRST" and exclude `P?`; an issue found with two numbers is reported and read by the lower.
4. claim-workflow.md agrees with SKILL.md ("lowest P number first"; no `P9` default); pick-next eval updated.
5-8. Migration script rewritten: `P?` issues never get a number (stray `P2` beside `P?` removed and listed); `--main-broken` and `--requested` are explicit lists, with area:build bug candidates printed; old `P1` order bug (`P3`/`P2`), requested (`P4`), mcp/build/process (`P5`), else `P6`; old `P2` enhancements `P8` (`P6` only with an open PR linked); idempotent via a plan file with a per-row done flag, refusing with "migration already started: pass the plan file (--plan FILE)"; `P0` kept and re-described as retired, never deleted; end-state assertions and counts. Its `--dry-run` was run read-only against the repo to test it.



## Re-check follow-ups (head 78681207)
- Merged main; PROCESS_VERSION stays 29 (main reads 28).
- Old-`P1` issues without `bug` that are `area:mcp` or titled `MCP:` plan as `P5`; one WITH `bug` is a bug whatever its area. The 11 label-less MCP items (#1084, #1062, #1013, #962, #954, #937, #734, #732, #731, #730, #729) now plan as `P5` (dry-run, read-only, confirmed). Other label-less old-`P1`s are still listed for a hand check (none today).
- Dry-run counts (main-broken empty, `--requested 530-548,617,661,1103,1104`): P1 5, P2 0, P3 17, P4 20, P5 25, P6 22, P7 20, P8 51; `P?` 5 (three lose a stray `P2`: #655, #658, #659); 19 untriaged. Issues filed since will differ.
- An old-style `P1` filed while the migration runs must be re-rated by hand.
- The end check fails (exit 1, lists them) until the 19 untriaged issues have a priority. Chosen: the runner triages those first (no new flag; simplest).

title: fix(post): a stop or go-home asked after a live-tool section posts at the end of that section
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps`: the section end's C-axis live-tool branch returned before `afterOp()`, the function that writes the optional stop (M01), program stop (M00) and go-home asked after an operation. The ask was neither posted after the live section nor reset, so it came out after the NEXT section. The live branch now falls through to the one shared `afterOp()` call, so every section, turning or live, ends with its own ask. A refused live section (no live-tool words) still consumes its ask.

## Reproduction (turning section, live cross drill asking the stop, turning section; test mill-turn `millturn-live.mch`)

Before (main 6f1adf06), program stop asked after the cross drill:
```
M9
M1004
M1002
G99
(OPERATION: Face two - G54)
...
M9
M05
M00            <- after Face two, not after the cross drill
G28 U0 W0
```
Optional stop: the same, `M01` after Face two's `M05`. Go home: `G28 U0` / `G28 W0` after Face two's `M05`, and the program-end home then skipped as already done.

After (golden `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/fanuc-lathe/live_then_stop.nc`):
```
M9
M1004
M1002
G99
M01            <- end of the cross drill (M00 / G28 U0 + G28 W0 in the same place)
(OPERATION: Face two - G54)
...
M9
M05
G28 U0 W0
M30
```

## End-of-section order (live section)

`G80` if open, `M9`, live spindle off (`live_tool.spindle_off`), C axis off (`c_axis_off`), `G99`, then the asked M01 / M00 / G28 U0 + G28 W0. The turning branch's order (coolant off, spindle stop, spindle-mode reset, stop words) with the live release words in the spindle-stop place: the driven tool is stopped and C released before an operator reaches in, and the home moves X and Z only, after C is released. No new codes: every word is the machine file's or one the post already wrote. Recorded in `docs/decisions/1188-live-section-after-op.md`.

## Other early returns checked

- `fanuc-lathe.cps` / `tormach-lathe.cps` `startPreamble` / `endPreamble`: only the `sectionOpen` guards; `tormach-lathe.cps` has no live branch and calls `afterOp()` on every section end - fine.
- Mill posts `fanuc`, `haas`, `heidenhain`, `mazak`, `sinumerik`, `doosan-dnm`: no return before `afterOp()` - fine.
- `tormach`, `carvera`, `tormach-plasma`: write no after-operation words and do not declare `afterModes`; the engine refuses a stop/home ask for them by name (seen in the new refusal goldens) - fine.

## Goldens

No existing golden changes (all `crates/app/tests/golden` and `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden` byte-identical). New: recorded stream `live_then_stop.cnc` and its goldens in all 11 per-post suites (`fanuc-lathe/live_then_stop.nc`; the other ten are named refusals - no liveTooling / afterModes).

## How tested

Pinning tests (`crates/post/tests/script_fanuc_lathe.rs`): `an_optional_stop_after_a_live_section_posts_at_its_end`, `a_program_stop_after_a_live_section_posts_at_its_end`, `a_go_home_after_a_live_section_posts_at_its_end` (each: the word after `M1004` and `M1002`, before the next section's first block, posted exactly once), `no_stop_asked_after_a_live_section_posts_no_stop`; the three asked-stop tests fail on main. Recorded case `live_then_stop` in every `script_*` suite plus `recorded_streams::live_then_stop_stream_is_current`.

Gate: `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (all suites), app `lathe_post`, `lathe_post_css`, `lathe_post_tormach`, `lathe_post_refusals`, `c_axis_live`, `c_axis_unwind`, `lathe_cycle_exit`, `conformance`, `golden_cl`, `solid_law_goldens` green; clippy `-D warnings` on camcraft-post + camcraft-app clean; `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` green on head f3c3c34a.

## Not exercised

Not run on a real control. The live-tool codes of the test machine (M1001-M1004) are placeholders, not a builder's words.

title: fix(turning): the workholding rpm limit is judged for the post that runs - every work-spindle section, never a live tool's speed
body:
**Built on #1202 (merged to main as 75ad984c)** - its dialect reader and section derivation are unified here; nothing of #1202 is duplicated. The two predicates are now one.

## What changed

**First: the workholding limit no longer fails open.** Two reviews found the dangerous direction: a mill-turn's on-centre Drill at 8000 rpm under a 2000 rpm chuck posted `G97 S8000 M03` (head 81e4cb01), and the same drill with no machine loaded, or a mill machine, posted through either lathe post (head b0434952). The rule now keys on the POST that runs, not on the operation's kind; the machine's kind only ever widens what is judged (a milling post on a lathe or mill-turn, below):

- Section: `lathe_voice::voice_of` (#1202's one derivation, also its lathe door; its live-tool test `post::dialect::states_live_tool` is what `post::dump` writes `PARAM LiveTool` from - the stream is byte-identical, all goldens and recorded suites untouched).
- Script: `post::dialect::work_voice(cps)` - the manifest `capabilities` mask read three ways (turning -> work spindle, milling only -> tool spindle, none -> undeclared). `dialect::speaks_turning` now reads it too, so both rules share one mask reader.

Third review (head c08685ea): a mill-turn's facing op at 3000 rpm under a 2000 rpm chuck posted `S3000 M3` through `fanuc.cps` / `haas.cps` (main refused it). Fixed: on a lathe or mill-turn a work-spindle section is judged at its rpm whatever the post calls itself - chosen over a door that refuses turning kinds through a milling post, because judging adds a refusal only over the limit, while a door would change programs that post today with no limit stated.

### Every cell: machine kind x post dialect x section (verdict with a limit stated)

Work = a section `lathe_voice::voice_of` puts on the work spindle (turning kinds, on-centre Drill); Tool = a milling section (door-refused under a turning post); C = live tool (moves state C).

| Machine | Post | Work | Tool | C |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| none | turning | judged (on-centre drill; turning kinds not creatable) | not judged - #1190 door refuses it | C rate (no machine: no C rate -> refused by name) |
| none | milling | not judged (tool spindle) | not judged | not judged (engine refuses a live section through a mill post) |
| none | undeclared | judged | judged (stricter, #1199) | C rate |
| mill | turning | judged (on-centre drill) | not judged - door refuses | C rate |
| mill | milling | not judged (tool spindle; turning kinds not creatable) | not judged | not judged (engine refuses) |
| mill | undeclared | judged | judged (stricter) | C rate |
| mill-turn | turning | judged | not judged - door refuses | C rate |
| mill-turn | milling | **judged (this fix)** | not judged (tool spindle) | C rate |
| mill-turn | undeclared | judged | judged (stricter) | C rate |
| lathe | turning | judged | n/a (milling kinds not creatable) | C rate |
| lathe | milling | judged | judged (one spindle holds the chuck) | C rate |
| lathe | undeclared | judged | n/a | C rate |

Pinned: the Work/Tool columns by `lathe_workholding_mill_post::every_machine_dialect_and_section_cell_gives_its_verdict` (facing and mill Face through fanuc-lathe / fanuc / undeclared on none, mill, mill-turn, lathe) and `lathe_workholding_kinds::a_lathe_post_is_held_to_the_chuck_whatever_machine_is_mounted` (on-centre drill, none and mill); the C column on a mill-turn by `lathe_workholding_live` (other machines' C cells read from the code, not built).

And the original #1174 fix holds: a 10000 rpm live cross drill under a 100 rpm chuck is not refused by the tool's rpm. Refusal text shows one decimal when whole rpm would print the speed and the limit the same ("2000.4 rpm ... maximum of 2000.0 rpm").

No post script touched. MCP `set_workholding_max_rpm` unchanged. Decision: `docs/decisions/1174-chuck-limit-work-spindle-only.md`.

## Pinning tests

- `lathe_workholding_mill_post::a_mill_turn_facing_op_through_a_milling_post_is_held_to_the_chuck` (fanuc and haas: 3000 over 2000 refused by name, at 2000 posts; fails on c08685ea)
- `lathe_workholding_mill_post::a_mill_turn_milling_section_through_a_milling_post_is_not_judged` (mill Face at 8000 posts `S8000` through fanuc and haas)
- `lathe_workholding_mill_post::every_machine_dialect_and_section_cell_gives_its_verdict`

- `lathe_workholding_kinds::a_lathe_post_is_held_to_the_chuck_whatever_machine_is_mounted` (no machine and a mill machine, fanuc-lathe and tormach-lathe: refused at 8000, posts at exactly 2000)
- `lathe_workholding_kinds::a_mill_post_drives_the_tool_spindle_so_the_chuck_limit_does_not_judge_it` (fanuc.cps posts `S8000 M3` with a limit stated)
- `lathe_workholding_kinds::an_undeclared_script_takes_the_stricter_reading` (fanuc-lathe without its manifest line: refused)
- `lathe_workholding_kinds::a_milling_script_on_a_plain_lathe_still_turns_the_work`
- `lathe_workholding_kinds::a_speed_a_hair_over_the_chuck_prints_a_decimal`
- `lathe_workholding_kinds::a_mill_turn_on_centre_drill_is_judged_like_the_lathes` (+ the Bore is refused by the #1202 door), the per-kind table tests (lathe, mill-turn in thirds, heavy slow-kinds lane)
- `lathe_workholding_live` (cross drill not judged; C section by C rate; unrated C), `lathe_workholding_rpm` (G97 3000/2000 refused; G96 clamp; `None` posts as before)
- `post::dialect::tests::the_mask_names_the_spindle_a_plain_section_drives`

## How tested

`cargo test -p camcraft-post`: 223 passed, 0 failed. App: lathe_workholding_mill_post 3 (new), lathe_workholding_kinds 10 (+1 heavy), lathe_workholding_live 3, lathe_workholding_rpm 6, lathe_work_spindle 5, mcp_workholding 1, lathe_spindle_law 8, lathe_post 7, lathe_post_css 10, c_axis_live 5, c_axis_unwind 7, recorded_post_streams 2, operations 117, golden_cl 25, project_roundtrip 71 - all pass. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` green on the final head.

## Not exercised

Not run on a real machine. Kinds that do not generate from seed params on the test bar are covered by the derivation, not posted one by one. The heavy slow-kinds row was not re-run after the #1202 merge. A posed or off-centre section under an undeclared script is judged at its rpm (stricter than needed, until #1199). C sections are judged by the stated C ceiling, not per-move C speed. `work_voice` loads the script in the JS engine; the gate caches it once per distinct post.

Changelog: The workholding (chuck) rpm limit is judged for the post that runs: every section a turning post opens on the work spindle is held to it whatever the operation or machine (a mill-turn's on-centre drill, or a lathe post with no or a mill machine, is refused over the limit), C-axis live-tool sections by the machine's C rate, a milling post's tool spindle is not judged, and a live-tool cross drill is no longer refused by the tool's rpm

title: fix(post): the lathe posts state G97 before a section that is not constant surface speed
body:
## What changed

A lathe section that posted `G96` now cancels it at its end: a bare `G97` right after the main spindle stop (`M05` / `M5`), before any after-operation word (`M01`, `M00`, home). Every following section opens under constant rpm unless it states `G96` itself, and no program ends in constant-surface-speed mode. Both lathe posts take the rule: `assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` and `assets/posts/tormach-lathe.cps`. No other shipped post writes `G96` (`git grep -n G96 assets/posts`).

### Reproduction (Fanuc lathe, test-bench mill-turn, CSS turning then a `LiveTool` section at 3000 rpm)

Before (main at 6a10c5ad):
```
G50 S6000
G96 S200 M03
...
M9
M05
G54
(T0202 EM)
T0202
G98
M1001
M1003 S3000
```
After:
```
G50 S6000
G96 S200 M03
...
M9
M05
G97
G54
(T0202 EM)
T0202
G98
M1001
M1003 S3000
```

### The rule, and why (full entry: `docs/decisions/1173-g97-before-live-tool.md`)

**The section end cancels G96 when the section posted it.** I picked this over "every section start states its own mode" because every following section goes through the section end, whatever its kind: live tool, drill on centre, thread, tap, probe, speed 0, no spindle stated, a legacy stream, or a kind added later. A rule at the start would have to be repeated in every `startPreamble` branch. It also could not cover the program boundary: the header states no spindle mode, so an unconditional `G97` in the live branch would change every live-tool program, including ones that never had a G96. The section-end rule changes only programs that post a G96.

The cost: one bare `G97` line per CSS section. Two CSS sections in a row post `G96 S200 M03` ... `M05` / `G97` / ... `G96 S200 M03` ... `M05` / `G97`. The flip is harmless because the spindle is already stopped, and it is pinned as the negative case.

Unchanged: when G96 is chosen, the G50 / `D` clamp logic (machine, tool and workholding limits), the per-rev feed words, and every program with no G96 section.

Tormach PathPilot lathe has no live branch: it does not declare `liveTooling`, so the engine refuses a C section by name. Its drill and thread sections could still follow a G96 section, so it gets the same rule.

## Goldens that changed

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/facing_css.nc`: one line gained:
  ```
   M9
   M05
  +G97
   G28 U0 W0
   M30
  ```
  No other existing golden changed. Every lathe golden (`lathe_post`, `lathe_post_tormach`, `lathe_post_tormach_thread`, `c_axis_live`, `c_axis_unwind`, `conformance`, `golden_cl`, `solid_law_goldens`) and every recorded per-post golden is byte-identical, because none of them posts a G96.
- New: recorded case `css_then_live` (stream `crates/post/tests/recorded/streams/css_then_live.cnc`, built and guarded by `recorded_streams.rs`). It posts on a test-bench fixture `crates/post/tests/recorded/machines/millturn-live.mch`: the shipped `millturn.mch` plus placeholder live-tool words M1001-M1004. These are not a real builder's codes, so the file stays a test fixture and is not shipped. `recorded::machine_of` now returns a path so a case can use such a fixture. `fanuc-lathe/css_then_live.nc` shows `M05` / `G97` before the live branch. Every other post refuses the C section by name: 10 new `.refusal` goldens.
- Assertions updated because of the new `G97`: `lathe_post_css::applying_the_turning_suggestion...` (it said "no G97 at all"; now: no `G97 S`, one bare `G97` after `M05`) and `lathe_post_tormach::css_arcs_part_load_and_a_trip_home_speak_linuxcnc` (it now ends `M9 M5 G97 G30 M30`).

## Pinning tests

- `lathe_post_refusals::a_live_tool_section_after_a_css_one_posts_g97_before_its_live_spindle`: the twin with a `LiveTool` section. It asserts `M05\nG97\nG54\n(T0202 EM)\nT0202\nG98\nM1001\nM1003 S3000\n` and checks that the live section's own end adds nothing.
- `lathe_post_refusals::a_thread_after_a_css_section_opens_under_g97`: `G97` is the mode word before the thread's first S.
- `lathe_post_refusals::a_drill_after_a_css_section_finds_g97_already_in_force`: the same check for a drill on centre.
- `lathe_post_refusals::two_css_sections_in_a_row_each_state_their_own_g96` and `lathe_post_tormach::two_css_sections_in_a_row_each_state_their_own_g96`: the negative case. Exactly two `G96` lines and two bare `G97` lines, no `G97 S`, and the program ends in `G97`.
- `lathe_post_tormach::a_section_without_surface_speed_posts_g97_after_one_with_it`: extended so the CSS section ends `M5\nG97\n`.
- `script_*::css_then_live` (all 11 per-post suites) and `recorded_streams::css_then_live_stream_is_current`.

## How tested

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: every suite green.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app` on `lathe_post`, `lathe_post_css`, `lathe_post_tormach`, `lathe_post_tormach_thread`, `lathe_post_refusals`, `lathe_workholding_rpm`, `c_axis_live`, `c_axis_unwind`, `lathe_cycle_exit`, `lathe_spindle_law`, `conformance`, `golden_cl`, `solid_law_goldens`, `recorded_post_streams`: all green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on the final head: it ran the post suites (all 19 binaries: ok) and, because a shared golden (`facing_css.nc`) changed, every app suite (1195 s). All green except `coarse_laws`: 4 tests, which are already red on main at 6a10c5ad and unrelated to this diff. The test expects the old refusal text "re-import with a larger budget", and `model_fidelity::TOO_COARSE` on main says "larger STEP facet budget". That is tracked by #1175 / #1178. What the gate chose: post: axis_direction_cli, comp, comp_plane, cycle_hop, mch_head_search, post_engine, recorded_streams, script_* (11); app: every suite (shared test input `tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/facing_css.nc`).

## Not exercised

- Not run on a real control. The behaviour of a bare `G97` on a stopped spindle comes from the Fanuc-style and LinuxCNC public programming references, not from a machine.
- The live-tool words in the fixture are placeholders.
- The workholding-clamp interaction was not re-derived: `lathe_workholding_rpm` is green and the clamp code is untouched.

Changelog: The lathe posts (Fanuc lathe, Tormach PathPilot lathe) cancel constant surface speed with G97 at the end of every section that used G96, so a following live-tool, drilling or threading section never runs its S word as a surface speed (#1173)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1173

title: feat(edm): wire EDM 4-axis - upper and lower profiles paired into rulings by a stated rule
body:
Stacked on #1163 (on #1144, #1139, #1123, #560, #551). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

A Wire Contour can now cut the ruled surface between two profiles given separately (#290 D2).

- **Op.** `WireContourOp.four_axis: Option<WireFourAxis>` (`pairing`, `sync`, `tolerance`); absent by default, omitted from the file when absent, so a one-profile cut's file, stamp, CL and NC are unchanged. The pairing rule has no default in the file. Edited through `EditOperationParams` / the MCP parameter patch (the same JSON door); the page shows the rule, the tolerance and the sync pairs as numbers.
- **Profiles.** The selection is read as two picks (a face's one outer ring, or a closed edge chain), each flat; the higher is the upper profile. Their heights must be the op's top and bottom planes (`app::operation::wire_ruled`).
- **Pairing** (`motion::wire_edm::pairing`). One monotone map between the two rings' arc lengths, fixed by anchors: by normalised arc length from each profile's point nearest the start hole, or by sync pairs with arc length between them. A ruling at every vertex of either ring; each move ends on a ruling's lower point, its pose the wire toward the upper point; upright at the start hole. The path's note states the rule.
- **Laws** (`motion::wire_edm::ruled_laws`). Fold: consecutive rulings whose ends run against each other (`a . b < 0` - the section turns back inside the part height). Crossing: the wire's section at a quarter height crosses itself. Ruled kerf: at 33 heights the wire's section stands off the stated surface by #1163's leaning-kerf reach `k sqrt(1 + (t.u)^2)`.
- **A twisted ruled surface.** A straight wire cannot touch it along its whole height, so offsetting both profiles by the kerf gouges between the planes (about 12 um on a square-to-round corner with a 0.33 mm kerf). The generator widens the offset on both planes, uniformly, until the kerf stands clear at every height read, says in the notes how much stands on the profile planes, and refuses past the op's `tolerance` (default 0.05 mm). A constant taper needs exactly #1163's `1 / cos(angle)`.
- **Refused by name:** crossed sync points ("sync pair #3 crosses sync pair #2"), doubled, unpaired or off-profile sync points, a folding or self-crossing pairing, open profiles or one open and one closed, a ruling past `edm.max_taper_deg` (unstated refuses), a twist past the tolerance, profiles that are not two / not flat / not on the op's planes, a taper angle stated beside the two profiles, a lead whose leaning kerf enters the surface. The U/V stroke, U/V axes, guide planes and guide reach are #1163's machine check, unchanged (it reads poses).
- **Verify.** A 4-axis cut's poses are read as the wire's lean exactly as a stated taper's; kerf, threading and slug run at every judged height; a gouge blocks the post.
- **Post.** `PARAM WireFourAxis` (the rule's words) opens the section; `wire-iso.cps` writes the same `taper_on` / `uv` / `taper_off` codes from `edm.codes` as a tapered section and names the cut in a comment.

## Sources (Clean Room)

Piegl and Tiller, "The NURBS Book" (ruled surface between two parametrised curves, chord-length parametrisation); Farin, "Curves and Surfaces for CAGD"; do Carmo, "Differential Geometry of Curves and Surfaces" (the tangent plane along a ruling of a non-developable ruled surface); Liu, "Five-axis NC cylindrical milling of sculptured surfaces", CAD 27(12), 1995. No vendor post, control manual or CAM product behaviour was consulted. Decisions: `docs/decisions/537-wire-4axis.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests:

- `crates/app/tests/wire_4axis.rs`
  - `a_square_to_round_punch_posts_its_golden_and_verifies` - goldens `tests/golden/wire_4axis_punch.cl` (a pose on every move) and `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_4axis_punch.nc` (synthetic fixture); the wire clause reports no problem.
  - `a_constant_taper_by_sync_points_is_the_taper_golden_and_arc_length_differs` - the CL equals #1163's `wire_taper_punch.cl` byte for byte, the NC equals `wire_taper_punch.nc` but for the comment naming the cut; arc length on the same two profiles gives other rulings.
  - `crossed_folded_and_unpaired_sync_points_are_refused_by_name`
  - `a_pairing_past_the_machine_or_off_the_planes_is_refused_by_name` (max taper at generation, U stroke at the post, one profile, taper + 4-axis, planes off the profiles)
  - `a_ruling_that_gouges_the_part_blocks_the_post`
  - `the_four_axis_block_round_trips_and_its_rule_is_never_defaulted` (JSON door, stamp, undo, the door's refusal of a NaN tolerance)
- `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/ruled_tests.rs` (8 tests): square-to-round keeps the kerf out and a zero tolerance refuses it; arc length vs sync points; the constant taper equals `wire_contour_tapered` move for move; crossed / folded / unpaired / off-profile / doubled sync points; open and mismatched profiles; steep rulings; a conical die.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/536-wire-taper` green on the final head 263442bc (motion lib, the whole app suite set - a new golden is shared test input - and the mapped ui suites; 0 failed); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## What was not exercised

- No real EDM control (D10): the goldens are posted against the synthetic fixture with invented codes.
- The die side at the app level (the motion crate pins a conical die); a die whose start hole is equidistant from several sides has no single nearest point - its arc-length seam is then the first tie, and a pairing that folds or twists for it is refused, not guessed.
- A model whose tessellated twisted wall bulges past the ruled surface of its two end profiles is refused by the wire laws as a gouge (the fixtures here are split along the inner diagonal). Follow-up #1170.
- Sync points are numbers on the page, not viewport picks (#1171). Fans and profiles stitched from several runs are refused by name (#1172). Open-profile 4-axis waits for #1109.
- UI: the new rows have no structural-test assertion of their own; no snapshot PNG was changed.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill's DTO notes are not updated (a process file); the block rides `params` through the existing tools (#1108).

Changelog: Wire EDM 4-axis: a Wire Contour cuts the ruled surface between separately picked upper and lower profiles, paired by arc length or by sync points; crossed, folding or unpaired pairings, rulings past the machine's taper and U/V limits and a twist past the stated tolerance are refused by name.

Effort: max (no escalation)

Fixes #537

title: feat(ui): original icons for tool kinds, tree rows, status badges and actions
body:
Slice 2 of #661: sections 4, 6, 7 and 8. Same pipeline, grid and style as slice 1 (PR #1116); nothing in `cargo xtask icons`' render/lint/check changed.

## What changed
- **31 new SVG masters** in `assets/ui/svg/` with their 32 px PNGs (`cargo xtask icons`; `--check` 0 breaches; the 41 `op-*` PNGs are byte-identical).
- **Tool kinds -> icons:** `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tool_icons.rs` (exhaustive match on `ToolKind`, sibling of `op_icons.rs`).
- **Status badges:** `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tree_badges.rs` - `status_badge` (what the row text already says: `BLOCKED` or warnings -> warning; else never / ok / stale; a stale path outranks its old warnings) and `row_glyph`, which paints the row glyph plus the badge on a disc of the row ground. `painted.rs` calls it (painted.rs shrinks 419 -> 414). `OpStatus` is unchanged, no new state, no command.
- `IconSet::load` also leaves a shared copy of the handles in the egui context (`IconSet::from_ctx`), because the property pages are not handed an `IconSet`.
- **11 PNGs deleted** (post, sim, fixture, debug-info, and the Tabler box-model, cube, transform, player-play, maximize, eye, eye-off). `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` is updated: 8 Tabler chrome glyphs remain, so the Tabler licence stays.
- **`cargo xtask icons --sheet` labels each icon** with its file stem, using a 3x5 bitmap font of our own (`xtask/src/icon_font.rs`). **PROCESS_VERSION 25 -> 26** (xtask is a process file).
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/661-icons-tools-tree.md`.

## Icons by section (all drawn original; none from Tabler; nothing from SolidCraft, HSMWorks, Fusion or any CAM product)
- **4. Tool kinds (13):** end mill, ball nose, bull nose, drill, tap, boring bar, turning insert, grooving blade, threading insert, form gauge, chamfer mill (`ToolKind::Taper`, which the UI calls a chamfer mill), probe, and, **beyond the checklist, plasma torch** (`ToolKind::Torch`, #670).
  - Mill tools hang from a solid holder block. Lathe tools run left from a solid tool-post block on the right (the turning ops have their chuck on the left).
  - That frame is what keeps Drill the tool apart from Drill the op, and Probe the tool apart from Probe the op.
- **6. Tree rows (7):** setup, part/model, stock, work offset, fixture, machine, operations folder.
- **7. Badges (4):** not generated (ring), OK (disc with a check), stale (disc with clock hands), warning (triangle with "!"). They are solid shapes with the mark cut out (even-odd fill) so they read at 9 px.
- **8. Actions (7):** generate (raster path, arrow and spark), post (page with an arrow out), simulate (play mark with speed lines), show, hide, frame all, debug info.

## Wired / drawn but not wired
- **Wired:**
  - Tool library rows in the browser.
  - The setup's Tool list table.
  - A glyph of the selected tool's kind beside the op page's tool picker. The combo's items stay text: an icon per item needs a custom popup.
  - The Setups, Machine and Operations tree rows. Machine wore the simulate glyph and Operations the generate glyph until now.
  - The ribbon Setups door (now the setup glyph instead of the vise).
  - Status badges on every op row.
  - All 7 actions, through the existing `Icon` slots (same keys, new files).
- **Not wired:** the Tools page Catalog rows and its summary line in `pages.rs` (1000+ lines; the 400-line law said do not grow it). Setup *node* rows keep their radio, not an icon. The warning badge has a real data source (`tool_problem_of` plus the cached warnings), so nothing is left drawn but unwired.

## Least happy with
- `tool-form` (could pass for goggles).
- `act-generate`.
- Redrawn after the first review round:
  - `tree-part` is now a stepped solid and `tree-stock` a plain block, so they no longer read alike at 16 px.
  - `tree-fixture` is now two tall jaws, the clamped part and the screw bar, no longer a dense block.

## How tested
- **Pinning tests:**
  - `every_tool_kind_has_its_own_svg_mastered_icon`: enumerates the kinds from the editor's own kind numbering, not a hand list; every kind gets a distinct `tool-*` glyph with a master, never an op's glyph.
  - `tree_rows_badges_and_actions_are_svg_mastered`.
  - `status_badge_follows_the_row_status`.
  - Slice 1's `every_op_kind_has_its_own_svg_mastered_icon` and its "no two slots share a PNG" assert still pass.
  - xtask's `committed_icon_pngs_match_their_svg_masters` and the new `sheet_labels_wrap_stems_and_keep_the_family`.
- **Gates:**
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib`: 577 passed.
  - `cargo xtask icons --check`: 0 breaches.
  - clippy `-D warnings` on xtask and camcraft-ui: clean.
  - `cargo test -p xtask`: 49 passed, fully green after merging main. The `lathe_post_css` gate-map break was main's own and is fixed there by PR #1187.
  - `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on the final head: green (ui suites ok, xtask ok).
- Merged origin/main (37d93ae5 and later) with no conflicts; PROCESS_VERSION stays 26, since main reads 25.
- I looked at the 16 px contact sheet on the dark and light bands and redrew simulate (the first draft read as a figure).

## Not exercised
- Not seen in the running app (no GUI launch): the badge's placement and ground disc, the picker glyph, and the tree rows at real DPI.

## Snapshots
- No file under `crates/ui/tests/snapshots/` changed. The browser tree, ribbon (Setups door, action glyphs), status strip and op page goldens will differ at the next cut's refresh.

Changelog: Tool kinds, the browser's setup rows, operation status badges and the CamCraft actions have their own original icons; the tree shows each operation's status as a badge (#661)

Refs #661

title: fix(turning): read a lathe holder body on the holder's own side of the axis
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main 7e3c75f9).

## What changed

The holder law (#369) read a lathe body point at `|X + x|`, with `X` signed along the path's signed meridian (`SignedMeridian`). That frame takes its + side from the path's **first** off-axis point, which need not be the side the holder stands on. Take a rear tool that starts a hair past centre: every later tip is at X < 0 of that frame, and the body was read mirrored through the axis. A lip reaching the part was judged clear, and a clear body was judged to cross the axis.

- New `crates/app/src/operation/turning_holder_side.rs`: `holder_side` gives the holder's side as a property of the whole path. A rigid holder never flips mid-path, so the side is the one the path reaches farthest on. The other side may hold only a past-centre overrun of at most `PAST_CENTRE` = 2.5 mm, as in a face pass cleaning the centre pip. A path on both sides beyond that, or within 2.5 mm of the axis on both sides, is refused by name: "the lathe holder body cannot be judged: the path stands on both sides of the spindle axis ...".
- `turning_holder::judge` reads `Reach::radii(side * X)`. On the + side the call is `radii(x)` exactly as before, so it is byte-identical. `body_axes`, which draws the body (#1038), flips its radial by the same side, so the drawn holder is still the judged one.
- `camcraft-tools::lathe_holder`: the docs now state that X is signed along the holder's own +x, which is away from the axis on the holder's side, front or rear post alike.

**Which signed X the generators produce.** Every turning generator places its tips at `Frame::point(rho >= 0, ..)`, and a face pass runs to `rho = 0` at most. So every generated path has its tips at X >= 0 of its own frame and reads as before. No turning op today carries X < 0, so the defect was latent and the issue stays P2, not re-rated P0. This is stated in the pinning test and in `docs/decisions/1102-lathe-body-signed-reach.md`.

**UI/MCP wording.** Main has no "+x points away from the spindle axis" text. That text is in #1043, and under this law it is now true as written. No wording change was needed here.

**Expected merge with #1043 / #1061.** This PR touches only the reach reading in `turning_holder.rs` (a `side` field on `Scene`, one `holder_side` call in `judge` and one in `body_axes`, and the `radii` argument), plus a new module. Merging either way should be additive.

## How tested

- `operation::turning_holder_side::tests::the_side_is_where_the_path_reaches_and_a_past_centre_overrun_keeps_it`: front paths are +1, a face run 0.4 past centre keeps +1, and a rear path starting 0.5 past centre is -1. Both-sides paths are refused by name, and so is a non-finite radius.
- `operation::turning_holder_side::tests::a_rear_tool_past_centre_is_read_on_its_own_side_like_its_front_mirror`: this runs `judge` end to end. A rear tool (tip at X -8) whose body lip reaches the part is convicted, and the same tool with an outward body passes. Both match the front mirror at X +8. A face start 0.4 past centre reads on the front side. A both-sides path is refused.
- Mutation check: with the old `radii(x)` reading put back, the rear pin fails (`Ok([])` against `Ok([(1, true)])`), which is the missed strike.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head bd33d29b: green (app suites, the 130-suite gate map of `app::operation` plus `--lib`, and the ui suites; 0 failed, 9.8 min). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-tools --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- A real rear-turret machine definition, because none exists. Also the GUI drawing of a flipped body (the `body_axes` flip is not pinned by its own test).
- No golden or snapshot changes.

Changelog: The lathe holder law reads a holder body on its own side of the spindle axis for a tip at either signed X, and refuses by name a path that stands on both sides (#1102)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1102

title: feat(edm): sinker orbit patterns (circular, vector, planetary) as explicit moves
body:
**Stacked on #1131** (M5's #541, sinker burn to depth, branch `issue/541-sinker-burn-depth`). Retarget to `main` before #1131 merges. Fork synced at v0.18.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 17).

## What changed

A Sinker Burn can now **orbit at the burn floor** after the plunge. The orbit is circular, vector or planetary, and it is expanded into explicit Feed chords (#290 D3), so the 3-axis stock sim's box atom (#541) verifies every move that would post. Corner joins are included, under the same laws as #541's burns.

- `motion::sinker_orbit` (new) holds the pattern geometry.
  - circular: out along +X to the radius, then one full circle;
  - vector: out to the radius and back along N evenly spaced directions from +X;
  - planetary: an Archimedean spiral from 0 to the radius over N turns, closed by a full circle.
  - Every vertex is on or inside the stated radius (an ulp-past rounding is pulled back in), so no chord overshoots it. Chords keep a sagitta of 0.001 mm or less. Their count is a multiple of 4, so the ±X/±Y directions are vertices and a rectangular electrode's walls move out by exactly the radius. The counts are bounded (vectors 1..=72, turns 1..=20), so an orbit cannot balloon into a hang.
- `motion::sinker::burn_to_depth` runs the orbit at the tip Z at the servo feed and returns to the centre before the rapid retract. With `orbit: None` the plain plunge's CL and params digest are unchanged.
- `SinkerBurnOp.orbit: Option<SinkerOrbit>` is an additive field and file key (`orbit: { kind, radius, vectors, turns }`), so old files load. It is edited through `CreateOperation` / `EditOperationParams`. MCP reaches it through the existing params JSON door (`add_operation` / `edit_operation`, `"orbit": null` drops it). There is no new command, so there is no new MCP tool. The minimal sinker page gets Orbit / radius / vectors / turns rows on Passes.
- **Machine law** (`sinker_op::orbit_law`, #290 D6), refused by name at generation:
  - `machine X lists no vector orbit under edm.orbits ...`
  - `machine X states no maximum orbit radius (edm.max_orbit_radius) ...` (absent is not unlimited)
  - `the circular orbit radius 0.600 exceeds machine X's maximum orbit radius 0.500`
  - The job and the staleness stamp read it through `burn_gap`, so a re-stated orbit list or maximum marks the op stale. A garbled orbit is refused at the door (`is_sane`).
- **No schema change.** `edm.orbits[]` and `edm.max_orbit_radius` already exist in the `.mch` edm section from #530 (on this base), and #1141's post reads the same fields. They are read as they are. This PR emits no `EdmOrbit` PARAM: the orbit posts as its explicit moves, and a canned word on top would be a double orbit (D3's later item).
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/544-sinker-orbits.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/sinker_orbit.rs` (new, 6 tests):
  - `sinker_orbit_circular_matches_golden`: golden `tests/golden/sinker_orbit_circular.cl`, which I read. It has the plunge to Z 14.050, out to +0.200 X, 32 CCW chords on the r = 0.2 circle back to +X, a return to the centre, and the retract. Max excursion is 0.200.
  - `a_circular_orbit_widens_the_simulated_cavity_by_its_radius`: on the simulated stock (0.05 cell), the cavity floor reaches electrode + gap + radius on ±X and ±Y, and the next column out stands untouched. The same burn without the orbit stops one radius short. The furthest move is the radius exactly.
  - `every_orbit_pattern_stays_in_its_radius_and_verifies_clean`: all three patterns stay inside the radius with chords only, and `simulate_document` finds 0 gouge cells in the orbit-sized cavity.
  - `an_orbit_wider_than_the_parts_cavity_is_convicted_by_the_stock_sim`
  - `an_unlisted_pattern_and_an_over_radius_orbit_are_refused_by_name`: also covers the unstated maximum (refused), radius == max (admitted), and the garbled-orbit door.
  - `the_orbit_round_trips_the_file_and_rides_the_mcp_params_door`: file round trip, MCP add, an over-max edit refused at generate, undo, an unlisted pattern refused, `orbit: null` back to a plunge.
- `motion::sinker_orbit` unit tests: every pattern for radii 0.0005..12 is inside its radius and closes on the centre; the chord tolerance holds and the axis directions are vertices; garbled numbers are refused by name.
- `sinker_burn.rs` (#541) is unchanged apart from `orbit: None` in its literals, and its golden is byte-identical.
- Gate: the full `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head `49904407` ran tools, post, sim, motion, app and ui: 3437 passed, 1 failed. The failure is `coarse_laws::every_kind_is_either_judged_or_refused_for_a_stated_reason_on_a_reduced_model` ("SinkerBurn is judged while a tolerance is left"). It is **pre-existing on the #1131 base**: I reproduced it on the base tree without this commit. `fidelity_law.rs` refuses `Section::Sinker`, but the test's `refused` list has no `SinkerBurn`. This PR touches neither file. It belongs to #1131.
- The sinker suites (`sinker_burn`, `sinker_orbit`), `edm_machine`, `edm_conditions`, `golden_cl` and `project_roundtrip` are green. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- **Not exercised on a real EDM control.** The fixtures are synthetic: an invented condition, invented orbit words and an invented 0.5 mm maximum.
- Posting waits on #542 (#1141). That post refuses arcs, and how it treats the lateral orbit chords has not been checked here. The post script is untouched.
- The stock view / playback (field eye) still refuses an electrode by name (#541), so the orbit is judged by the program verdict's column engine only.
- The minimal sinker page gains orbit rows; #548's full pages (PR #1165) will need them carried over.
- Interaction with #543's undersize (PR #1136) and #546's wear compensation was not exercised. Both touch the same op, and whichever merges second may need a small merge.

Changelog: Sinker Burn orbits (circular, vector, planetary) at the burn floor, expanded into explicit moves the stock sim verifies; a pattern the machine does not list, or a radius past its stated maximum, is refused by name (#544, PR #1166)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #544

title: feat(edm): wire EDM constant taper - posed moves, leaning-kerf verify, max-angle and U/V refusals
body:
Stacked on #1144 (on #1139, #1123, #560, #551). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

Expected merges: #539 (tabs) and #540 (no-core) are worked on the same base and will likely touch `WireContourOp`, `WireParams`, the DTO and `wire_page.rs` - both sides add fields, keep both. #1147 / #1150 are stacked nearby.

## What changed

A constant wire taper (#290 D2, D5, D7), as the move pose:

- **Op**: `WireContourOp.taper_deg` (signed degrees; 0 = vertical, positive widens the profile downward from the top plane). The DTO omits it at 0, the stamp digests it only when non-zero, so every existing file, stamp, CL and NC is unchanged. The Geometry tab has a Taper angle field.
- **Generator** (`motion::wire_edm::taper`): the profile and every #532 law are held on the top plane at the kerf measured across the leaning wire (`k / cos a`). Each lower-plane vertex is moved `H tan a` along the mitre, so each side's face is planar at exactly the angle. Each move's pose is the wire's direction toward the upper guide. The wire stands upright at the start hole. Refused by name: no `edm.max_taper_deg`, an angle (or a corner's lean) above it (naming the op and the angle), a side the lean folds over, a corner too sharp to lean.
- **Verify** (`sim::verify::wire`): `WireJob.taper` lifts #534's posed-move refusal only for a cut that states a taper. At every judged height the wire's section is `to + t (z - z0)`. The kerf's reach toward the product is `k sqrt(1 + (t.u)^2)` (the leaning kerf's elliptical section). The slug is judged per height. So a gouge at any height blocks the post.
- **Machine check** (`machine::wire_edm`): every pose is judged against the max taper, the guide planes (`edm.lower_guide_z` / `upper_guide_z`, which must hold the programmed plane), and the U/V offset against the U and V strokes. Missing guide planes or a missing U/V axis are refused by name. The lower guide's X/Y is also checked against X/Y travel.
- **Post**: `posting_wire` turns each leaning move into the lower guide's X Y plus `PARAM WireU`/`WireV` (the upper guide's offset), computed from the pose and the guide planes. `wire-iso.cps` writes `edm.codes.taper_on` before the first leaning move, `uv` (a template with `{u}` `{v}`) on each one, and `taper_off` once the wire is upright, before the wire cut. A missing code refuses by name. The angle-word form is not offered (see the decision record).
- Fixture `wire-iso-fixture.mch` now states guide planes, a 15 degree maximum, U/V strokes and synthetic taper codes. `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` lists the new params. The decision record is `docs/decisions/536-wire-taper.md`.

## Sources

Plane trigonometry only (the section of a leaning cylinder, the polygon mitre) over #290's D2/D5/D7. ISO 6983 U/V as secondary axes parallel to X/Y. No vendor material.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/wire_taper.rs` (new):
  - `a_tapered_punch_posts_its_golden_and_its_cl_shows_the_poses`: goldens `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_taper_punch.nc` and `tests/golden/wire_taper_punch.cl`; the wire laws are clean.
  - `a_zero_taper_is_the_vertical_golden_byte_for_byte`: checked against the existing `wire_contour_punch.nc`, on the extended fixture.
  - `a_taper_past_the_machines_maximum_is_refused_by_name`: 30 degrees on a 15 degree machine, plus an unstated maximum.
  - `a_uv_offset_past_the_stroke_or_the_guides_is_refused_by_name`: U stroke, guides' reach, no U axis, no guide planes.
  - `a_taper_whose_lower_edge_gouges_the_part_blocks_the_post`
- `motion` unit test `a_taper_leans_every_side_by_its_angle_and_zero_is_the_vertical_cut`
- The existing wire suites (wire_post, wire_verify, wire_contour, golden_cl, sim wire tests), the quick gate and clippy `-D warnings` on motion/sim/app/ui: clean. `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/534-wire-verify` on the final head e34cf882: sim, motion, app (incl. wire_taper, wire_post, wire_verify, wire_contour, golden_cl, edm_*) and ui suites all ok (12.1 min, 0 failed).

## Not exercised

- Not run on a real EDM control (D10). The fixture's taper codes are invented.
- Angle-word taper dialects and arcs under taper (refused).
- A die with sharp inside corners under taper: the corner law refuses it as for a vertical cut.
- No snapshot PNGs changed.

MCP: the Wire Contour's DTO carries `taper_deg` (optional), so the existing op tools take it with no new command.

Changelog: Wire EDM: constant taper on the Wire Contour - posed moves, leaning-kerf verification at every height, max-angle / guide / U-V stroke refusals, and UV taper words from the machine's edm.codes (#536)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #536

title: feat(edm): wire no-core burnout - a pocket burnt out by offset rings, no core left
body:
Stacked on #1144 (on #1139, #1123, #560, #551). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

Wire EDM no-core burnout (#540, part of #290): a Wire Contour with a burnout clearance burns a closed pocket's whole interior away, so no core is left to drop.

- **motion** `wire_edm/burnout.rs` (new): `wire_burnout` - offset rings of the pocket from the stated wall clearance inward, 0.9 x the kerf offset apart, cut innermost first from one threading at the start hole (straight lead in, straight links ring to ring, straight lead back). Refused by name: clearance below the kerf offset (`clearance_door`, shared with the command door), no start hole, a start hole outside the clearance, the punch side, a pocket too small, a ring pattern that splits into islands. The kerf certificate runs with the clearance; the **no-core law** sweeps the kerf along the whole path out of the pocket (plus a wall ring) and refuses any piece not joined to the wall, by connectivity. At clearance = kerf offset the outer ring is the finished wall and the #532 corner minimum applies.
- **sim** `verify::wire`: `WireJob.burnout` - the slug law reads a burnout as "must free nothing"; any freed piece is `WireFinding::Core`, blocking the post. Kerf and threading laws unchanged, so a ring that burns a wall blocks the post as a gouge.
- **app**: `WireContourOp.burnout: Option<f64>` (seed `None`); `condition_of` refuses a clearance below the condition's kerf (CreateOperation and EditOperationParams, undoable); `generate_wire` branches; the stamp writes it only when set; `wire_verify` passes the flag. File mirror key `burnout_clearance` (absent = contour) - the MCP `edit_operation` params door patches that mirror, so it carries the field with no new tool.
- **ui** `wire_page.rs`: Passes tab - "Burn out the pocket (no core)" and "Wall clearance".
- **post**: no change - the burnout is one continuous threaded cut, so wire-iso.cps posts one thread / condition / comp-off before it and one cut / tip disposal after.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/540-wire-no-core.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/burnout_tests.rs`: `a_pocket_burns_out_with_no_core_left` (independent connectivity check: every piece the kerf leaves touches a wall), `a_clearance_below_the_kerf_is_refused_by_name`, `a_missing_or_misplaced_start_hole_and_a_punch_are_refused_by_name`, `a_pattern_that_cannot_reach_every_point_is_refused_by_name` (neck split; a single-ring path leaves a core), `at_the_kerf_offset_the_outer_ring_is_the_wall`.
- `crates/sim/src/verify/wire/tests.rs`: `a_burnout_frees_nothing_and_a_core_is_refused`.
- `crates/app/tests/wire_burnout.rs`: `the_burnout_posts_its_golden_with_no_slug` (new golden `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_burnout_pocket.nc`, through the gate with #534's laws), `a_clearance_below_the_kerf_is_refused_and_the_field_is_undoable` (command door, edit door, undo, file round trip), `a_burnout_pass_that_gouges_a_wall_blocks_the_post`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/534-wire-verify` green on the final head (sim, motion, app, ui suites); wire_post / wire_verify / wire_contour / wire_burnout by hand green; existing goldens byte-identical (wire_contour_punch.nc untouched, all app suites pass); clippy `-D warnings` on motion, sim, app, ui clean.

## Not exercised

- A real EDM control (D10): the golden is on the synthetic fixture with invented `FX-...` codes.
- An MCP round trip through the server (the door is the file mirror, tested by save/reopen).
- Pockets with islands, or a raster/spiral pattern (refused / not offered; see the decision record).

## Expected merges

Additive, but these edit the same lines: #539 (tabs) and #1150 (skims) both likely add fields to `WireContourOp` / `WireContourDto` / the stamp arm / `wire_page.rs` destructure / `WireJob` - keep both sides. #1150 also edits `posting_wire.rs` (untouched here).

Fixes #540

title: fix(post): doosan-dnm index writes A only for a stated A rotary
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main 7e3c75f9, which includes #1092).

## What changed
- `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`, non-RTCP indexing path in `tilt()` only: the A word is now written through #1092's `angleWord("A", ...)`, and `missingLetter` runs first. A turning letter the machine does not state is refused by name ("indexed move commands A - the machine states no A rotary"), and no word is posted. A stated C that turns is refused by name too ("indexed move commands C - this dialect's indexing path writes only an A rotary"). Before this change that path dropped C silently.
- On a machine that states A, the output is byte-identical: `angleWord` is `w()`, which is `"A" + fu(v)` for the finite angle `tilt()` already requires.
- Other direct rotary-letter writers: there are none left. Doosan's probe macro `ax + fu(pos)` writes only X/Y/Z, and fanuc.cps's non-RTCP path refuses every tilt.
- The edit stays inside the indexing block, so it merges additively with the open doosan-dnm PRs #961, #981 and #1034 (coolant, units and probe coolant, in other sections).
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1155-doosan-index-a-word.md`.

## How tested
- Pinning test `doosan_dnm_post::doosan_dnm_index_names_only_a_stated_rotary` (app). It checks three things. An A index on a machine with no rotaries is refused by name, with no A word. A turning C on millturn.mch (states C, non-RTCP) is refused by name, with no C word. On the shipped doosan-dnm.mch the motion lines are exactly `M11 / G00 X0 Y0 Z10 A90 / M10 / G01 X50 Y0 Z-1 F400`. I confirmed it fails on the upstream script: no warning, and the A word was posted.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green. It ran only the changed test, because .cps is not gate-mapped.
- By hand: every `camcraft-post` suite passed (all `script_*`, recorded_streams, cycle_hop, post_engine, vendor_mch_cli). These app suites passed: doosan_dnm_post 9, fanuc_post 12, fourth_axis_pose 9, conformance 6, tilt 8, rotary_verify 9, probe_spindle_stop 2, post_unit_word 5, recorded_post_streams 2.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test doosan_dnm_post -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No golden moved.

## Not exercised
- No real Doosan control was used.
- C indexing on a C table is refused for now, not implemented.

Changelog: doosan-dnm post refuses by name an indexed move that turns a rotary the machine does not state (or a turning C, which the indexing path never wrote) instead of posting an A word the control lacks or silently dropping C (#1155)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1155

title: feat(edm): wire tabs and the tab cut-off - the slug held until it is freed, an unheld slug refused
body:
Stacked on #1144 (on #1139, #1123, #560, #551). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

Expected merges: other open work on the same stack touches the same files additively - #538 (skim passes, on #1139) and the #1147 (open runs) integration into #1144's stack. This PR adds fields to `WireContourOp` / `WireContourDto` / `WireParams` / `WireJob` / `WireVerdict`, a new `motion::wire_edm::tabs` module and a second wire section in `posting_wire::stream`; conflicts there should be keep-both. `wire-iso.cps` is unchanged.

## What changed

Wire EDM tabs (#290 D6), off by default, and the hold law that completes #534's slug law.

- **Op parameters** (`operation::types::wire_edm`, `project::wire_edm_dto`): `tabs: { count, width, at[], cutoff_condition }` (absent = off) and `capture: bool` (absent = false). Every tab key is optional in the file, so a missing one loads and is refused by name at generation. An untabbed, uncaptured op writes no new key, so existing project files are byte-identical.
- **Generator** (`motion::wire_edm::tabs`, new): the count, width, positions and cut-off condition are each refused by name if missing. Impossible layouts are refused too: a gap (width + kerf) that does not fit on one straight side (a width at or past the side, a tab on the facets of a round), overlapping tabs, a stretch between tabs the start hole cannot reach without the kerf entering the product, and a cut-off condition whose kerf offset differs from the main cut's. The main cut leaves the tabs: each run is entered by its own lead, cut both ways, and left back along its own kerf, so the wire is never rethreaded mid-program. The cut-off follows in the same path. The path returns to the threading point once per run and once per tab, and `cutoff_split` reads the cut-off's start from that.
- **Verify** (`sim::verify::wire`): `WireJob.cutoff_from` / `capture`. For a tabbed cut, the main cut must free nothing (`TabsDoNotHold`), and the whole path must free the stated piece. An untabbed cut whose slug drops is refused (`Unsupported`) unless a capture is stated. `WireVerdict.held` / `captured` feed the report line ("holds its slug by tabs through the main cut; the tab cut-off frees ..." / "... into the stated capture").
- **Post** (`posting_wire`): a tabbed cut streams two sections. The main cut ends at a program stop (M00, so the operator secures the slug), then "<op> tab cut-off" runs with its own `EdmCondition`. The post script is not changed.
- **Stamp**: the tabs and the cut-off condition's wire and gap are digested only when tabs are on, so no existing stamp moves.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/539-wire-tabs.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/wire_tabs.rs` (new):
  - `a_die_with_two_tabs_holds_its_slug_until_the_cut_off`: a die with two tabs. The main cut never crosses a gap, the cut-off crosses each gap once each way, the gate passes with the "held by tabs" line, and the program has the main condition, then an M00, then the cut-off condition. **New NC golden** `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_contour_die_tabs.nc` on the synthetic fixture, with an invented second condition `C120`.
  - `an_unheld_slug_is_refused_and_a_capture_passes_it`: the same die with tabs off and no capture is refused by name ("drops unsupported"). With `capture` it passes.
  - `missing_or_impossible_tab_parameters_are_refused_by_name`: 13 refusals, each by name.
- `sim::verify::wire::hold_tests` (new): an unheld slug refused or captured; tabs hold, then the cut-off frees; a closing main cut reads "the tabs do not hold it".
- `project::wire_edm_dto::tests::the_tab_keys_round_trip_and_are_absent_when_off`.
- Existing goldens are byte-identical: `wire_contour_punch.nc`, `wire_contour_die.cl`, `wire_contour_punch.cl`. `wire_post` / `wire_verify` fixtures now state `capture: true`, and their line assertions take the new " into the stated capture" tail.
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/534-wire-verify`: green on dc3a06f1 (sim, motion, app, ui suites; 0 failed, 13.6 min). By hand: app `wire_tabs`, `wire_post`, `wire_verify`, `wire_contour`, `golden_cl`, `edm_machine`, `edm_conditions`; motion `--lib wire_edm`; sim `--lib wire`. Clippy `-D warnings` on motion, sim, app and ui (all targets) is clean.

## Not exercised

- Not run on a real EDM control (#290 D10). The codes and conditions are synthetic.
- No UI fields for tabs or capture (the op page is #535's). They are reachable through the project file and the MCP parameter patch (DTO).
- Tabs on arc moves: the wire path has none today. A cut-off condition with another kerf offset is refused, not stepped.

Changelog: Wire EDM: tabs (count, width, positions, cut-off condition - all stated, none defaulted) hold the slug through the main cut and a tab cut-off section frees it; an untabbed cut whose slug would drop is refused unless a capture is stated (#539)

Effort: high

Fixes #539
