title: feat(edm): sinker electrode wear compensation in Z
body:
**Stacked on #1131** (#541 sinker burn to depth, branch `issue/541-sinker-burn-depth`), which is itself stacked on #560 (#531 EDM condition table), stacked on #551 (#530 EDM machine kinds). The chain is #551 -> #560 -> #1131 -> this PR. Until those merge, their commits show here; this PR adds one commit on top of #1131's head. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
- **A wear rate per condition.** `edm.conditions[]` gains an optional `wear`: the electrode's axial wear rate, as mm of electrode lost per mm burned (dimensionless, not unit-scaled). `parse_mch` (so `LoadMachine` and the project reader) and `Edm::is_sane` refuse a rate that is not a finite ratio in [0, 1), by name ("... is not an axial wear rate ..."). No rate ships with any machine; rates are user data (#290 D4).
- **A measured wear and a layer step on the op.** `SinkerBurnOp` gains `layer`, `wear_lost` and `wear_over`. A wear measured between burns (length lost over depth burned) wins over the condition's rate. With neither stated, the burn is **not compensated**: the path note and the op page say `electrode wear: not compensated (no wear rate stated)`. `CreateOperation` / `EditOperationParams` (and the project reader) refuse a measured rate of 1 or more, a half-stated or non-finite measurement, and a non-positive layer step, all by name, through a new `OpParams::named_refusal` door that runs ahead of the generic "not usable".
- **Compensation in Z** (`crates/motion/src/sinker_wear.rs`, `burn_compensated`). The burn is fed in layers. Each layer's tip is programmed `rate * d` deeper, where `d` is how far that layer's nominal floor lies below the work top. Every move is re-checked against the bound: the stated floor plus the gap, minus `rate` times the stated depth. A move past it is refused as over-deep, by name. All of #541's refusals still apply. The electrode-length law now reads the deeper, compensated tip. With no rate and no layer step, the moves are exactly #541's (pinned).
- **The stock sim judges the worn electrode.** `plan_program` maps each programmed tip back to where the worn electrode burns (`worn_tip`, the exact inverse of the compensation). A compensated burn to the cavity's own floor therefore reads 0 gouge cells, and a nominal floor past the model is still convicted.
- **Staleness.** The op digest adds the layer step and the measured wear, and the stamp adds the condition's rate, each only when stated. Existing digests do not change.
- **File, MCP, UI.** The three op keys are additive and optional: older files load unchanged and write no new keys. MCP drives them through the existing params JSON door (`add_operation` / `edit_operation`). No new command or tool was needed, and a test pins this. The Sinker Burn page's Passes tab gains Layer step, Measured wear and Measured over, plus the compensation status line.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/546-sinker-wear-comp.md`.

## How tested
- New suite `crates/app/tests/sinker_wear.rs`:
  - `sinker_wear_layers_match_golden`: golden `crates/app/tests/golden/sinker_wear_layers.cl`. I read it: three 2 mm layers at rate 0.02, gap 0.05, with tips at Z 18.010, 15.970 and 13.930 (that is 18.05 - 0.04, 16.05 - 0.08 and 14.05 - 0.12).
  - `a_condition_wear_rate_deepens_each_layer_and_the_sim_judges_it_clean`
  - `a_missing_wear_rate_shows_not_compensated`
  - `a_bad_wear_rate_is_refused_by_name`: machine file and op commands.
  - `a_measured_wear_wins_over_the_condition_and_round_trips_the_file`: includes an older file with no new keys.
  - `the_wear_fields_ride_the_mcp_params_door`
- Unit tests in `motion::sinker_wear`: wear off equals the plain burn, per-layer deepening plus its inverse, and refusals of the rate, step and reach.
- `crates/app/tests/sinker_burn.rs`: the op literal gains the three new `None` fields; no assertion changed.
- Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on this head (b0e121ce), 24.3 min. The tools, post, sim, motion and ui suites pass. In the app suites, every binary passes except one test, and that test **fails on #1131's own head too**: I ran it alone on `origin/issue/541-sinker-burn-depth`, and this PR doesn't change it:
  - `coarse_laws::every_kind_is_either_judged_or_refused_for_a_stated_reason_on_a_reduced_model`: "SinkerBurn is judged while a tolerance is left". The fidelity law refuses a Sinker Burn on a reduced-fidelity model, but the test expects it to be judged.
  The fix belongs on #1131. The sinker_burn, sinker_wear, edm_machine, edm_conditions, golden_cl and project_roundtrip suites pass. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
- **Not exercised on a real EDM control** (#290 D10). The conditions and wear rates are synthetic fixtures.
- Wear is axial only; corner and side wear are not modelled. No orbit (#544), no multi-electrode undersize logic (#543), and no sinker post (#542). Layers are a stepped plunge with no retract between them.
- The field-arm stock view still refuses an electrode program (as in #541).

Changelog: Sinker EDM: electrode wear compensation in Z - a stated axial wear rate (per condition in the machine file, or measured on the op) deepens each burn layer by the wear it states, bounded and refused by name past it; with no rate the burn says "not compensated" (#546)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #546

title: feat(sinker): generate an electrode from a cavity's picked faces
body:
Stacked on #1136 (→ #1131 → #560 → #551). Fork synced at v0.18.0. Until those merge, this PR's diff against `main` includes theirs; its own change is the last commit.

## What changed

A sinker EDM electrode is generated from the picked faces of a part's cavity - its level floor and every vertical wall standing on it - and added to the document as #541's electrode tool, in one undo step.

- **`motion::sinker_cavity::cavity_of`** (pure, no world) reads a face set as one cavity. Each face is checked on its own (finite, in range, planar, non-zero area, closed boundary), classed by its outward normal, and the walls are matched to the floor's outer ring edge by edge: a wall stands on a floor edge when one of its edges lies on it at floor height and its normal points into the floor. Every floor edge must be covered end to end.
- **`motion::sinker_electrode::derive`** offsets the outline inward by `undersize + orbit` with the geometry crate's polygon offset (`geo2d::Region::offset_sharp`, Clipper2) and extends the electrode a stated stub above the cavity's mouth. The sizes are the arithmetic `cavity - 2 x inset`; the offset polygon must agree within 10 nm or the derivation refuses.
- **`standing_in`** clips the part's facets against the cavity's column above the floor: a boss, a rib or an overhang in the electrode's way refuses the electrode with the spot.
- **`operation::sinker_faces`** resolves the picks (the one pick rule, #692; outward normals by the facets' winding) and reads a condition's undersize by id through #531's door.
- **`commands::ElectrodeFromFaces`** is the undoable command (its write and inverse are `AddTool`'s). **MCP: `electrode_from_faces`** runs it; its reply carries a `burn` object that `add_operation`'s `params` takes as is.

## Rectangular cavities only, for now

The stock sim burns an electrode with #541's box atom: an axis-aligned rectangular face. So only a cavity whose outline is an axis-aligned rectangle yields an electrode. A rounded corner, a rotated rectangle, an L, a curved wall, a drafted wall or a stepped floor is refused by name, and the refusal names the follow-up: **#1152** (a sim atom and a tool record for an electrode body). The offset outline is already computed and carried on the result for it.

Orbit (#544) is not merged: an optional orbit radius is accepted and taken off the electrode, and the tool's answer says so. Until #544 changes #543's size law, a Sinker Burn judges such an electrode without its orbit.

## Refusals, each by name

Empty face set · a face with a non-finite or out-of-range coordinate · a zero-area or degenerate face · an open loop (a boundary that does not close) · a curved (welded) or non-planar wall · a leaning (drafted) wall or tilted floor · a face looking down · no floor · two floors (faces from different cavities, or a stepped cavity) · only the floor · a wall of another cavity (stands on none of the floor's edges, reaches below it, or faces away) · walls that do not close around the floor · a self-intersecting outline · a non-rectangular cavity (#1152) · an inset that consumes the cavity · a garbled undersize, orbit, stub or pickup · picks on different models, on no part, a stale id, a chain or a vertex · an open, inside-out or non-manifold body · the part standing in the cavity's column · a taken or reserved tool name.

## How tested

Run one by one (`cargo test -p <crate> ... -- --exact` style), debug:

- `camcraft-motion --lib sinker_electrode` (7 tests): `a_rectangular_cavitys_faces_yield_its_electrode`, `a_cavity_reads_whatever_the_winding_split_or_order`, `every_degenerate_face_set_is_refused_by_its_own_name`, `a_cavity_the_box_atom_cannot_burn_is_refused_by_name`, `the_model_standing_in_the_cavitys_column_is_found`, and the seeded fuzz: `fuzz_a_damaged_cavity_is_always_refused_by_name_never_a_panic` (6000 sound cavities, each then damaged one of 20 named ways and required to refuse by that name) and `fuzz_garbage_faces_never_panic_and_never_answer_a_nonsense_electrode` (20000 garbage face sets with NaN, infinities, `f64::MAX`, denormals).
- `camcraft-app --test sinker_electrode` (8 tests): `a_pockets_faces_yield_an_electrode_that_burns_that_pocket_in_the_sim` (the generated rough leaves stock and gouges nothing, the generated finish leaves the program verdict clean), `the_verdict_convicts_the_generated_electrode_burned_off_its_point` (the contrast: 1 mm off centre gouges), `the_electrode_is_one_undo_step_and_its_name_is_checked`, `the_condition_door_reads_the_undersize_or_refuses_by_name`, `a_face_set_that_is_no_single_cavity_is_refused_by_name`, `faces_from_different_cavities_are_refused_by_name`, `a_boss_in_the_cavity_is_in_the_electrodes_way`, `a_rounded_pocket_is_refused_by_name_until_the_sim_burns_a_body`.
- `camcraft-app --test sinker_electrode_mcp`: `the_electrode_is_generated_and_burned_over_mcp_with_the_gui_commands`.

The fuzz found one hole while this was written: a denormal stub vanished into the depth, giving an electrode no longer than its cavity. The stub now has a floor (1 micron) and the length is checked against the depth.

Gate (local, debug, head `c93678aa`):
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-motion --lib`: 205 passed, 0 failed, 1 ignored.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test sinker_electrode --test sinker_electrode_mcp --test sinker_burn --test sinker_undersize --test mcp --test mcp_pick --test mcp_pockets --test mcp_order --test commands_undo --test tool_law --test pocket_recognition --test edm_conditions --test edm_machine`: 109 passed, 0 failed.

## What was not exercised

- **Not exercised on a real EDM control.** Synthetic conditions and parts built in code only (#290 D10).
- No GUI entry: the sinker pages are #548's; the command is what its button will run.
- The full quick-gate plan (every suite whose gate map names `app::commands` / `app::operation` / `app::mcp`, about 190 app binaries and 7 ui suites) was not run; the change is additive (new modules, one appended tool-table row, no existing function edited), and the suites named above were run instead.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill's tool table is a process file and is not touched here (`tools/list` is the live registry).
- STEP-imported parts: the fixtures are meshes built in code. A wall that is off vertical by more than a millionth is refused as leaning.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/547-electrode-from-faces.md`.

Changelog: Sinker EDM: an electrode is generated from the picked faces of a part's cavity (its floor and walls), offset inward by the undersize and extended to a holder stub - `ElectrodeFromFaces`, MCP `electrode_from_faces`; rectangular cavities only, every other face set refused by name (#547)

Effort: max (not escalated)

Fixes #547

title: fix(app): the program sim, setup sheet, tool list and cutting data know a tool-less wire cut
body:
**Stacked on #1123** (issue #532, the Wire Contour op; itself on #560, #551). Until those merge, this PR's diff also shows their commits. The commit for this issue is the last one on the branch. Retarget or merge after #1123.

Fork synced at v0.18.0 (process files at PROCESS_VERSION 17).

## What changed

A Wire Contour mounts no library tool (#532), so its `Operation::tool` is the empty word. Each reader changed below checks `KindInfo::mounts_tool()` and nothing else: no kind matches, no "is the name empty" checks. A milling op whose tool was deleted still mounts a tool, so it is refused or listed exactly as before. Each surface has a pinning test for that too.

| Surface | Before | Now |
|---|---|---|
| Program stock sim (`stock_sim.rs` plan walk, new `stock_sim_wire.rs`) | `Die1: tool  is not in the library` | `plan_program` leaves the wire cut out of the plan, the same way the probe and torch arms do. `simulate_document` refuses by name: `Die1: a wire cut is verified by the wire laws, not the stock sim`. The post gate shows this as its non-blocking "not judged" line, and the setup sheet's sim line says "SIM: not judged - ...". |
| Setup sheet, op row (`setup_sheet/operations.rs`) | empty TOOL cell | TOOL cell `cond C110`, and under the row `CONDITION C110  WIRE D 0.250  GAP 0.040`, read through `wire_op::condition_of` (the door generation uses). A condition the machine no longer states prints `! wire condition: <refusal>`. |
| Setup sheet, tool table (`setup_sheet/tools.rs`) | `(tool '' is no longer in the document)` | No change in this file: it reads `tool_list::for_setup`, which no longer has the row. A wire setup prints "(no tools in this setup)". |
| Tool list / export (`tool_list.rs`, `tool_list_export.rs`) | a row for tool `""` | No row. A wire EDM has no tool table. The export reads the same rows, so no change was needed in it. |
| Cutting data (`cutting.rs`, found in the audit) | `tool  is not in the library` | `a Wire Contour mounts no library tool - its cut is the machine's EDM condition, and the cutting-data table speaks for milling tools only` |

`stock_sim.rs` gets only three touches, to keep the later merge with #1140 a keep-both: the `#[path]` module line, a 3-line skip arm, and one call line. The file was already 421 lines before this PR (now 428). The new logic is in `stock_sim_wire.rs` rather than added to it.

Why refuse the verdict instead of only skipping the cut: judging the uncut stock would report rest material wherever the wire cut through, which is a wrong answer. A program that mixes a wire EDM setup with a mill setup is already refused by the carry law (two machines), so no gouge verdict is lost today. Decisions: `docs/decisions/1110-wire-tool-readers.md`.

## Audit of the other `op.tool` readers

| File | Verdict on a wire cut | Why |
|---|---|---|
| `cutting.rs` | **fixed** (above) | `suggest` looked the empty name up as a library tool. |
| `fixture_struck.rs` (`op_hits`) | fine | No tool means `Ok(vec![])` (no hits). This file is display only (it tints the struck fixture) and feeds no post. A wire cut's workholding verdicts belong to the wire laws (#534). A milling op with a lost tool is still refused at the post by `tool_gate::tool_problem_of`. |
| `fixture_carried.rs` (`carried_fixture_problems`) | fine | No tool means `tool_r = 0.0`, which is only the carry lattice's sizing radius. The fixture-in-carried-body check still runs on the carried body. |
| `operation/footprint.rs` | fine | Only the `Face` arm reads the tool. A Wire Contour takes the `_ => Some(region)` arm, so its footprint is its profile region. |
| `posting_index_swing.rs` | fine | A wire EDM states no work A axis, so `work_a` is `None` and the loop `continue`s before the tool is read. The post refuses a wire cut by name first anyway (`op_streams`, #532). |
| `tool_numbers.rs` (`clash`, `clash_per_machine`) | fine | `""` is not in `numbers()`, so it is skipped ("not a tool: the post names that refusal itself"). An empty name can never clash with a real tool. |
| `sim_tool_body.rs`, `rest/ahead.rs` (outside the issue's list, read while auditing) | fine | No tool means `Ok(None)` (nothing to spin) and no rest mask, the same as a never-cutting op. |

## Tests

New suite `crates/app/tests/wire_readers.rs`. Its gate map covers app::stock_sim, app::setup_sheet, app::tool_list, app::tool_list_export, app::cutting and app::posting_sim. It has 7 tests, and each surface gets one wire pin and one milling-missing-tool pin:

- `the_program_sim_answers_a_wire_cut_by_name` (also covers `verification_report().not_judged` and `setup_sheet::simulate_verdict`)
- `a_milling_op_with_a_missing_tool_is_still_refused_by_the_program_sim`
- `the_setup_sheet_shows_the_wire_condition_and_no_missing_tool`
- `the_setup_sheet_still_says_a_milling_tool_is_gone`
- `the_tool_list_and_its_export_hold_no_row_for_a_wire_cut`
- `the_tool_list_keeps_a_row_for_a_lost_milling_tool`
- `the_cutting_data_table_says_why_it_cannot_speak_for_a_wire_cut` (also checks that the milling refusal text is unchanged)

Gate: the full `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the final head `d3c517cc` was green in 17.3 min, with 0 failed across post, motion, app and ui (2918 passed, 24 ignored). The stack's diff pulls in the shared CL goldens, so nearly every app suite ran, setup_sheet, tool_list, stock_sim_document, sim, cutting_data, wire_contour, edm_conditions, edm_machine, golden_cl and wire_readers among them. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` was clean.

## Not exercised

- The UI: the feeds page would now show the cutting-data refusal text for a wire cut. Whether a wire op shows that page at all is #535's.
- The stock view and the MCP render overlay on a wire document. They walk `plan_program`, which now skips the cut, but no test drives them on a wire document.
- A program mixing wire and mill setups: the carry law refuses it before this code is reached.
- No snapshot PNGs, post scripts, verification laws, op/machine pages or contour-generator changes.

Changelog: The program stock sim, setup sheet, tool list and cutting data handle a Wire Contour (no library tool): the sim refuses by name, the sheet shows the EDM condition, wire diameter and gap, and the tool list has no empty row (#1110)

Effort: high (not escalated)

Fixes #1110

title: docs(mcp): camcraft-mcp skill lists set_raw_stock_only; PROCESS_VERSION 20
body:
Adds the `set_raw_stock_only` row to the stock section of `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`, after `set_stock`, and bumps `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` to 20 (main's 19 was taken by #965). Merges main. Files only, no build.

Row as added:

> `set_raw_stock_only { "on": boolean }`: For a stock made from a model (`set_stock` `from_model`), say whether that source model is raw stock only - a casting or blank you cut into, not the finished part. Default off: the model is judged like every model. On: the gouge verdict leaves it out. One undo step. Refused by name when there is no stock yet ("set the stock first"), when the stock is not made from a model, or when the source model has no geometry. The mark holds only while the model is still the stock's source and its geometry and placement (position and rotation) are unchanged, so moving or turning the model voids it; otherwise it is ignored and the post says so by name. An operation that machines the model (as its source or in a boundary pick) puts it back in the verdict. If the mark leaves nothing to judge, the post is refused by name.

Where each fact was read (on main):

- Name, parameter `on` (boolean, required), default off, one undo step: `crates/app/src/mcp/setup_tools.rs:28` (registration in `TOOLS`, aggregated by `mcp/tools.rs`), `:254-256` (schema), `:259-264` (handler: `env.history.execute`).
- Refusals: `crates/app/src/commands/stock_source_only.rs:34` ("no stock '...' - set the stock first"), `:47` (source model not in the document or no geometry), and the not-from-a-model refusal in `new` (same file, ~line 56).
- Placement in the validity check: `crates/app/src/stock_print.rs:1-6` (fingerprint hashes local facets then `Location`: position and rotation).
- Mark holds only while source and geometry match, otherwise ignored with a named note: `crates/app/src/stock_source.rs:7-16` (module doc), `:113-126` (`void_note`).

title: feat(edm): Wire Contour skim passes - per-pass condition, offset and direction
body:
Stacked on #1139 (on #1123, #560, #551). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

Expected merges: retarget to `main` after #1139 merges. #1143 (Wire UI, also on #1139) touches `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wire_page.rs`; this PR changes one line there (the op destructure gains `..`), so a trivial conflict at most. #534 (verify) and #1109 (open profile) on #1123 are not touched.

## What changed

The Wire Contour gains skim passes: a rough pass, then N skims, each naming its own machine condition (and so its own offset, wire radius + that condition's gap), with an optional direction reversal per skim.

- `operation::WireContourOp.skims: Vec<WireSkim { condition, reverse }>`; file / MCP JSON `skims: [{ condition, reverse? }]`, absent when empty (rough-only files and goldens unchanged). Edits ride `EditOperationParams` (undoable) and the existing MCP params door.
- Command door (`wire_op::condition_of`): every skim's condition resolved through #531's door, refused by name when it names none or the machine does not state it; then `motion::wire_edm::check_passes`: a pass nearer the profile than the finishing (last) pass ("would cut past the finished profile", rough included), a skim farther out than the pass before it ("would cut only air"), a skim condition with another wire diameter ("one threading cuts every pass with one wire").
- Generator: `motion::wire_edm::wire_passes` (new `skims.rs`) runs #532's single-pass generator per pass at its own offset, every law at that offset; each pass leads in from the threading point and back; a reversed skim walks clockwise. No skims is `wire_contour` exactly.
- Stamp digests each skim's condition numbers and direction (writes nothing for no skims - no stored stamp moves).
- Post stream (`posting_wire`): a mid-section `PARAM EdmCondition <skim id>` before each skim's first move (after each return to the threading point); a path that does not return once per pass is refused.
- `wire-iso.cps`: a condition that arrives with the wire threaded is the next skim's - `(SKIM n)`, the condition select and `comp_off` again at its first move; the wire stays threaded.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/538-wire-skims.md`.

## How tested

- New golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_contour_punch_skims.nc` (rough C110 + skim S21 + reversed skim S31 on #533's synthetic fixture): three distinct offsets (X-20.165 / -20.145 / -20.135), three condition selects, one thread, one cut.
- `wire_post`: `a_rough_and_two_skims_post_three_offsets_and_condition_selects`, `no_skims_is_the_rough_program_and_json_unchanged`, `skims_edit_undo_and_round_trip`, `each_skim_refusal_is_named_at_the_door`; the existing `the_punch_contour_posts_its_golden_through_the_gate` passes with #533's golden unchanged (no golden moved).
- `camcraft-motion` unit: `skims_cut_their_own_offsets_and_none_is_the_single_pass`, `skim_laws_refuse_by_name`.
- `wire_contour` suite (all 7) green; `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/533-wire-iso-post` on head 0e96ca1c: motion, app (every suite - the new golden is shared input) and ui suites, 0 failed (12.4 min). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- No real EDM control (D10): the fixture's conditions and codes are synthetic (three synthetic conditions S21, S31, W20 added to it).
- A punch drops after its rough unless held - tabs are #539; the program does not claim a hold.
- No UI editor for the skim list yet: follow-up #1148 (after #535 / #1143).

Effort: high (no escalation).

title: feat(edm): wire contour cuts an open run from the stock's edge
body:
Stacked on #1144 (on #1139, #1123, #560, #551) - this diff shows their commits until they merge; merge #551, #560, #1123, #1139, #1144 first. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

The Wire Contour op (#532) now cuts **one open run entered from the stock's edge** - a cut-off line, a slot, a relief - besides one closed profile (part of #290).

- **Kerf side stated, never inferred:** `side` gains `left` / `right` (of the run's travel = its point order) beside `die` / `punch`. Die/punch on an open run is refused by name ("an open profile has no punch or die side; state the kerf side: left or right of the run's travel"); left/right on a closed profile likewise. Still no serde default for `side`.
- **No start hole:** both ends must reach (or pass) the stock's edge (1 um tolerance). The path is the run's one-sided parallel at wire radius + gap (mitred joins), extended along the run's own end directions until the wire stands **kerf offset + a stated `clearance`** off the stock: threaded there in the air, run out the same way at the far end (no return).
- **Refused by name:** no stock, an end that stops inside the stock (with its distance), a run that never enters the stock, a self-crossing run, one that doubles back, several runs or a run mixed with rings, an inside corner tighter than wire radius + gap (cover law, same 2 um as #532), a run-out that would cut the stock, a bad clearance.
- The kerf law and the cover law now run over an open polyline too (`laws::cover_run`, `kerf(.., given_closed, ..)`); the closed path is byte-identical (both #532 goldens unchanged).
- App: `WireContourOp.clearance` (seeded 1.0 mm; the file omits it at the seed, so closed-cut files read/write as before), `is_sane` bounds it, the generator gets the setup's stock outline (stock facets projected to XY, read only when a run is picked). The existing MCP door (`params_from_json` / the edit patch) carries `side: left|right` and `clearance` - no new MCP tool (#1108 is the dedicated one).
- UI: the minimal wire page offers the four sides and a "Run-out clearance" row (#535 owns the real page).

Decisions: `docs/decisions/1109-wire-open-profile.md` (side in one field, travel = point order, no centred kerf yet, no blind runs - a run ending inside the material is a closed cut from a start hole, run-out shape, clearance seed).

## Readings

Plate 100 x 50, synthetic condition C110 (wire 0.25, gap 0.04, offset 0.165), clearance 1.0. Cut-off at x = 60, kerf right: every wire point at x = 60.165 (1e-9); threaded at Y-1.165, run out at Y51.165. Left: x = 59.835 - the two stand apart by the 0.33 kerf. A U slot from the edge (2 mm corners, kerf left, inside the U): every ride point exactly 0.165 off the run (1e-6) and inside the slot; the same U with sharp corners is refused ("minimum inside radius is 0.1650 mm") on the left and cut (mitred) on the right.

## Integration with #1144 (wire-iso post #1139 + wire verify #534)

`issue/534-wire-verify` is merged into this branch (`5c49075a`, no textual conflicts) and the open run is joined to both (`0d82d2e7`):

- **Verify** (`sim::verify::wire`): a third side `CutSide::Open` for `left|right`. The kerf law judges the run, run-in and run-out included, against the part at every judged height, so an open run whose kerf touches the part is a gouge and blocks the post. The start-hole/threading and slug laws are skipped, and the report line says so: "Cutoff1 open run (right of travel): kerf judged; start-hole and slug laws not applied (...)". Both ends, where the wire is threaded and cut, must stand clear of the stock by the kerf offset at every height (`OpenEndInStock`). The app gate maps `left|right` to `Open` and no longer refuses an open run for having no start hole.
- **Post** (`wire-iso.cps`): it threads at the path's first point (the run-in, in the air) and cuts the wire at section end after the run-out. It writes only the path's moves, so no return to the threading point exists. Without AWT the operator notes read "at the run-in point outside the stock" and "at the run-out point". The closed punch golden is byte-identical.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1109-wire-open-profile.md` now covers how verify and the post read an open run.

## How tested

- `camcraft-motion` lib `wire_edm::open_tests` (3): `a_cut_off_across_a_plate_stands_the_kerf_offset_on_the_stated_side`, `a_slot_from_the_edge_rides_inside_at_the_kerf_offset`, `every_open_run_refusal_is_named`; #532's 5 `wire_edm::tests` unchanged and green.
- `golden_cl`: new `wire_open_cutoff_matches_golden` (`tests/golden/wire_open_cutoff.cl`); `wire_contour_die_and_punch_match_golden` unchanged - **no golden moved**.
- `camcraft-app` `wire_contour`: new `the_open_run_fields_ride_the_commands_and_the_json_door` (EditOperationParams + undo, NaN clearance refused at the door, JSON door both ways, a closed file names no clearance, left/right on the closed slug refused at generation).
- Integration: `wire_post::an_open_cutoff_posts_its_golden_and_a_gouging_one_is_refused` (new NC golden `tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_contour_open_cutoff.nc`, synthetic fixture dialect). A 60x50x12 part in a 100x50x12 bar, its x=60 top edge picked as an open chain: it generates through the commands, is judged, and posts with one G0 to the run-in at Y-1.165, cuts to Y51.165, then FX-CUT with no return. The same run with its kerf on the part's side is refused at the post (`Cutoff1: wire gouge`) and no NC is written. The punch golden is asserted byte-identical. Also `sim` `verify::wire::tests::an_open_run_is_judged_by_its_kerf_with_no_start_hole_or_slug` (clean pass with no slug and the skip said; a gouge; an end in the stock).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/534-wire-verify` on the final head `0d82d2e7`: **green**, 13.7 min (sim 3 s, motion lib 27 s, app 676 s: every suite because a shared golden changed, wire_post/wire_contour/wire_verify included; ui 115 s). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- Earlier: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/issue/532-wire-contour` on `42bee8fa`: **green** - motion lib (33 s), app (the whole suite, because a golden was added; 645 s), ui (lib and 7 suites). The first clippy run flagged one needless-range-loop in `open.rs` (fixed in `42bee8fa`); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean on the final head.

## Not exercised

- **Not exercised on a real EDM control**; the condition and the post's EDM codes are synthetic.
- The stock read in `generate.rs` is now exercised end to end by the integration test above. A slot (two edge-reaching ends on one side) is pinned only at the generator.
- The capture/tab law for the offcut a cut-off frees is not judged: no slug law runs for an open run (#539 owns tabs).
- The page's new rows were drawn only by the registry-wide tab law test.

Changelog: Wire EDM: the Wire Contour cuts an open run (a cut-off or a slot) entered from the stock's edge, with the kerf stated left or right of travel and the wire threaded and run out a stated clearance off the stock; an end inside the stock, a missing kerf side, a self-crossing run and a too-tight corner are refused by name (#1109)

Effort: high (not escalated)

Fixes #1109

title: feat(sim): wire EDM 2.5D verification - kerf, threading and slug laws block the post
body:
Stacked on #1139 (on #1123, #560, #551) - this diff shows their commits until they merge; merge #551, #560, #1123, #1139 first. Fork synced at v0.18.0. Not exercised on a real EDM control.

**Integration with #1139 (#533 wire post).** `issue/533-wire-iso-post` is merged into this branch (`8cd0aff6`), keeping both sides: `posting_wire.rs` holds #533's Wire Contour stream and this PR's wire clause, mounted once in `posting.rs` as `wire` with the clause re-exported; `wire_contour.rs` asserts the combined truth (the note points at the wire laws, and the wire cut streams with its condition). With a real wire post underneath, the verdict now stands between a judged cut and NC text: `wire_post::the_wire_laws_stand_between_the_cut_and_its_nc_text` (`3e852d68`) posts the clean punch through `wire-iso.cps` to #533's golden (unchanged, byte-identical) and refuses a die whose kerf burns the plate by name (`Die1: wire gouge: the kerf of move ...`), writing no NC file.

## What changed

Wire EDM verification of a 2-axis cut (#534, part of #290 D7). Every finding blocks the post; nothing is a warning.

**Laws** - `crates/sim/src/verify/wire/` (pure 2D, `judge(&WireJob) -> WireVerdict`):
- **Kerf law (gouge).** Each move's segment must stay at least the kerf offset (wire radius + spark gap, from the condition) from the product's section, and must not stand in it, at every judged height. The first move that breaks it is named with its depth, the spot, the height and how many moves gouge. The check uses exact point-to-segment distance, not an area threshold.
- **Threading law.** The start hole must be stated, the path must start at it, and the product must stand clear of it by the kerf offset at every height through the full stock height. Each failure is refused by name.
- **Slug law.** The kerf (the offset disc swept along the whole path, `Region::sweep`) is taken out of the material section (stock and part), and the connected pieces inside the cut's filled outline are the ones freed. A die whose freed piece holds part material ("the part drops") is refused, and so is a punch whose freed pieces hold none ("only waste drops"). A cut that frees nothing is refused too.
- **What "the part" is, by the stated side.** For a punch it is the model. For a die it is the model when the start hole stands outside it (a die plate with the opening as its hole). When the start hole stands inside the model, the model is the opening (#532's whole-model die) and the stock around it is the product.

**Gate** - `crates/app`:
- `operation/wire_verify.rs` gathers the inputs live, at the post. That is the cached path, the condition's offset, the side and start, and the part and stock sliced at both ends of the span the wire passes plus about every 2 mm between (at most 9 heights). The span covers the op's planes, the part and the stock, whichever reaches farthest.
- `posting_wire.rs` adds the wire clause to `verification_report`, beside the plasma clause. Every finding is a blocking problem. The not-judged line says the 3D stock sim did not run for the wire, and names the piece each cut frees: "Die1 frees 7xx mm² near X0 Y0 (waste)" or "Punch1 frees ... (the part)".
- A wire cut taken from the stock, or one with no path, is refused by name at the gate.
- The machine check's wire note no longer says verification is not built. It now points to the post's wire laws, and the one assertion in `wire_contour.rs` that read the old note was updated to match.

Decisions in `docs/decisions/534-wire-verify.md`. They cover: judged live at the post, the whole height the wire passes, exact distance rather than area, the product reading per side, threading clearance = the kerf offset, slug connectivity, and no capture/tab law until #539.

## How tested

- `camcraft-sim` lib, `verify::wire::tests` (5): `a_correct_punch_passes_and_drops_the_punch`, `a_correct_die_passes_whether_the_model_is_the_opening_or_the_plate`, `a_kerf_into_the_part_is_a_gouge_naming_the_move`, `a_missing_moved_or_crowded_start_hole_is_refused`, `the_slug_is_read_for_the_stated_side` (a punch stated on a die plate's hole, a die stated on a punch outline, and a die plate with no stock).
- `camcraft-app` `wire_verify` (3), through the commands and the gate: `a_correct_die_and_a_correct_punch_pass_and_name_the_piece_they_free`, `a_kerf_into_the_part_blocks_the_post_naming_the_move` (a 12 mm opening model in a 20 mm plate, so above the opening the wire burns the plate), `a_missing_start_hole_blocks_the_post`.
- `wire_contour` (7) still green, with the machine note's assertion updated.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/issue/532-wire-contour` on the final head `82bf9b54`: **green**, 4 steps and 0 failed (sim 19 s, motion 9 s, app 602 s for the whole suite list including `wire_contour` and `wire_verify`, ui 90 s).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- After merging #1139: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/533-wire-iso-post` on head `3e852d68`: **green**, 4 steps, 0 failed (sim 12 s, motion 4 s, app 522 s incl. `wire_post` 5, `wire_contour` 7, `wire_verify` 3, ui 86 s); clippy -D warnings on sim/app clean.

## Not exercised

- **Not exercised on a real EDM control.** The condition is synthetic, and nothing was cut.
- On this PR alone (without #1139) there is no wire post; the integration above is what puts the verdict in front of NC text.
- Taper (#536): the laws read straight, vertical, unposed moves and refuse anything else by name. The ruled surface between planes is not judged.
- Capture/tabs (#539, D6): a correct slug passes and is named on the report line. An unsupported slug is not refused, because no capture parameter exists yet.
- A pre-drilled start hole's diameter is not modelled (the op states a point). "Too small" means the product stands within the kerf offset of the threading point.
- Only the op's source model is judged. Another model on the same setup that stands in the wire's column is not checked.
- A selection-sourced (picked-edge) wire cut was not tested through the gate.

Changelog: Wire EDM: a Wire Contour is verified at the post in 2.5D: a kerf into the part (naming the move), a missing or crowded start hole, and a slug on the wrong side (die vs punch) or a cut that frees nothing each block the post by name, and the report names the piece each cut frees (#534)

Effort: high (not escalated)

Fixes #534

title: chore(process): PROCESS_VERSION 18 - covers the camcraft-mcp skill rows merged with #930
body:
## What
Bumps `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` from 17 to 18 (one line, nothing else).

## Why
PR #1117 took PROCESS_VERSION 17. PR #930 (merged as 49799c64) also changed a process file (`.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`: rows for `set_tool_holder` and `list_holder_library`) while the number stayed 17, because both PRs changed 16 -> 17 and git merged the identical change. AGENTS.md says the second to merge takes the next number, so forks that already synced at 17 will not pull #930's change until the number moves.

## Files only, no build
Only `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` changes. No cargo run.

## What a fork must do
Pull the process files: `git fetch upstream` then `git checkout upstream/main -- AGENTS.md .claude/agents .claude/skills .claude/PROCESS_VERSION xtask .cargo/config.toml scripts/gate.ps1 scripts/gate.sh scripts/release.ps1 scripts/collect-decisions.ps1 scripts/collect-decisions.sh`, then commit on a `process-sync` branch as `chore(process): sync process files to upstream PROCESS_VERSION 18`. The announcement and the full steps are in pinned issue #681.

title: feat(edm): generic ISO-style sinker post, every EDM code from the machine's edm.codes
body:
Stacked on #1131 → #560 → #551. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
- **`assets/posts/sinker-iso.cps`** ("Sinker EDM (ISO)", `posting::SINKER_POSTS`): a generic ISO-style sinker post. It writes only the RS-274 words itself (G0 with changed axis words, G90, the setup's work offset, `( )` comments). Every EDM-specific code comes from the machine's `edm.codes` (#290 D5): `metric` / `inch` (the unit word), `pickup` (`{tool}`), `reference` (`{offset}`, the electrode's pickup offset), `condition` (`{id}`), `depth` (the servo burn, `{z}`, optional `{f}`) and `end`. A stated orbit uses the machine's `edm.orbits[].word` (`{radius}`). **A missing code refuses the post by name** ("... states no edm.codes.depth ... - fill it from the control's manual"). A placeholder the post does not fill, or one with no value, is refused the same way. The burn posts as rapid approach, the `depth` code, rapid retract; a feed with X/Y travel, a feed up, an arc, a cycle, compensation, an rpm or a coolant ask is refused by name.
- **`edm.codes` in the machine file** (`crates/post/src/machine/edm_codes.rs`): role -> non-empty template string; a garbled value refuses the file by its role. The mirror (and the raw CLI door, through the same parser) now carries a wire/sinker machine's `kind` and `edm` section into the script; every other machine's mirror is byte-identical.
- **The serves law, in the engine** (`crates/post/src/post/machine_edm.rs`, called before `onOpen`): a script declares `serves = "sinker_edm";`. On a wire or sinker EDM, a script that does not declare that kind is refused by name before it runs, so every mill, lathe and plasma post stays refused on a sinker (and wire) EDM. A script that declares kinds is refused on any other machine, so the sinker post is refused on a mill. It holds for the app, the CLI and user `.cps` files alike. `post_serves` lists the sinker post for sinker EDMs only; `default_post_for(SinkerEdm)` is it. Wire EDM stays unserved (#533).
- **Stream PARAMs** for a Sinker Burn (`crates/app/src/posting_edm.rs`): `EdmCondition` (the op's condition id) and `ElectrodePickup` (mm). `EdmOrbit` / `EdmOrbitRadius` are documented in `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` and read by the post, ready for #544; nothing emits them yet.
- **Fixture dialect** `crates/app/tests/edm/sinker-iso-dialect.mch`: SYNTHETIC invented words (`E{id}`, `M100 H{offset}`, `M101 Z{z}`, `M150 R{radius}`), not any control's.
- Docs: `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` (the `serves` manifest key, a sinker-post section) and `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` (`edm.codes` roles). **PROCESS_VERSION 16 -> 23** (one above the highest open value, #1124's 22); it renumbers at merge.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/542-sinker-iso-post.md`. Follow-up filed: #1135 (the empty sinker template joins the built-in machine library).
- MCP: no new command. The existing post selection and posting tools address the new registry name.

## Goldens
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/sinker-iso/sinker_burn_cavity.nc`: the recorded CL golden `sinker_burn_cavity.cl` posted from the post crate (the #926 direction; the CL's regeneration is pinned by app's `sinker_burn_cavity_matches_golden`).
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/sinker-iso/sinker_burn_program.nc`: the real Sinker Burn op posted through `posting::post_setup` with "Sinker EDM (ISO)".

## How tested
Pinning tests:
- `crates/post/tests/sinker_post.rs`: `the_sinker_burn_posts_to_its_golden_against_the_fixture_dialect`, `every_missing_sinker_code_refuses_the_post_by_name` (each of metric, pickup, reference, condition, depth, end; inch; an empty section), `a_code_naming_a_placeholder_the_post_does_not_fill_refuses_by_name`, `a_stated_orbit_posts_the_machines_word_and_an_unlisted_one_refuses`, `a_mill_post_on_a_sinker_and_the_sinker_post_on_a_mill_are_refused` (fanuc, haas, tormach-plasma, fanuc-lathe on the sinker; sinker-iso on a VMC and on no machine), `a_feed_with_xy_travel_or_an_rpm_is_refused_by_name`.
- Unit tests: `post::machine_edm::the_serves_law_reads_both_ways`, `post::machine::edm_codes::codes_read_as_words_and_garbage_refuses_by_role`.
- `crates/app/tests/sinker_burn.rs` (through the real op): `the_sinker_burn_posts_through_the_generic_sinker_post_to_its_golden`, `a_missing_sinker_code_refuses_the_post_by_name`, `a_mill_post_on_a_sinker_machine_is_still_refused` (Fanuc, Haas, the plasma post; `post_serves` / `default_post_for`).
- `conformance.rs`: `every_sinker_post_refuses_every_mill_golden_by_name`; the registry and extension pins list the sinker post. Every shipped post still posts every golden byte-exact.
- Adjusted for the new registry entry: `plasma_post_refusals::the_mills_posts_decline_a_plasma_stream_and_the_1300pl` (the sinker post is refused by the serves law there), `smoothing::off_is_byte_identical_and_writes_no_smoothing_word` (skips the sinker post).

Gate (worktree target, sccache), head 82576ead:
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green - tools, post (incl. `sinker_post`), sim, motion, app (incl. conformance, golden_cl, posting, sinker_burn, edm_machine, edm_conditions, plasma_*, smoothing), ui; 12.8 min, 0 failed. (The base includes the whole stack, so it ran broad.)
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised
- **Not exercised on a real EDM control** (#290 D10). The dialect, condition and part are synthetic fixtures; a user with a real machine fills `edm.codes` from the control's manual and dry-runs before any burn.
- No orbit is generated yet (#544), so the orbit words are pinned only from a hand-built stream.
- No Hub run. If the Hub can simulate a sinker program, this waits on that run before it is flagged ready.
- No library sinker machine yet (#1135).

Changelog: Sinker EDM: a generic ISO-style sinker post ("Sinker EDM (ISO)") posts a Sinker Burn with every EDM code (unit, pickup, reference, condition, burn to depth, orbit, end) read from the machine's edm.codes; a missing code refuses the post by name, and only a post declaring it serves sinker EDM may post for one (#542)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #542

title: refactor(sim): the app holders carry stock as CarriedStock, on either engine
body:
Step E3 of #637: the app's stock holders carry stock through one engine-agnostic type, so a carried program can run on the field engine. The column engine stays the default, call for call - no shipped verdict, golden or stamp changes.

## Design answers (full text in `docs/decisions/637-carried-stock-holders.md` and the [issue comment](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/issues/637#issuecomment-6815368088))

1. **Representation:** a transformed query frame, never a re-sample (the bake before a cut is a re-index on the origin-locked lattice). New here: the field arm builds its solid in the stock lattice's own frame (corner at the origin), so every verdict column is a field cell centre.
2. **Floor:** the lower end of the column's one material interval (`column_span`). A column cut through used to read back as air (`-inf`), which a verdict reads as "nothing to judge". It now reads the stock's own extent (top at the stock's floor, floor at the stock's top, both finite), so the column stays empty and the verdict convicts it.
3. **Clip:** the column law as a solid - the body minus the half-infinite prism above the entered stock's top over its footprint - not a plain intersection, which would delete material standing beside the new block (less material than the column engine reports).
4. **Agreement lane:** sim pins in the quick lane, an app heavy lane over the three carried suites' fixtures, and a per-thread engine switch so one process reads both.

## What changed

- **camcraft-sim:** `CarriedStock` (`Column(Body)` | `Field(Box<FieldBody>)`) in `stock_sim/carried.rs`: `carry`, `simulate`, `clip_under`, `into_body`, `deviate`. `FieldBody::body` (`carried_read.rs`) reads the field back onto the column `Body`, so `deviate`, `display`, `volume` and `bounds` are the column carry's own code on both arms. `clip_columns_under` is the clip loop moved out of the app.
- **camcraft-app:** `stock_sim_held.rs` holds `Held` (`Plain(Stock)` | `Carried(CarriedStock)`), `first_body` and the engine switch (`stock_sim::with_carry_engine`, `carry_engine`, env `CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE=field`). `stock_sim_carry::walk` / `judge` / `incoming_body`, `simulate_document`, `rest/across::sweep`, `rest::prior_state` and `rest::PriorPlan` go through it. The carried-body cache key takes the engine on the field arm only (the column key is unchanged).
- A cylinder stock is refused by name on the field arm (`FIELD_CARRY_SHAPE_REFUSAL`): its mesh is an inscribed polygon and would hold less than the column engine's disc at the rim.
- Old project files: nothing persisted changes.

## Tests

- `crates/sim/tests/carried_stock.rs` (6, quick lane): a block off the cell pitch on both arms - uncut, cut, carried through all 8 lattice turns and cut again, two carries with a cut between, the clip under a block and a round (then flipped and cut), a cut-through column convicted on both arms before and after a flip, degenerate field blocks refused.
- `crates/app/tests/carried_engine_agreement.rs`: heavy lane `both_engines_read_every_carried_document_alike` (`#[ignore]`, release): 14 documents mirroring `setup_carry`, `rest_across_setups` and `carried_verify`; per document the program verdict, the incoming body, the rest grid, verify's prior, the entered body and verify's bounds are read on both engines. **0 findings, max |delta| 0 on every read, 54 s in release.** A mutation check (field tops raised 1e-3) made it fail on every document, so the lane is not vacuous. Plus `the_engine_switch_is_scoped_and_defaults_to_the_column_engine` in the default lane.
- The carried suites run whole on the field arm (`CAMCRAFT_CARRY_ENGINE=field`): `setup_carry` 9/9, `rest_across_setups` 7/7, `carried_verify` 8/8, `carried_fixtures_cache` 6/6.
- Gates on head 68d317b7 (Linux): `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` green - sim suites 203 s, motion 11 s, every app suite 1009 s, 0 failed (it covers `setup_carry`, `rest_across_setups`, `carried_verify`, `carried_fixtures_cache`, `stock_sim_document`, `remachining`, `suppressed_rest`, `top_stock`, `setup_stock_source`, `stock_engine_agreement`). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean. Release heavy lanes: `carried_engine_agreement -- --ignored` 1/1 (54 s), `stock_engine_agreement -- --ignored` 3/3 (37 s).

## Not exercised / known limits

- Field arm only (not the shipped default): a cylinder stock is refused; a from-model stock is built (`FieldBody::mesh`) but no lane document uses one; ball, taper and bull-nose tools are not in the lane's documents (all flat end mills, which is why the deltas are exactly 0).
- On a cut-through column the field arm reports the gouge depth to the stock's floor, not the tool's depth below it (the column engine's number). Same class, different magnitude; the sim pin states both. No lane document cuts through.
- The field arm is slow in debug (the carried suites take 15-50 s each against under 1 s on the column arm); release is about 4 s per document.
- The operation priors (`drill_prior`, `top_stock`, `carried_stock`) still receive the read-back tops as a `Dexel` through `Columns::of_grid`; removing `Dexel` from the app is #586's remaining work, and the default flip is #589.
- No golden moved. No snapshot PNG touched. Windows and macOS not run.

Changelog: none (refactor; the column engine remains the default and every shipped verdict is unchanged).

Effort: max (not escalated). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

Refs #637

title: feat(post): generic ISO wire EDM post - codes as machine data
body:
Stacked on #1123 (on #560, #551). #551 and #560 are in rework, so this stack may need a `git merge` of the updated base later. This PR does not edit their files (`edm.rs` is untouched: the codes live on `Machine.edm_codes`).

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

- **`assets/posts/wire-iso.cps`** ("Generic ISO Wire EDM", #290 D5). It posts the 2-axis Wire Contour in RS-274 / ISO 6983 words: `%`, G21/G20, G90, G17, the work offset, G0/G1/G2/G3 (incremental I J), M00/M01, M30. Every EDM-specific code comes from the machine's `.mch` `edm.codes`: `condition` (a template holding `{id}`), `comp_off`, and, when `edm.awt: true`, `thread`, `cut` and `tip_disposal`. Each missing code refuses the post as "machine <m> states no edm.codes.<x>". Without AWT the post writes M00 so the operator can thread the wire at the start and cut it at the end.
- **Kerf vs pre-offset path (#532's decision):** the op's moves are already the wire-centre path. The post therefore cancels compensation before every cut and never engages it, so the kerf is applied only once. The post writes no F word, because the condition sets the cutting rate.
- **Refusals by name:** a machine that is not `kind: wire_edm`, a rapid while the wire is threaded, a Z change, a posed move, an arc off the XY plane, a cycle, a tool change, a spindle speed, and a section that is not wire work.
- **post crate:**
  - `machine/edm_codes.rs` parses `edm.codes`; a garbled entry refuses the file by name.
  - The mirror and `script_props` expose `machine.kind` and `machine.edm = {codes, awt}` for EDM kinds.
  - New engine door: `PARAM EdmCondition` through a script without the `wireEdm = true` manifest flag is refused by name, so no cutting post can post a wire path.
- **app:**
  - `posting_wire.rs` streams the op's section (`EdmCondition`, `WireSide`, no TOOL or spindle).
  - The post is in `BUILTINS`, and `WIRE_POSTS` serves `wire_edm` only. It is the default post for a wire EDM, and no cutting post serves a wire EDM.
  - `op_streams` no longer refuses the Wire Contour. Any other tool-less kind is still refused.
- Docs: `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`, `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` (the PARAMs). The decision record is `docs/decisions/533-wire-iso-post.md`.

## How tested

- `wire_post.rs` (new):
  - `the_punch_contour_posts_its_golden_through_the_gate`: the full `posting::post_script` gate, verification included, matches the golden `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/wire-iso/wire_contour_punch.nc`. It also checks the order G0 -> thread -> condition -> comp off -> cut -> wire cut -> tip disposal, and that there is no Z, F, G41/G42 or spindle word.
  - `each_required_code_removed_refuses_the_post_by_name`: removing each of the 5 codes refuses by name. A machine without AWT posts with two M00 stops and needs no AWT codes. A condition template without `{id}` is refused.
  - `a_mill_machine_and_a_cutting_post_are_refused_by_name`: the VMC machine is refused, every other built-in post is refused the wire section (`wireEdm`), and a mill golden through the wire post is refused.
  - `the_registry_offers_the_wire_post_for_wire_edms_only`
- Synthetic fixture `crates/app/tests/edm/wire-iso-fixture.mch`: the codes are clearly fictional (`FX-THREAD`, `FX-COND {id}` ...) and the condition is invented.
- Updated: `wire_contour.rs` (the op now streams with its condition, where it used to be refused), `conformance.rs` (the registry, extension tables).
- Unit test in `edm_codes.rs`.
- Gate on the final head (b9ddec58): `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/issue/532-wire-contour` green - post suites (lib, axis_direction_cli, comp, comp_plane, mch_head_search, post_engine) and every app suite (the new golden is shared test input, so quick ran the whole app set), 0 failed; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- **Not exercised on a real EDM control (#290 D10).** The golden is posted against the synthetic fixture dialect. A user with a real machine fills `edm.codes` from its manual and dry-runs before any cut.
- No wire verification yet (#534). No taper, 4-axis or skims. No UI for editing `edm.codes` (they are hand-stated in the `.mch` for now). The CLI raw-machine door passes `edm` through unvalidated, and the script validates each code it reads.

Changelog: Wire EDM: a generic ISO wire post ("Generic ISO Wire EDM") posts the 2-axis Wire Contour, with every EDM code (condition, compensation cancel, AWT thread/cut, wire-tip disposal) taken from the machine's `edm.codes` and refused by name when missing (#533)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #533

title: fix(motion): hold the adaptive planning budget per margin attempt
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0. **Stacked on #1080** (#982, itself stacked on #1007): the diff against `main` shows their commits too; this PR's own change is the last commit (`budget.rs`, `budget_twins.rs`, `grow.rs`, one line of `lib.rs`, `rotary_adaptive.rs`, the decision file). The twins need #1080's `rings::OPEN_INSET` hook, its level reader and its microlift fix - on main the same levels flip to "refused for travel" on the lift edge once the budget lets them through.

## What the knife edge was

Not the limits. The growth planner (`adaptive/grow.rs`) grows an area from a wall margin that closes 2.5 um a revolution; where the margin is spent before the fronts are done (about 140 revolutions at the first rung) the whole plan is made again from a wider margin (`MARGIN_SCALES` 1.0, 1.6, 2.4). Whether a plan needing about 140 revolutions finishes inside the first margin or just after is a matter of nanometres. The #850 budgets were **summed over the attempts**, so "ran out of margin" also meant "the retry starts with a whole attempt already spent" - the sum jumped by 22.5 k tool radii on an 8 nm change.

The r7 bar's developed level at radius 5.0 (release, Linux x86-64):

| openings deeper by | first attempt | second attempt | before (summed) | now (per attempt) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0, 8, 16, 32, 510 nm | runs out of margin at 22.5 k r, 377-380 k vertices | done in 24.5-24.7 k r, 396-400 k vertices | refused at 30 k r, 85-86 revolutions into the retry; rings | HSM-planned |
| 62, 125, 250 nm | done in 22.3 k r, 375-377 k vertices | - | HSM-planned | HSM-planned |

The window's levels 6.0 and 5.0 are the same band and the same case (first attempt done at 8, 125 and 250 nm).

## What changed

- `adaptive/budget.rs`: laws 2 (30 k r) and 3 (600 k vertices past 5 k r) are counted for each margin attempt on its own - `Work::attempt()` resets the sums, called at the top of `Planner::grow`. Limits, law 1 and every refusal text are unchanged.
- Counted per attempt, a sum moved by at most 0.7 % (length) and 1.6 % (vertices) over every perturbation tried; the nearest attempt on our fixtures is 24.7 k of 30 k r (1.21x under) and 400 k of 600 k vertices (1.50x under), pinned as margins.
- The "never hang" bound is now three attempts of 30 k r (the ladder's three rungs) instead of 30 k r in all. Only a plan that runs out of margin uses more than one attempt; law 3 still stops a heavy plan inside its first. The bar's level 5.0: ~11 s to be refused before, ~14 s to be planned now.

## Verdicts that change

- `rotary_adaptive`, r7 bar, level 5.0: was "refused past the budget", cut by rings at a full-width load (13 breaks); now HSM-planned (8545 planar moves, 1935 arcs, 18.4 % D, no in-cut break past 5 degrees). The pin names 6.5, 6.0, 5.5, 5.0 as planned and forbids a budget refusal.
- `rotary_adaptive`, window, levels 6.0 and 5.0: were refused past the budget; now HSM-planned (18.8 % D, no break). Pinned the same way.
- Nothing else: across every motion suite and the app suites that plan Adaptive (release, `--include-ignored`) no other plan reaches a second margin attempt; every other refusal (the island at 109 revolutions / 600 037 vertices / 9.4 k r, the stepped block, the bands refused up front) falls inside its first attempt with the same counts. No golden file moves.

## How tested

- `adaptive::budget::tests::each_margin_attempt_is_held_to_the_budget_on_its_own` (default suite).
- `adaptive::budget::twins::the_r7_bars_levels_decide_the_same_way_under_sub_micron_perturbations` and `...::the_windows_levels_decide_the_same_way_under_sub_micron_perturbations` (heavy lane, release `--ignored`, ~100 s together): openings 0, 8, 16, 62, 250 nm deeper; every level under the skin HSM-planned in every twin, no budget refusal, no planner overload, load within the suite's law, each attempt within the stated margins. Both are red at 0 nm without the change.
- `rotary_adaptive::adaptive_plans_the_developed_levels_under_the_load_and_kink_laws` and `::the_developed_window_reaches_the_planner_and_names_each_refusal` now state the levels' verdicts.
- The existing budget refusal fixtures are unchanged and green (`budget::fixtures`, `adaptive_hsm`'s island, motion and app `pocket3d_hsm`).
- On the final head 5516dbc3: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/982-microlift-acceptance` green (motion lib, adaptive_band, adaptive_hsm, adaptive_orbit_seam, pocket3d_hsm; 0 failed); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; release `--include-ignored`: motion lib 201/201, rotary_adaptive 6/6, adaptive_hsm 6/6, adaptive_band 2/2, adaptive_orbit_seam 1/1, motion pocket3d_hsm 4/4, app pocket3d_hsm 2/2, pick_agnostic 7/7, shoulder_adaptive 3/3. Before the change was final, every motion test (`--include-ignored`, release) and every app suite that mentions Adaptive ran green with a probe that printed each margin attempt.

## Not settled here / not exercised

- Which margin a plan is made from still turns on nanometres, so the twins post different plans (all HSM, all within the load law). On the r7 bar's level 5.0 the plan made inside the first margin (62, 125, 250 nm) posts 5 in-cut breaks of 5.0-6.2 degrees at the band's end; the wider-margin plan (0, 8, 16, 32, 510 nm, the unperturbed bar among them) posts none. Those are #1050's end kinks, present on main whenever the first margin suffices; this change newly accepts only the wider-margin plan. The twins hold level 5.0 to at most 5 (`BAR_50_BREAKS`, to go with #1050) and the unperturbed bar to none. Making the plans alike, not only the verdicts, is #882's.
- Only Linux x86-64 was measured; another platform's libm puts the margin edge at other nanometres (the twins cover both sides here).
- The batch and release tiers and the UI suites were not run (motion only is touched).
- Decision: `docs/decisions/1051-planning-budget-edge.md`.

Changelog: Adaptive: the planning budget is held per margin attempt, so a level is no longer refused (and cut by Offset rings) or HSM-planned depending on nanometre-scale geometry; the rotary r7 bar's level 5.0 and the window's levels 6.0 / 5.0 are now HSM-planned.

Effort: max (not escalated)

Fixes #1051

title: feat(thread): external threads on a boss at the operation level
body:
Stacked on #1045 (on #1005). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

The Thread operation cuts external threads on a boss.

- **`external` on the operation.** `OpParams::Thread { external }`: the list then holds bosses (`radius` = major radius, `entry_z` = top, `floor_z` = shoulder). File / MCP key `external`, additive, written only when set; the stamp digests it only when set, so no internal thread goes Stale.
- **Boss recognition.** `drilling::recognize_bosses`: the hole recogniser's weld, circle fit and rim-span law with the facing vote inverted (closed round upright walls facing away from their axis). Stepped walls are never folded. Detect holes (button and MCP `detect_holes`) reads bosses when the operation is external. The Thread page gets "External thread (on a boss)", "Detect bosses" and a per-row Remove (a round base is a boss too).
- **Judging a tool beside a boss, without the silhouette** (`operation::thread_boss`):
  - crest law: tangency against each boss's MINOR circle (major less 0.6134 x pitch), nothing else in the region. The drawn wall is not what the crests answer to, so a matched thread is not convicted on every helix (the #1071 flaw, not repeated);
  - root law: the solid law with the cutter narrowed by the EXTERNAL depth: roots, tip, shank, holder against the whole part, shoulder included;
  - neighbour law (new): the crest ring at full radius over the cutting length against every facet that is not the threaded boss's own wall, gouge tolerance only. The boss a run of feeds threads is read from the helix's own centre, never from nearness.
- **Air law** (`thread_entry::judge_bosses`, #992's external analogue): every position the feeds take the tool through is read in the stock the program ahead leaves; a column under the tool's disc, more than one cell outside the boss, standing above the tip refuses the thread by name (place, heights, how far out and how deep to clear). Unknown prior is refused.
- **Door** (create / edit / retool, again at generate): a boss no thicker than the thread is deep; a thread longer than the mill reaches beside a boss (shank wider than the tooth roots, or the holder); infeed against the external depth.
- **Simulation.** An external thread is swept at its external root radius (`thread_op::sim_radius`); the internal depth read 0.07 x pitch of the boss as cut and the post gate called it a gouge. Internal threads and taps unchanged.
- The kernel ride is used as #1005 pinned it; nothing in #1005 / #1045 was reworked. No bugs found in them.

## Sources

ISO 68-1 / ISO 965-1 / DIN 13 (external design root 17/24 H = 0.6134 P); Machinery's Handbook, "Thread milling"; Smid, "CNC Programming Handbook", thread milling chapter; Sutherland-Hodgman clipping and point-to-polygon distance (O'Rourke). No HSMWorks / Fusion material consulted. Decisions: `docs/decisions/985-external-threads.md`.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/thread_boss.rs` (11 tests): `an_external_m8_thread_verifies_clean_and_posts_helical_moves` (generator verdict, post gate and program sim clean; G02 with Z; goldens), `a_single_form_mill_threads_an_m10_boss_one_turn_per_thread`, `left_hand_and_conventional_external_threads_verify_clean_too`, `detect_reads_the_bosses_of_an_external_thread_and_holes_of_an_internal_one`, `a_boss_standing_in_uncut_stock_is_refused_by_name`, `a_part_wall_the_roughing_left_standing_in_the_sweep_is_refused`, `a_wall_inside_the_crest_rings_sweep_is_a_gouge_that_blocks_the_post`, `impossible_bosses_are_refused_when_the_operation_is_made`, `a_hole_list_read_as_bosses_never_passes_silently`, `moving_the_roughing_after_the_thread_marks_it_stale_and_refuses_it`, `the_external_flag_edits_undoes_and_round_trips_the_project_file`.
- Unit: `operation::thread_boss::tests` (7), `operation::thread_entry::tests` (3 new), `operation::thread_op::tests::an_external_thread_narrows_the_roots_by_the_external_depth`, `drilling::boss::tests` (4).
- MCP: `mcp::external_thread_milling_over_the_tools`. UI: `thread_mill_page_tests::the_geometry_tab_switches_between_holes_and_bosses_and_apply_undoes`, `a_listed_feature_can_be_removed_from_the_draft`.
- Goldens: `thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form.cl`, `nc/thread_mill_external_m8_multi_form.nc`, `thread_mill_external_m10_single_form.cl`.
- Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/992-thread-undrilled` green on the final head ab0f88fa (motion, app - every app suite, since the shared thread fixtures changed - and ui suites; 12.1 min, 0 failed); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised / left open

- A near-net or cast stock with nothing machined ahead is refused (as a cored hole is under #992). Posed (3+2) external threads are refused.
- The simulation does not draw the thread form; the boss shows at its drawn diameter.
- The neighbour law walks the facets the path's box reaches with no spatial index; not timed on a large model.

title: feat(edm): sinker rough and finish with undersize from their conditions
body:
Stacked on #1131 (→ #560 → #551). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
- **Sinker Burn passes** (sibling ops, one electrode per op): each Sinker Burn gains `pass` (single / rough / finish; single keeps #541's law unchanged) and the finished cavity `cavity_x` / `cavity_y`.
- **Undersize law** (`motion::sinker_undersize::judge`): a rough or finish reads its condition's `undersize` and `gap` through #531's `Edm::condition` by id, after the sinker-kind check (`sinker_op::condition`, the door the gap and undersize now share). Per axis it refuses by name: electrode + 2×gap wider than the cavity (the wall would be burned past size), a finish that burns short of the cavity ("sinker finish leaves the cavity under size"), and an electrode that is not `cavity - 2×undersize`. The tip stands one undersize above the finished floor (`SinkerParams.stand`), so a rough leaves `undersize - gap` on floor and walls alike.
- **Order law**: a finish looks back (program order, same setup, unsuppressed) for the rough of the same cavity. If its undersize is not smaller, a new advisory `Warning::SinkerFinishOrder` names both numbers. It does not hold the post, because the finish's own size law already holds the cavity to size.
- Stamp digests the undersize and the rough a finish follows. DTO keys are additive and written only for rough or finish. The UI Passes tab gains the pass and the cavity X/Y.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/543-sinker-undersize.md`.

title: fix(motion): the plan's crossing check reads a shared end a rounding apart as a touch
body:
## What changed

The adaptive planner's own self-crossing check (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/guard.rs`, the `scan` behind `first_crossing` / `crossing_pairs`) asks a new pair predicate, `crosses`, instead of the exact-sign `proper`.

- `crosses` is the same proper-crossing (orientation) test, with one change. A chord end within `TOUCH` = **1e-9 mm** (1 pm) of the other chord's line counts as *on* it (sign 0), where only an exact zero did before. Two chords cross only when each one's ends stand strictly on opposite sides of the other's line. The test compares `|orient| <= TOUCH * |ab|`, with no division.
- So a shared end point a rounding apart is read the way an exact shared vertex always was: a contact, not a crossing. That covers an orbit closing a ulp off its start (#980's seam), a microlift return landing on a chord end, and a ring starting on the last ring's vertex. A real crossing still crosses.
- A non-finite point (NaN, +-inf) in any walk now reads as a crossing at that point (its walk paired with itself). Before, the length filter dropped NaN chords silently, and the bounds check looked only at x, so an infinite y slipped through.
- `guard::proper` is unchanged: `lift_link` uses it for its own link law, which this PR leaves alone (#1080 touches it).
- Only `guard.rs` changed, plus the new `guard_tests.rs` (pulled in with `#[path]`, so `mod.rs` is untouched), plus the decision file. No overlap with #953 or #1080.

### The tolerance and why
f64 rounding on a 10 m workspace is ~2e-12 mm per coordinate, so 1 pm sits about 1000x above it. Cutting tolerances are microns (the verifier's is 0.005 mm), about 1e6x above it. A chord end within 1 pm of a line can only meet the other chord at that end, so nothing a tool could cut hides inside it. The full reasoning is in `docs/decisions/1048-guard-shared-ends.md`.

### Changed from the brief: contacts are not crossings
The first version excused only shared ends and treated T-touches and collinear overlaps as crossings. That failed the pinned `adaptive::tests::a_channel_is_grown_as_one_spiral_that_never_crosses`: in the lifted plan, pass 197 retraces pass 196's last chords exactly (32 chord pairs on the same line, same direction). The exact-sign law always read that as a contact (orient 0), and so does the verifier's law (a). A stricter check would send a good adaptive plan to Offset rings, the very loss this issue is about. The fix is therefore the old law with its exact zero widened to `TOUCH`. Whatever contact it accepted exactly, it now also accepts a rounding off. This is pinned and recorded in the decision file.

## Tests (pins, `crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/guard_tests.rs`)
- `a_figure_eight_crosses_and_a_spiral_does_not` (moved from guard.rs, unchanged)
- `a_spiral_returning_to_its_seed_within_rounding_does_not_cross`: jitters of 1e-15 and 1e-12 mm in 8 directions
- `a_return_landing_on_a_chord_end_does_not_cross`
- `a_ring_starting_on_the_previous_rings_vertex_does_not_cross`

  Each of these three also asserts that the old exact-sign `proper` tripped on at least one of its jitters, so the knife edge is really exercised.
- `a_real_crossing_near_a_shared_point_still_crosses`: a chord crossing 0.15 mm past a shared vertex, and a vertex a micron through the chord
- `a_contact_is_no_crossing_and_a_micron_past_is`: the decided case. T-touches exactly on the chord, at ±1e-12 and at 5e-10 mm, a collinear overlap and a retraced chord are not crossings. A vertex 1e-6 mm past the chord is.
- `a_non_finite_point_reads_as_a_crossing`: NaN and ±inf in x or y
- `the_bucketed_scan_agrees_with_all_pairs`: 40 rounds of random walks that reuse each other's vertices 1e-12 apart, comparing the grid scan with the all-pairs predicate

## Effect on the planner, goldens
No golden moved. `golden_cl` passes, and no golden file is in the diff. No fixture changed from Offset rings to adaptive or back in the suites run below. `a_channel_is_grown_as_one_spiral_that_never_crosses` still asserts `first_crossing(&pl.passes).is_none()` on its plan.

## Gates (Linux x86_64, final head)
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: ok (motion lib + adaptive_band, adaptive_hsm, adaptive_orbit_seam, pocket3d_hsm), 1.1 min
- By hand, debug: motion lib (197 passed), machining2d 66, rotary_adaptive 2, offset_shells 6, tiny_step 3, adaptive_hsm 1, adaptive_orbit_seam 1, pocket3d_hsm 3. App: golden_cl 25, conformance 6, shoulder_adaptive 3, roughing2d 7, whole_model_pocket 5, pocket3d_hsm 1, pick_agnostic 5. All green.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- Heavy pins (release `--ignored`): all green and none moved. motion adaptive_hsm (5, the M11.4 C metric report and the island budget pin included), motion pocket3d_hsm `the_stepped_block_holds_the_planner_laws_level_by_level`, motion rotary_adaptive (3), motion offset_shells (1), and app pocket3d_hsm `the_users_bore_roughs_adaptive_level_by_level_and_verifies_clean` (272 s; its pinned counts and verify-clean hold)

## Not exercised
- Windows and macOS (the predicate is plain f64 arithmetic, the same on every platform. The plan differences of #1010 come from elsewhere)
- The UI and snapshot lanes (nothing in them is touched)

## Left open
- #1129 (filed): the verifier's law (a) (`sim/verify/laws.rs`, `proper_cross`) is still exact-sign. A plan with an end shared a rounding apart, which the planner now accepts, could still read as crossing there and hold the post. Still safe (refused by name), but the two laws should agree.

Changelog: The Adaptive (HSM) planner no longer reads two walks that meet at one point, a rounding apart, as crossing itself, so such a level keeps its adaptive plan instead of falling back to Offset rings (#1048)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fork synced at v0.18.0

Fixes #1048

title: fix(posting): the index swing judges the swept work against the standing steel
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0. Not stacked: branched from upstream main (see "Subplate" below).

## What changed
The index-swing clause judged only the tool against the work the rotary sweeps. It now has a second half, `crates/app/src/posting_swing_standing.rs`, which judges the swept work (stock, parts, the fixtures that turn with it) against what stands still:
- **The face the rotary stands on.** The machine file has a new optional key on a work-turning rotary, `axis_to_table`: the rotary's centre height over its own mounting face. `crates/post/src/machine/swing.rs` reads it by the same law as `nose_to_axis`: unstated reads as unstated, garbled input is refused by name. The microARC 4 states 3.15 in (Tormach 4th-axis comparison sheet). If the swept radius plus 5 mm reaches that face, the post is refused, and the message names the op, the index (`A90.000`), the swept radius, the figure and the clearance.
- **Fixed fixtures over the work's X span.** Each is judged by its bounding box's distance from the A line in YZ. A strike is refused as "standing fixture <name>". Steel that sits wholly beside the work in X is clear.
- **What it cannot judge is named, never silent.** A machine with no `axis_to_table`, a fixed fixture with no facets or non-finite facets, and a fixed fixture whose box reaches across the centerline over the work (a tailstock, the rotary's own body) are listed in the gate's not-judged line: `index swing did not judge the work against the standing steel: ...`. That line reaches the status line, the viewer header and the script result through `GateReport::not_judged`.
- `posting_index_swing.rs`: `swept_radius` becomes `swept` (it returns the radius plus the X span). `work_a` and `index_angle` are now shared with the new clause. The tool half's behaviour is unchanged.
- The microARC tester-kit project carries the new figure (80.01 mm). `assets/machines/AGENTS.md` documents the key.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/1107-swing-work-vs-standing.md`.

**Subplate (#1082).** Not stacked on #1082. A table, plate or subplate under the rotary raises the centerline along with the rotary, so the nearest standing face under the rotary is always its own centre height below the line, whatever the stack. #1082's subplate is covered by this law without reading its stack model. Steel beside the rotary that reaches under the work is judged once it is modelled as a fixed fixture.

## How tested
Pinning tests in `crates/app/tests/index_swing.rs` (13 pass: 9 existing, unchanged, plus 4 new):
- `work_swinging_into_the_face_the_rotary_stands_on_is_refused_by_name`: the bar on a rotary 2 mm inside the margin is refused by name and the post writes nothing. The same bar with 2 mm to spare passes.
- `a_standing_fixture_under_the_work_is_judged_by_its_distance_from_the_line`: a low plate under the bar clears, a block beside the bar in X clears, and a riser 15 mm under the line is refused by name.
- `standing_steel_the_swing_cannot_read_is_named_not_judged`: with no `axis_to_table` the program posts and the gap is named. A tailstock across the line is named too.
- `the_shipped_microarc_states_its_centre_height_over_the_table`.
- Post unit test `nose_to_axis_reads_scaled_or_refuses_by_name` is extended to `axis_to_table`.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the head 5716d312: green (post suites and 98 app suites plus lib, 4.1 min, 0 failed). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised
- The GUI by hand.
- A real long part on hardware.
- Per-angle swings: the swing is judged over the full turn, like the tool half.
- Fixtures that are not boxes are judged by their bounding box, which is conservative.
- The release lanes.

Changelog: The index swing now refuses a post when the work it sweeps would strike the face the rotary stands on or a standing fixture; machine files state the rotary's centre height as `axis_to_table` (microARC 4: 3.15 in), and steel it cannot judge is named (#1107)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1107
