title: feat(edm): sinker burn to depth with a single electrode
body:
#560 and #551 are merged into upstream main; this branch merges upstream/main. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed
- **Electrode as a tool** (`ToolKind::Electrode`, `crates/tools/src/electrode.rs`). It reuses the existing `Tool` fields: `diameter` = face X, `width` = face Y, `flute_len` = length below the holder, `shank_len` = pickup offset. rpm 0 and a sharp face are required by law. A garbled electrode is refused by name at AddTool / ChangeTool / the library reader. `EDM-E10X6` joins the starter catalog, and the project file round-trips the kind.
- **Sinker Burn op** (`OpType::SinkerBurn`, tag 41, `Section::Sinker`, `Family::Sinker`). It is admitted only on a `sinker_edm` machine; on any other machine the family door refuses it by name. Milling ops on a sinker stay refused (#530). Only an electrode mounts it.
- **Depth from a stated datum.** The datum is the work top, the cavity floor (a stand-off) or the electrode tip at the approach plane. A burn past the cavity floor datum, past the model's floor, or deeper than the electrode is long is refused by name (`crates/motion/src/sinker.rs`).
- **Spark gap** (coordinator note from #560's review). The op names a condition id, which is required. The command checks that the setup's machine is a sinker EDM, then asks `Edm::condition` for `ConditionField::Gap` only, never a wire field. Lookup is by id only, never by role. The tip stops one gap above the floor. The op's stamp digests the resolved gap, so a re-stated condition marks the op stale.
- **CL**: an approach rapid, one feed plunge and a rapid retract. Golden: `crates/app/tests/golden/sinker_burn_cavity.cl`.
- **Stock-sim verification** (#290 D7). A new column-engine **box atom** (`crates/sim/src/stock_sim/dexel_box.rs`, `simulate_box`) sweeps the face grown by the gap and is exact per column. The program verdict (`simulate_document`, carry walk) cuts sinker ops with it. The field eye (stock view and playback) refuses an electrode program by name; it has no box atom yet. Rest masks count an electrode as removing nothing, which is the safe side.
- **UI**: a minimal Sinker Burn op page (`sinker_page.rs`) keeps the tab law and edits through `EditOperationParams`. The full sinker pages are #548. The tool editor gains an electrode X/Y row.
- **MCP**: no new tool is needed. `add_tool` (definition), `add_operation` (kind "Sinker Burn"), `edit_operation`, `generate` and `undo` drive the same undoable commands, and a test pins this.
- **Posting**: refused. #542 owns the sinker post (#533 the wire). `post_serves` is only the picker's listing law, so the post door itself refuses: `posting_family::edm_at_post`, called by every writer (`post_setup`/`post_script` via `post_script_body`, the per-mount `post_each` and the per-op writer) right after `op_streams`, refuses any program whose setup's machine is a wire or sinker EDM by name ("Setup1: no post for a sinker EDM machine yet (#542) - Burn0 is not posted and no file is written; ...") before a byte is written. The MCP `post` tool and the script `post` verb ride the same writers. Pinned by `sinker_burn_held::the_post_refuses_a_burn_on_its_sinker_until_an_edm_dialect_ships` and the MCP leg of `sinker_burn::the_sinker_burn_is_driven_over_mcp_with_the_gui_commands`.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/541-sinker-burn-depth.md`.

## How tested
- Pinning tests in `crates/app/tests/sinker_burn.rs`:
  - `sinker_burn_cavity_matches_golden`
  - `a_rectangular_electrode_burns_its_cavity_to_the_stated_depth`: the column tops sit at the floor inside the face plus gap and are untouched outside it, and the program verdict reads 0 gouge cells.
  - `a_burn_deeper_than_the_cavity_is_convicted_by_the_stock_sim`: a 1 mm overburn is convicted.
  - `a_depth_past_the_floor_datum_is_refused_by_name`: all three datums.
  - `a_sinker_burn_needs_a_sinker_and_a_stated_condition`
  - `an_electrode_is_refused_at_add_tool_when_garbled_and_round_trips_the_file`
  - `the_sinker_burn_is_driven_over_mcp_with_the_gui_commands` (ends with the MCP `post` tool refused by name, no file written)
  - `a_spark_gap_that_lifts_the_tip_out_of_the_work_is_refused_by_name`: a gap placing the tip at or above the approach plane, or not smaller than the burn below the work top, is refused (review of #1131).
- `crates/app/tests/sinker_burn_held.rs::the_post_refuses_a_burn_on_its_sinker_until_an_edm_dialect_ships`: `post_setup`, `post_mounts` and `post_per_op` all refuse by name and the folder stays empty.
- UI: the electrode tool glyph (`assets/ui/svg/tool-electrode.svg`, original, rasterised by `cargo xtask icons`) is pinned by `op_icon_table::every_tool_kind_has_its_own_svg_mastered_icon`.
- Unit tests: `motion::sinker` (datums, refusals) and `tools::electrode`.
- Registry and law tests were updated for the appended kind: `stamp_follows_every_input` (42 rows), `ribbon`, `tool_law`, the catalog order, and the UI tips and tab law.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base HEAD`) is green: tools, sim, motion, app and ui suites (10.5 min). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised
- **Not exercised on a real EDM control** (#290 D10). The condition and the part are synthetic fixtures.
- The field-arm stock view and playback of a sinker program are refused by name; that box atom is for #548.
- No post: refused by name at the post door until #542 (sinker) / #533 (wire) ship a dialect. No orbit (#544), no undersize passes (#543).
- Shared tables (op kinds, sections, families) take small appended edits. The wire stack (#532) will append next to them, so whichever PR merges second renumbers its kind tag.

Changelog: Sinker EDM Sinker Burn: a rectangular electrode (a tool-library kind) burns to a depth read from the work top, cavity floor or electrode tip, placed by the machine condition's spark gap; a depth past the floor is refused by name and the stock sim convicts an overburn (#541)

Fixes #541

  - New job **`wasm`** (ubuntu-24.04, `contents: read`, 45 min timeout): `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown`, apt `clang-18` / `llvm-18` (CC/AR for wasm32 set via `GITHUB_ENV`), `bash web/build-app-wasm.sh --release`, `web/check-app-page.sh target/web`, an `if: always()` warning if `Cargo.lock` is left modified (#949), upload `target/web/` as artifact `wasm-app`.
  - Job **`site`** now `needs: [wasm]` with `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` (the pattern `publish` uses). After `zola build` it downloads `wasm-app` only when `needs.wasm.result == 'success'`, replaces `site/public/app/` with it and runs the check on the Pages artifact's `app/`; otherwise it emits `::warning::Browser build missing: ...` and keeps the site's own `app/` page.
  - `pages` is unchanged. No new trigger: still `vX.Y.0` tags and hand-run `workflow_dispatch` (which builds and deploys nothing).
- `web/check-app-page.sh` (new, runs locally too): the four files are present and non-empty, the `.wasm` starts with the wasm magic, no `src=`/`href=`/import-map value/`import`/`fetch`/`new URL`/`new Worker` names a root-absolute (`/x`), protocol-relative (`//x`) or `http(s):` URL, and no `SharedArrayBuffer`.
- Site: `content/app.md` + `templates/app.html` are the page at `app/` when the site has no browser build (a local preview, or a release whose wasm build failed): it says so and why, so the link is never a 404. The front page (`templates/index.html`, because only the templates read `version.toml`) gets "Try CamCraft in your browser" with the version, WebGL2, and what does not work yet (#31: no file picker, no playback without threads, no WebGPU, views needing desktop GPU features say so). `guide/first-run.md` gets a short "Trying it in the browser first" section. The old "coming" paragraph is gone. One `.button` CSS rule.
- `docs/decisions/1103-wasm-app-on-pages.md`: path layout, failure behaviour, #949 handling, no new trigger, no wasm-opt.

No change to `web/index.html`, `wasi_shim.js` or the build script: every URL was already relative (`./wasi_shim.js` in the import map and module script, `./camcraft-ui.js`, and the glue's `new URL('camcraft-ui_bg.wasm', import.meta.url)`). The check now pins that.

## Review fixes (head 1e345767, after merging origin/main)

- **The front page claims only what was deployed.** The `site` job appends `app = true|false` to the gitignored `site/version.toml` before `zola build`; `true` only when the `wasm` job succeeded, the artifact downloaded (now `continue-on-error`) and `web/check-app-page.sh` passes on it. `templates/base.html` reads it as `app`; `templates/index.html` shows one of three lines. The first-run page is Markdown and cannot read the flag, so it says "when this site's release has a browser version" and points at the front page.
- **The check in `site` is never fatal for the docs.** It now runs twice in `site`: on the downloaded artifact (decides the flag), and on the copy at `public/app/` (proves the Pages artifact holds it). A failure of the second drops the copy, flips the flag to `false` and rebuilds the site (about 0.3 s), with the same `::warning::Browser build missing: ...` annotation. Kept rather than moved to the `wasm` job only, because the issue's "Done means" asks for a check on the Pages artifact.
- **Plain wording:** "Open CamCraft X in your browser", "needs a browser with WebGL2 (a current Chrome, Firefox, Edge or Safari)" once, no "wasm32"/"shell" on the site.

### What a visitor sees

| Case | Front page | `/app/` | Run |
|---|---|---|---|
| wasm ok, both checks pass | button "Open CamCraft X in your browser" + "same release, nothing to install, needs WebGL2 (...)" + the early-version limits | the app | green |
| wasm job failed (or artifact did not download / pre-check failed) | "The browser version of CamCraft X is not available: it did not build for this release. Use the desktop downloads." (link to `/app/`) + limits | page "CamCraft in the browser": not part of this copy of the site, why, desktop downloads | `::warning::Browser build missing: ...`; docs and release deploy |
| copy at `public/app/` fails the check in `site` | same as the failed case (flag flipped, site rebuilt) | same stand-in page | `::warning::Browser build missing: its copy at app/ failed ...`; docs deploy |
| local preview (no `version.toml`) | "CamCraft in the browser comes with a released copy of this site; this local preview does not have it." | stand-in page | - |

Verified: pinned Zola 0.23.6 in WSL, `zola build` + `zola check` pass in all three flag states (none / true / false), front-page text read back from the built HTML for each; the `Build the site` step's body run in WSL with a passing and a failing fixture as `/tmp/wasm-app`: passing -> app/ holds the four files, `app = true`, button shown; failing -> warning printed, `app = false`, site rebuilt, app/ is the stand-in, "not available" shown. The real build output was checked before (first round); the worktree was removed after that push, so the second round used fixtures and did not rebuild the wasm.

## Wiring

```
linux, macos, windows, freebsd ─┬─> aur/snap/flatpak ─┐
                                └─────────────────────┴─> publish (release page) ─┐
wasm ──[artifact wasm-app = target/web/]──> site (!cancelled)                       ├─> pages (tag only; site + publish success)
          app = wasm ok && artifact && check(artifact)  -> version.toml `app = ...`  │
          zola build -> public/app/ = app.md stand-in                                │
          app:      public/app/ := wasm-app; check fails -> drop, app=false, rebuild │
          no app:   ::warning:: Browser build missing; stand-in stays ───────────────┘
          upload-pages-artifact(site/public)
```

## #949 (Cargo.lock)

Not stacked on #1009. The wasm build runs on its own runner and only `target/web/` leaves it, so a rewritten lock cannot reach any package or the site. The script on main already restores the lock via its EXIT trap (locally: `git status` clean after the build). The workflow warns if it ever is not. #1009 merges independently in either order.

## Readings (point 5)

- **Local build:** `web/build-app-wasm.sh --release` in the worktree on Windows (Git Bash, clang 21 msys2) - **exit 0, 7 min 09 s wall**, fresh `target/` (sccache was on PATH, so some third-party crates may have been cache hits): camcraft-app ~2 m 46 s, camcraft-ui cdylib ~2 m 33 s, wasm-bindgen-cli 0.2.129 install 1 m 15 s. `Cargo.lock` clean afterwards.
- **Sizes:** `camcraft-ui_bg.wasm` 29,878,727 B (28.5 MiB), gzip -9 8,983,088 B (8.6 MiB); `camcraft-ui.js` 154 KB; whole Pages artifact ~29 MB. Pages limits: 100 MB/file, 1 GB site - well inside.
- **Billed minutes per cut (estimate):** the `wasm` job on a cold 4-vCPU ubuntu-24.04 runner, no cache: apt ~1 min, wasi sysroot + cargo fetch ~1 min, two release builds + wasm-bindgen-cli ~10-15 min -> **about 12-18 billed Linux minutes (1x)**; the `site` job grows by seconds (artifact download + copy). Not measured on a runner.
- **wasm-opt:** not used - binaryen has no version+checksum-pinned download here, and the size does not need it.
- **Threads / COOP-COEP:** Pages sends no COOP/COEP headers. The glue and shim contain no `SharedArrayBuffer` (checked by the script), and the build has no atomics/threads target feature, so nothing relies on cross-origin isolation.

## Tests / checks run

- `bash web/check-app-page.sh target/web` on the real output: ok.
- Simulated Pages artifact: pinned Zola v0.23.6 (linux musl, workflow's sha256 verified) in WSL Ubuntu-24.04, `zola build --base-url https://someone.github.io/Fork-Repo` -> app links resolve to `https://someone.github.io/Fork-Repo/app/` on the front page and first-run page; then `public/app/` replaced by `target/web` and the check run on it: ok.
- `zola check`: passes (11 pages, 0 orphans).
- Check script against a bad fixture (root-absolute import map, `/x` fetch, `//cdn` import, `/a.wasm` `new URL`, `SharedArrayBuffer`, non-wasm `.wasm`): all 7 reported, exit 1. Good fixture: exit 0.
- Workflow YAML parsed (python yaml): jobs, `wasm` permissions read-only, `site` needs/if, triggers unchanged. actionlint not available (no checksummed download found) - not run.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: "nothing in crates/ changed: no tests to run" (0 steps).

## Not exercised

- **The workflow did not run** (no tag, no dispatch - zero Actions minutes). The `wasm` job's Linux path (apt clang-18/llvm-18, `CC_`/`AR_` env, wasm-bindgen-cli build on Linux) is unproven until the next release tag; the local build was Windows.
- No browser was launched; loading `/Camcraft/app/` in Chrome/Firefox is unproven here (#31's earlier headless Chrome run covered the same page from a local server).
- The failure branches ran only as the step's shell body under WSL with fixtures, not inside Actions; `continue-on-error` on the download and the `needs.wasm.result` wiring are read, not run.

Fork synced: n/a (canonical repo, main a0891091).

Changelog: The release workflow builds the browser (wasm32) shell and publishes it at `/app/` on the GitHub Pages site, linked from the front page and the first-run guide; a failed browser build leaves a page saying so and never withholds the docs or the release (#1103)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #1103

title: fix(post): doosan-dnm states a touch probe's spindle stopped before its first move
body:
#1035: #574 made every built-in mill post state its spindle stopped (M5; MOTOFF on Mazak) after a touch probe's tool change and length offset, before its first move. A control whose tool change leaves the spindle turning (a same-tool continuation, a manual change) then still brings the probe to the part stopped. `doosan-dnm.cps` (#614) came after #574. Its `startPreamble` skipped S/M3 for a section with a stated speed of 0 but wrote no M5, and `probe_spindle_stop.rs`'s `MILL_POSTS` left it out.

Fork synced at v0.18.0, PROCESS_VERSION 17; merged with upstream main at a0891091.

## What changed

- `assets/posts/doosan-dnm.cps`: after the tool change, the G43 and the skipped spindle start, a section with a stated speed of 0 writes `M5`, before the first move. A cutting section is unchanged.
- `crates/app/tests/probe_spindle_stop.rs`: `("doosan-dnm", "M5")` joins `MILL_POSTS`, so both of its tests cover the post:
  - `a_probe_section_stops_its_spindle_after_the_tool_change_on_every_mill_post`
  - `a_cutting_section_states_no_spindle_stop_before_its_first_move`
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1035-doosan-probe-m5.md`.

**Overlap with #1034** (#995, @mkinney, open draft): it edits the same `startPreamble`. It adds a `touchProbe` variable at the function's top line and gates the coolant line.
- This PR writes its condition inline after the spindle block instead (`spindleWait && !(sRpm > 0)`). A zero-speed section never clears `spindleWait`, so the condition still holds at that point.
- Neither PR touches the other's lines. A trial merge of this branch with #1034's head 5d8b71e2 is clean.
- I did not stack on #1034: it carries a breaking `feat(post)!` (Air coolant, #869) and merges at the next cut, which would hold this P2 fix until then.

## How it was tested

- Pinning test: `probe_spindle_stop::a_probe_section_stops_its_spindle_after_the_tool_change_on_every_mill_post`. It fails on main with "doosan-dnm: no M5 between the tool change and the first move" and passes with the fix. Its cutting-section twin stays green for doosan-dnm.
- Every app suite that posts through `doosan-dnm` or probes, run by hand, all green: `conformance`, `doosan_dnm_post`, `fourth_axis_pose`, `post_unit_word`, `golden_cl`, and the 12 `probe_*` suites.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: 66 passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green, but for a `.cps`-only change it plans almost nothing (#923). That is why the suites above were run by hand.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No snapshot PNG touched. No posted golden changes (none probes on doosan-dnm).

## Not exercised

- Not run on a Doosan control.
- The fix is pinned with the generic `3axis-vmc.mch`, as the other posts in `probe_spindle_stop` are, not with a Doosan machine file.

Changelog: Doosan DNM post: a touch probe section states its spindle stopped (M5) before its first move, like the other mill posts (#1035)

Effort: high (the issue's label: posted G-code is under the safety floor). Not escalated.

Fixes #1035

title: fix(app,ui): a stock copy carries its source's reduced-fidelity flag; a fidelity refusal silences the sim; tightened display colours
body:
Stacked on #1064 (base it on `main` and merge after #1064).

Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed, by #1056's points

1. **A stock copy carries its source's reduced-fidelity flag (done).** `SetStock` writes the copied model's chord error onto the `FromModel` stock, and its undo restores the stock's old flag. `UpdateModel`'s propagation trades the flag with the copy's facets both ways. `CreateSetup`'s datum clone and `DeleteSetup`'s undo carry it in `StockSnap`. `DeleteEntity` already restored any entity's flag. The project saves it on the stock row (the existing `coarse_mm` key), and the loader restores it for `FromModel` stocks. Deleting or renaming the source no longer stops the laws tightening. A refusal still names the model the facets came from, even after that model is deleted.
2. **Older projects (partly done, rest left open).** A stock from a #911-era file, where the flag lived only on the model, takes its source's flag on load (`model_fidelity::adopt_copies`). Files from before #911 are **not** handled. The version did not change with #911, so whether such a file holds a coarse STEP mesh cannot be known. Fixing that is file-format work: a version bump plus a "fidelity unknown" mark that is saved with the file, and then a choice between refusing and a named note. That is above this slice. It is recorded in `docs/decisions/1056-fidelity-flag-gaps.md` and left on #1056.
3. **The named refusal wins (done).** New `model_fidelity::program_tol`: when the gate refuses a program op for its model's fidelity, it returns that refusal as `Err`; otherwise it returns `verdict_tol`. `stock_sim::simulate_document` and `stock_sim_carry::judge` read it. The case found: a fine part in a stock copied from a too-coarse model, after that model is deleted. More generally, any op whose fidelity floor sits under the sim's 0.01 mm. The gate used to print a gouge line next to the refusal; now it prints the refusal alone, and the sim says it did not judge.
4. **Display tolerances (done).** `FieldView` gains `tol`, the tolerance its colours are gated at, filled from `program_tol` by `field_view` and by playback (`PlaySeed`/`FieldPlay`). `machined_classes::mesh_classes`, `ui` `trace/eye.rs` and `trace/cpu_eye.rs` read it instead of `DEV_TOL`. On a refused program the picture has no target, and its note gives the refusal.

## How tested

New suite `crates/app/tests/fidelity_copies.rs`:
- `a_stock_copy_keeps_its_flag_when_its_source_is_deleted`: delete, undo and redo; the refusal by the source's name still stands after the delete; box stocks stay unflagged.
- `the_copy_follows_its_source_through_updates_and_setup_clones`: UpdateModel and its undo, CreateSetup clone, DeleteSetup and its undo.
- `the_copys_flag_rides_the_project_file_and_an_older_copy_adopts_its_source`: the key is on the stock row, the file round-trips byte for byte, and a file with the key removed takes the source's flag on load.
- `the_named_refusal_wins_over_a_gouge_line_the_sim_would_read`: checked to fail without the fix. The gate printed `gouge: program cuts below the model in 2048 cell(s)` next to the refusal.
- `the_eyes_colours_are_gated_at_the_tightened_verdict_tolerance`: `field_view` and `FieldPlay::view` give 0.01 - excess on a 0.012 mm model, and `DEV_TOL` at full fidelity.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/904-reduced-fidelity-laws` is green on the final head (app suites and ui suites). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- The GPU and CPU eyes' changed argument (`fv.tol`) is covered only by the build and by the ui `trace_composite`/`trace_parity` suites at `DEV_TOL`. No pixel or snapshot run was done; snapshots are in the release lane.
- Projects saved before #911 (point 2, above).

No goldens or snapshot PNGs changed. `docs/decisions/1056-fidelity-flag-gaps.md` records the choices.

Effort: high (no escalation).

Changelog: A stock copied from a coarse STEP model keeps its reduced-fidelity flag after the model is deleted, and the project file saves it. A fidelity refusal is no longer joined by a gouge line from the sim. The stock view's colours use the tightened tolerance (#1056).

Refs #1056

title: feat(post): Fanuc Lathe writes inch programs from the document's unit
body:
Stacked on #981 (on #961). Fork synced at v0.18.0.

## What changed

`assets/posts/fanuc-lathe.cps` now writes an inch document as an inch program instead of refusing it. It declares `programUnits = "mm inch"` and reads `postOptions.Units`. The stream and every geometry or refusal check stay in mm; values are converted only in the word formatters:

| Word | G21 (unchanged) | G20 (new) |
|---|---|---|
| X (diameter), Z, I K, G76 first-block R, tool note D/R | mm, 3 dp | in, 4 dp |
| G99 F (feed per rev) | mm/rev, 4 dp | in/rev, 4 dp |
| G32 / G76 F (lead) | mm, 4 dp | in, 6 dp |
| G76 P(k) Q(dmin) Q(1st), G83 Q (no-point increments) | whole microns | whole 0.0001 in |
| G96 S | m/min | ft/min (m/min / 0.3048) |
| G97 S, G50 S, G83 P dwell, G76 P(m)(r)(a) | unchanged | unchanged |
| PART LOAD advance comment | `ADVANCE 30` | `ADVANCE 1.1811 IN` |

**Refused by name, never guessed:**
- A C-axis live-tool section on an inch program. Its feed is a composite rate that counts degrees as the linear unit, and how that rate works under G20 was not confirmed from a public source.
- A per-rev feed that rounds to `F0` at the program's digits.
- A G76 depth smaller than one least increment.

`program_units` drops Fanuc Lathe from its mm-only list, and `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` says the same. The decisions are in `docs/decisions/977-fanuc-lathe-inch.md`.

## Sources (public, behaviour only)
- RS-274 / ISO 6983 for G20 / G21.
- The public Fanuc 0i-T lathe programming vocabulary the post was already specced from: G96 / G97 / G50, G99, and the two-block G76 with P / Q as no-point counts of the least input increment (0.001 mm, or 0.0001 in under inch input).
- Published lathe programming guides with inch two-line G76 examples that use four-digit P / Q in 0.0001 in.

No vendor post, Fusion or HSMWorks material was used.

## How tested
- New suite `lathe_post_inch` (fixtures in `tests/fanuc_lathe_inch/`):
  - `every_turning_stream_posts_the_mm_program_in_inches`: covers facing, profile rough + finish, groove + part, axial drill, the G76 thread and the G32 thread. Each mm post must match its committed mm golden byte for byte, and Units mm must post exactly what no unit posts. Each inch program is checked word by word against its mm twin (lengths / 25.4, feeds / 25.4, increments / 2.54, SFM = m/min x 3.28084, everything else equal, G20 before any motion, no G21). The inch programs are committed under `golden/nc/inch/fanuc-lathe/`.
  - `the_inch_thread_words_are_pinned`: `G76 P010000 Q157 R0` / `G76 X0.378 Z0.315 P472 Q157 F0.07874`, plus the G32 lead `F0.07874`.
  - `an_inch_document_posts_inch_through_the_gate`: SetUnits inch, then `post_setup` gives the same program as the engine.
  - `surface_speed_is_feet_per_minute_and_rpm_never_scales`: `G96 S656` from 200 m/min, with `G50 S12000` unchanged.
  - `a_peck_counts_the_inch_increment`: `G83 ... Q394 P500`.
  - `what_inch_cannot_say_soundly_is_refused_by_name`.
- I also ran these suites by hand, all green: lathe_post, lathe_post_g76, lathe_post_refusals, program_units, mcp_units, c_axis_live, c_axis_unwind, lathe_post_tormach, lathe_spindle_law, lathe_blade_corner, lathe_nose_tip, coolant_followups, comment_escape, conformance, inverted_post, control_comp, wear_comp, program_entry, and every turning* suite.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/issue/902-document-units` (the new golden dir makes it run every app suite): green on 8e26be0c (all app suites, 12.9 min); clippy `-D warnings` clean on the new suite and program_units.
- No existing golden moved.

## Not exercised
- No real control. The inch digits (4 dp lengths and per-rev feeds, 6 dp leads, 0.0001 in increments) follow the published inch least increment and have not been proved on a 0i-T.
- Rounding per-rev feeds to 4 dp in inch is coarse on very small feeds: 0.0267 mm/rev posts as F0.001, about 5% low. That is a slower cut, never a faster one; see the decision file.
- C-axis live tooling in inch is refused, not converted.

Changelog: Fanuc Lathe post writes inch programs (G20; X/Z in inches, G99 in/rev, G96 in surface feet per minute, G76/G83 increments in 0.0001 in) for an inch document instead of refusing it; C-axis live tooling stays mm-only

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #977

title: fix(verify): a lateral rapid is re-read against the stock's top under it
body:
#1098 (#1091, the stock-top re-reading of vertical dives) has merged (0fc30b65); this branch has merged it from main, so the diff is this PR's own change only.

#1095: the rapid-in-stock law caps every column at the stock's highest point. #1098 re-reads a convicted vertical dive against the stock and part solids under the tool stack; lateral rapids kept the flat cap. A drill's link from hole to hole at its retract plane (Z 22), across the low part (Z 20) of a stepped from-model casting with a boss to Z 30 elsewhere, was convicted as if the boss stood under it, and the post was blocked.

Fork synced at v0.18.0, PROCESS_VERSION 26; merged with upstream main at 62a2c93a (head ca791ed2).

## What changed

- **`sim::verify::stock_top::acquit_by_stock_top`** now also re-reads an upright LATERAL rapid:
  - Each band of the stack (flute, shank, holder) is read over the capsule it sweeps along the move, against the highest vertex of any stock or part facet whose plan comes within its radius. This is the same upper bound as the dive's disc: for a closed shell, the topmost surface over a point is on a facet covering it.
  - The tip is taken at the rapid's lowest end for the whole move. A climbing or falling traverse is judged as if it ran level at its low end, which can only over-report.
  - Like the dive, it only removes convictions. It keeps the conviction for an open or non-manifold shell, a non-finite end, a posed rapid, a column-free mode (radial, revolve, rotary), or a flute capsule that meets no facet.
- New `dist2_seg_tri`: the plan distance from a segment to a triangle. A dive is the zero-length capsule. `dist2_seg_tri` of a point returns `dist2_tri` of it, float for float, so every dive verdict is unchanged.
- **Changed pin (#1098's):** `only_upright_column_dives_are_re_read` asserted that "a lateral rapid is never re-read", which is this issue's gap. Its diagonal dive to Z 22 over the low step, with the boss 7 mm past its end, is now acquitted. The same move posed stays convicted.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1095-lateral-rapid-stock-top.md`.

## How it was tested

New pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/stepped_stock_link.rs`: a part-sourced Drill of two holes in the part's open cavity, under a from-model casting stock, linking at the Z 22 retract plane.
  - `a_link_over_the_low_part_of_a_stepped_stock_passes_and_posts`: on the old law this fails (the link is `RapidInStock` and the post is blocked); now it passes and posts.
  - `the_same_link_across_the_boss_is_convicted`: convicted and post blocked.
  - `a_boss_under_the_tool_rim_along_the_link_is_convicted`: the boss 1 mm beside the centre line, under the 2 mm rim between the holes.
- `sim::verify::stock_top::tests` (5 new):
  - `a_traverse_over_the_low_step_is_acquitted`: along X, toward the boss along Y, and a falling traverse.
  - `a_traverse_crossing_the_boss_stands`: including one climbing over it.
  - `a_boss_under_the_rim_along_the_way_stands`.
  - `a_holder_band_over_the_boss_along_the_way_stands`.
  - `a_traverse_reads_the_part_and_fails_closed_like_a_dive`.
- #1098's own suites are unchanged and green: `stepped_stock_rapid`, `ladder_entry_height`, and the existing `stock_top` unit tests.

Gates:
- `cargo xtask gate batch` on 7e8d92cf (18.3 min): all green. That is geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion (slow suites included), app (`center_cut_multiaxis` included), ui and clippy `-D warnings`.
- No snapshot PNG touched.

## Review round (7e8d92cf)

- Merged main, which carries #1098's final rules. The conflicting line, the dive's `clear_of` call, keeps both sides: the `(c, c)` point trace and main's `m.to.z - e`.

title: feat(ui,mcp): work offsets listed by the setup's post; MCP takes an index (#931 slice 3)
body:
## #931 slice 3 of 3: the Setups combo lists the post's offsets; MCP takes an index

**Stacked on #1113 → #1101 → #945.** This PR targets `main`, so until those merge its diff also shows their commits. This slice is only the top two commits (`feat(ui,mcp): ...` and `fix(ui): ...`). Merge order: #945, #1101, #1113, then this one, retargeting each child before its parent merges. Fork synced at v0.18.0.

Effort: high (no escalation).

### What changed
- **Setups page / WCS page combo** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/setup_wcs_pick.rs`): lists offsets `1..=max` of the setup's **own** post (`setup::work_offset_names`, the cached table from slice 2). Each entry reads "Work offset n (NAME)", or "Work offset n" when the post gives that offset no name. The default post shows 6 entries. Tormach PathPilot shows 9 (G59.1-G59.3). If a setup holds a pick its post cannot express, for example offset 9 after switching to a six-offset post, that pick still shows as itself: "Work offset 9 - not on this post", listed alone after 1-6. It is never shown as offset 1. The post gate from slice 2 refuses it by setup name.
- **The wording is one function in app**: `setup_offsets::entry_label`.
- **Other UI words.** Slice 2 already moved the browser tree, the heights row, the viewport chips and the status line to the app's names. This slice changes the three texts that still named a fixed "G54-G59" range: the combo's hover, the heights page hint, and the WCS page's "Work offset:" line. The WCS page line appears in a release-lane snapshot, which gets regenerated at the cut; its structural twin `one_wcs` is updated here. I left the probe page's "Set G54".."Set G59" alone on purpose: the probe register arithmetic only reaches offsets 1-6 (triage point 4).
- **MCP `set_work_offset`** (`crates/app/src/mcp/setup_tools.rs`):
  - It takes `index`, 1-based. The words `G54`-`G59` are accepted as aliases of 1-6.
  - `word` stays as the older spelling of the same argument. If both are given they must agree.
  - `setup_offsets::parse_index` checks only the shape and the 1-255 sanity bound. The post's range is checked by `SetSetupWorkOffset::new` → `setup_offsets::check`, so the refusal is the same one the GUI gives, by setup name.
  - Replies carry `index`, `name` and `word` (an alias of `name`). So do `set_wcs` and `get_job`'s `setups[].wcs` (`mcp/job.rs`).
- **camcraft-mcp skill doc**: documents the new `set_work_offset` arguments and replies.
- **`.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` → 21**, because the skill doc changed. 21 is one above the highest bump in any open PR (20, #1033). **It renumbers at merge** if another process PR lands first. #681 needs the announcement when this merges.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/931-wcs-index-ui.md`.

### How it was tested
- New: `crates/app/tests/mcp_work_offset.rs` (4 tests):
  - `set_work_offset_takes_a_one_based_index_and_answers_index_name_and_word`
  - `the_legacy_words_are_aliases_of_offsets_one_to_six`
  - `an_offset_the_setups_post_cannot_express_is_refused_by_setup_name`
  - `the_schema_offers_index_and_keeps_word`
- New tests in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/setup_wcs_tests.rs`. These are AccessKit assertions with the popup open:
  - `the_combo_lists_the_setups_post_range_by_its_names`: 6 entries on the default post, 9 on Tormach
  - `a_pick_beyond_the_post_stays_visible_and_says_so`
- Updated: `an_unset_setup_reads_work_offset_one`, `the_picker_sets_the_setups_work_offset_through_the_command`, `offset_hint_names_the_real_pages_in_plain_words`, and the structural twin `setup_page_alignment_rows_structure` (asserts the combo value is "Work offset 1 (G54)" and no bare word).
- Green: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` (on de5829e8: post, app, ui suites, 0 failed); `mcp`, `mcp_setup`, `mcp_work_offset` and `wcs_index`; the ui lib, run from `crates/ui` (533 passed on the final head, `one_wcs` included); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`.
- No snapshot PNG changed.

### Not exercised
- **The combo needs the maintainer's hand check in the GUI.** Look at a Fanuc setup and a Tormach setup, and at the "not on this post" entry after switching a setup at offset 9 to Fanuc.
- No MCP tool sets a setup's post, so the MCP refusal is pinned against the default 6-offset post only. The Tormach range is pinned in app (`wcs_index`) and in the UI test.

Changelog: Work offsets are picked by number, up to what the setup's own post supports. The Setups page lists them as "Work offset n (NAME)", so Tormach shows 9. MCP `set_work_offset` takes a 1-based `index`; G54-G59 still work as aliases, and replies add `index` and `name`. (#931)

Fixes #931

title: feat(edm): 2-axis wire contour op - kerf offset to a stated punch/die side, start hole, corner refusal
body:
**Stacked on #560 (on #551) - this diff shows their commits until they merge; merge #551, #560 first.** This PR adds three commits on top of #560's head (`f5d8c06a`) and two merges of `origin/main` (no conflicts). Not exercised on a real EDM control.

## What changed

The first wire EDM operation (#532, part of #290; decisions D1, D2, D4, D8): **Wire Contour**, a vertical cut of one closed profile.

**Generator** - `crates/motion/src/wire_edm/` (beside the other 2D generators, on the existing offsetter):
- The wire-centre path is the profile's parallel at the **kerf offset = wire radius + the condition's spark gap**, on the **stated** side: inside the profile for a `die`, outside it for a `punch`. The side is never inferred.
- A straight lead-in runs from the stated **start hole / threading point** to the nearest point of the path; the profile is cut counter-clockwise; the lead-out retraces the lead-in.
- **Corner minimum:** an inside corner, slot, notch or neck the wire cannot cut (tighter than wire radius + gap) is refused by name with its spot and the minimum radius. Outside corners are mitred, so the wire never comes nearer than the offset.
- Refused by name, never trimmed: no start hole, a start hole on the product's side or nearer than the offset, an open profile, several profiles, a crossing or area-less ring, a profile smaller than the wire.
- The moves ride the lower programmed plane and state **no pose and no feed** (D2: it posts as XY; the control's generator sets the rate).

**Operation** - `crates/app`:
- `OpType::WireContour` (stored id 41, appended), its own **Wire EDM** section and family, admitted on a `wire_edm` machine only.
- Created and edited through `CreateOperation` / `EditOperationParams` (also paste and retype). At the command door, **a missing condition, gap or wire diameter is refused by name** through #531's `Edm::condition`.
- **A wire cut mounts no library tool.** Its wire diameter and gap come from the machine's condition table, their only source; a wire cut that names a tool is refused. The stamp digests the condition, so an edited table re-marks the cut Stale.
- The machine check on a wire EDM judges X/Y travel and names what it does not judge. The program gate refuses a wire cut by name until a wire post exists (#533).
- The op rides the project file (`wire_contour { top_z, bottom_z, condition, side, start }`). `side` has no default: a file or patch without it is refused.

`crates/ui` gains the match arms the new kind forces and a **minimal page** (`wire_page.rs`: side and start hole on Geometry, the two planes on Heights, the machine's conditions to choose from on Passes; no Feeds tab) - the UI's registry-wide tab law fails a kind whose tabs draw nothing. The ribbon's quick-add names no tool for a kind that mounts none, and its tip names a wire EDM as the machine wire work needs. No new icon; the real page, viewport picking of the start hole and the ribbon on a wire EDM document are #535.

Decisions the umbrella left open are in `docs/decisions/532-wire-contour.md` (no library tool, mitred outside corners, the 2 um cover tolerance, no arc fitting, lead shape, where each refusal stands, no CL format change).

## Readings

Synthetic condition `C110` (from no machine's manual): wire 0.250 mm, gap 0.040 mm. Profile: 40 x 20 mm, 2 mm corners in 3-degree facets.

| | wire-centre path, top side | distance to the profile |
|---|---|---|
| die | y = 9.835 | 0.165 inside |
| punch | y = 10.165 | 0.165 outside |
| apart | 0.330 | = kerf width (0.25 + 2 x 0.04) |

- On the straight sides the paths stand at the offset to 1e-9 mm in the motion test and 1e-6 mm through the commands (the model's silhouette in between). The nearest any path vertex comes to the profile is the offset to 1e-6 mm; the farthest is under 0.2 um past it (a 3-degree facet's mitre).
- A sharp 40 x 20 rectangle as a die: refused, "minimum inside radius is 0.1650 mm (wire radius 0.1250 + spark gap 0.0400)". The same rectangle as a punch: cut, with sharp path corners at (20.165, 10.165). A 0.1 mm fillet as a die: refused; a 0.2 mm fillet: cut.

## How tested

- `camcraft-motion` lib, `wire_edm::tests` (5): `a_die_and_a_punch_on_one_profile_stand_apart_by_exactly_the_kerf`, `a_corner_tighter_than_the_wire_is_refused_by_name`, `a_missing_or_misplaced_start_hole_is_refused_by_name`, `degenerate_profiles_and_numbers_are_refused_by_name`, `the_moves_ride_one_plane_with_no_pose_from_and_to_the_start_hole`.
- `camcraft-app` `wire_contour` (7): the family door both ways and no tool; the condition door at creation and edit; die and punch apart by the kerf through the commands, the machine check and the post's refusal; the corner and start-hole refusals at generation; the stamp reading the condition; undo / redo; the project round trip and the undefaulted side.
- `golden_cl`: `wire_contour_die_and_punch_match_golden` with `tests/golden/wire_contour_die.cl` and `wire_contour_punch.cl` (LF).
- `tool_law`: `every_kind_names_a_tool_set` now states the one exception (the wire family mounts none).
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` on the final head `13a12a25`: **green** - post, motion (195 passed), app (the whole suite, 285 test results, because a golden changed), ui (lib and 7 suites). The parents' `edm_machine` (7) and `edm_conditions` (6), `operations` (117) and `golden_cl` (26) are in that run.
- The first gate run was red: three registry pins (the kind count, two ribbon rows), the empty-rack tool refusal test, the UI tab law and the UI tip table. All were the new kind meeting laws that walk every kind; fixed in `cded9490`, and the second run is the green one.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- **Not exercised on a real EDM control.** The condition is synthetic; nothing here was cut.
- No wire post exists (#533), so no NC was written; the program gate refuses a wire cut by name.
- No verification of the wire against the part, the slug or the start hole's clearance (#534). The generator certifies only its own two laws (no move nearer the profile than the offset; no profile point the kerf misses).
- The page was only drawn by the registry-wide tab law test (every tab draws, one tab per field); no test clicks through it, and it was not looked at in the running app. On a wire EDM document the ribbon's Wire Contour cell creates a draft that the door refuses until a condition is named, and with an empty tool library the cell is disabled ("No tool yet") although the kind needs none - both #535.
- A picked-edge profile (a selection source) is wired the way the plasma profile's is but was only tested from a whole model's silhouette.
- A wire cut on a setup with an aligned part, carried stock or fixtures was not tested.

## Follow-ups filed

- #1108 `MCP: wire contour op` - `add_operation` requires a non-empty `tool`, and no headless way mounts a wire EDM with conditions yet, so the op is not reachable over MCP in this PR.
- #1109 open-profile contour (a cut-off or slot from the stock edge) - refused by name here.
- #1110 program sim, setup sheet and tool list still read a wire cut's empty tool name.

Changelog: Wire EDM: a Wire Contour operation cuts one closed profile at the kerf offset of the machine's condition (wire radius + spark gap), on a stated die or punch side, from a stated start hole; a corner the wire cannot cut and a missing start hole are refused by name (#532)

Effort: max (not escalated)

Fixes #532

title: feat(ui): original SVG operation icons and the SVG-to-PNG icon pipeline
body:
Slice 1 of #661: the SVG-to-PNG icon pipeline and the operation icons (checklist sections 1-3). Every `OpType` now has its own icon.

## What changed
- **Pipeline (`cargo xtask icons`, new `xtask/src/icons.rs`).** Each icon has an SVG master in `assets/ui/svg/*.svg`. The command rasterises it to the 32x32 PNG the UI already embeds (`assets/ui/<stem>.png`), and the PNGs are committed. `--check` re-renders every master and fails when a committed PNG differs from it (more than 8 per channel) or when a master breaks the house rules. `--sheet <out.png> [--px 16] [--zoom 4]` draws a contact sheet on a dark band and a light band so a person can look at the set. Rendering uses `resvg =0.45.1` (MIT OR Apache-2.0) with default features off. It is an **xtask-only** dependency: nothing new at runtime in the app or ui crates, and no `build.rs`. It reuses the lock's existing `tiny-skia 0.11`.
- **House rules (enforced by the lint):** Tabler conventions (`viewBox="0 0 24 24"`, no intrinsic size, round caps and joins, stroke 2 for the object and 1.5 for a toolpath/detail line), `currentColor` ink, shapes only (no image, script, text, style, href, `url(` or font). The loader still sets every pixel to white and lets alpha draw, so one PNG works in both themes.
- **41 original operation icons** (22 new, 5 stand-ins redrawn, 13 earlier originals redrawn, plus Trochoidal Slot and Plasma Profile, which are in the enum now). Each is drawn from what the operation does: a cutter and its path. Each family shares a frame: 2D in plan or section; multi-axis on a dome with the ball leaning on its normal; rotary on a bar with the tool riding the radial; every turning kind with a solid chuck block on the left.
- **Wiring.** `icons.rs` is now one macro table that generates the enum, `ALL`, the bytes and the texture keys (195 lines). `op_icon` moved out of the oversized `panes.rs` into a new `op_icons.rs` and maps every kind to its own slot; the old reuse law is retired. The turning section door now uses the Facing icon. Face is drawn in plan view, Facing in side view. The 18 PNGs nothing uses any more (13 earlier originals and 5 Tabler stand-ins) are deleted. `assets/ui/LICENSES.md` is updated: the op icons and their masters are ours, and the Tabler list excludes them.
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` -> 24 (main reads 23 after #1100) (`xtask/` is a process file). Fork note for #681: no action beyond the normal process sync; the new `icons` task needs `resvg` in the lock, which the synced `xtask/Cargo.toml` brings in.

## Icons by source
| Drawn original | Tabler |
|---|---|
| all 41 `op-*` icons (face, contour, pocket, adaptive2d, offset2d, slot, trochoidal-slot, trace, engrave, chamfer2d, deburr, circular, plasma-profile, drill, bore, thread, probe, pocket3d, finish3d, contour5d, parallel5d, swarf, advanced-swarf, rotary-contour, rotary-parallel, rotary-offset, multiaxis-rough, flow5d, multiaxis-contour, facing, profile-rough, profile-finish, groove-rough, groove-finish, part-off, threading, chamfering, taper-turning, multipass-turning, form-turning, boring-turning) | none new (the chrome icons are unchanged) |

Nothing comes from HSMWorks, Fusion or SolidCraft. SolidCraft's interface material has been under its own brand licence since upstream 312454f899 (recorded in the decision).

## Merged main (2026-11-12, about 55 merges)
- `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION`: conflict; now 24.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/structural.rs`: conflict. Kept main's new `ribbon_labels_whole_and_captions_painted` (#948). Main's version brings the file to 398 lines, so my `every_op_kind_has_its_own_svg_mastered_icon` moved, unchanged, into a new `tests/op_icon_table.rs`.
- `Cargo.lock`, `xtask/` (#965/#967 gate rework), `panes.rs`, `icons.rs`, `mod.rs`: merged without conflicts. `Cargo.lock` adds only `resvg` and its dependencies; existing entries changed only by gaining version suffixes (`png 0.18.1`, `kurbo 0.13.1`, `base64 0.13.1`), with no version moved. `OpType` on main has the same 41 kinds, so nothing new needed carrying into `op_icons.rs`.

## Decision
`docs/decisions/661-icon-set.md` covers the pipeline, the dependency, the house rules, the SolidCraft licence finding, and what was considered and dropped.

## How tested (pinning tests)
- xtask: `committed_icon_pngs_match_their_svg_masters` (every committed PNG matches a fresh render of its master), `lint_accepts_a_clean_master`, `lint_refuses_raster_scripts_text_and_external_refs`, `lint_refuses_off_grid_sizes_caps_and_weights`, `render_draws_ink_on_the_32_px_grid`. `cargo test -p xtask`: 38 passed.
- ui structural (`tests/op_icon_table.rs`): `every_op_kind_has_its_own_svg_mastered_icon` checks that every `KindInfo::ALL` kind maps to its own `op-*` icon with an SVG master, and that no two slots share a PNG.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui` (all suites, CWD `crates/ui`): green, lib 532 passed. `cargo clippy -p xtask -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -D warnings`: clean. `cargo xtask icons --check`: 0 breaches.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` falls back to **batch** because of the `Cargo.lock` change. The batch steps I did not run are the geometry/cl/tools/post/sim/motion/app suites. Their crates are untouched, and `resvg` only enters xtask's graph.
- Looked at: every icon at 32 px and the whole set at 16 px on dark and light (`cargo xtask icons --sheet sheet.png --px 16 --zoom 4`, and `--px 32 --zoom 2`).

## Least happy with
- **Thread milling**: the sawtooth hole walls are busy at 16 px.
- **Advanced Swarf**: a curved blade with the tool at two poses reads as "two tools" more than as "swarf, advanced".
- (Redrawn after review: Face is now a plan view with a serpentine raster, so it no longer echoes Facing; Groove Rough is the plunge comb with the blade lifted and Groove Finish the bare U finishing path, which now read apart at 16 px.)
- **5-axis Contour**: the ring arcs crowd the dome at 16 px.
- **Deburr**: a small ball on a broken corner; it is the subtlest icon in the set.

## Not exercised
Not seen in the running app (no GUI launch): the toolbar, tree rows and operation pages with the new textures.

## Snapshots
No file under `crates/ui/tests/snapshots/` is changed. The toolbar and tree icons will render differently in the release-lane pixel goldens (`egui_app*.png`), so those need the normal refresh at the next cut.

## Still owed on #661
Section 4 (tool types), 6 (tree rows), 7 (status badges), 8 (actions); section 5 (tabs) lands with #659.

Effort: high (not escalated)

Changelog: Every operation kind has its own original icon in the toolbar and the tree (turning, holes, 3D, multi-axis, 2D); icons are now SVG masters rasterised by `cargo xtask icons`. (#661)

Refs #661

title: feat(ui): the Setups page lists setups only; a setup's alignment, work offset, workholding and tools live on its own page
body:
## What changed
`setups_page` (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/pages.rs`) no longer repeats a setup's settings. Removed from the per-setup loop: Part alignment, Lay on a plane, three points, Axes in the plane, Work offset. Removed after the New setup row: the workholding section and the tool list. The no-setup branch (Create first setup + implicit workholding and tool list) is untouched.

Type: `feat` (new per-row control, changed page layout), not corrective only.

## What a user sees now
- **Setups page:** each setup row (name click-to-activate, "(active)", the one status line, **Open page**, Delete), the New setup row (Carry stock and WCS over + New setup), Export setup sheets, and a one-line pointer to the setup pages.
- **Setup<n> page:** unchanged; alignment, plane, points, axes and work offset on Settings, workholding on Fixtures, tool list on Tools.
- **Way in:** nothing on the Setups page opened a Setup<n> page (the name only activates; the browser's Setup<n> node opens it). Added a small **Open page** button per row: it sets the same `UiTarget::SetupNode(name, Settings)` the browser row does and focuses (activates) the setup via the browser's `focus()` helper, because the Fixtures and Tools pages only edit the active setup. No new command, no new state.
- `sheet_footer`'s hint is replaced by a truthful pointer; the old line about the Stock/Work offset pages is gone from this page.

## Tests
No existing test drove alignment or workholding through the Setups page (all already open `SetupNode`), so none needed re-pointing; the lib suite went from 536 to 538 passed (two new), none removed.
Pinning (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/setups_declutter.rs`):
- `the_setups_page_lists_setups_only_and_each_setup_page_keeps_its_settings`: two setups and a fixture; Setups page has 2 Delete, 2 Open page, New setup, Export, and none of Part alignment / Lay on a plane / Axes in the plane / Work offset / workholding / Tool list; Open page lands on Setup2 and activates it; each Setup<n> page (Settings, Fixtures, Tools) still shows them.
- `a_document_without_setups_keeps_its_implicit_sections_on_the_setups_page`.

Gate: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (538 ok), clippy -D warnings camcraft-ui, `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` green.

title: feat(app): work offsets post as an index bounded by the setup's own post (#931 slice 2)
body:
## What changed (slice 2 of 3: app)

Stacked on #1101 (slice 1), which stacks on #945. Fork synced at v0.18.0. Effort: high.

The app now hands the post the setup's 1-based work-offset index, not a word. The setup's own post sets the limit; core keeps only a sanity bound.

- **The stream carries the index.** `camcraft_post::post::Dump::wcs` is now a `u32`, where 1 is the first offset. `posting::wcs_context` returns `(index, origin)`. The post writes the word.
- **No fallback (triage point 2).** `setup::work_offset` no longer filters the stored pick. If a setup's post cannot express the stored offset, the offset is still never read as offset 1 or G54. That holds for the stream, the travel check, the label and the setup sheet.
- **Post-time gate.** New `setup_offsets::range_problems`, part of `verification_report`, so it applies to the single-file, per-mount and per-op posts. It checks each setup that has an operation against that setup's own post (`setup_mount::post_of`). An offset the post cannot express blocks the post, naming the setup and the post. Slice 1's engine refusal still runs behind it.
- **Command-time check.** `SetSetupWorkOffset::new` checks the pick against the setup's post (`setup_offsets::check`) and refuses by name.
- **Loader.** The six-offset cap is removed from `project/apply.rs`. Only the sanity bound remains (pick 0..=254, the `u8` that the height digest stores).
- **Names.** New `setup::work_offset_names(world, setup)` reads slice 1's `work_offsets(cps)` table. It is cached per (resolved post, script text) in a bounded map. `setup::offset_name`, `setup::wcs_name` and `setup::wcs_label` use it, and so do the setup sheet, the refusal texts, the spindle-law text and the shared-offset clause. The names are for display only and never go into the stream.
- **File format.** Offsets 1-6 are still saved as `G54`..`G59`, so existing files round-trip byte-identical. Offsets 7 and up are saved as their number. **Builds older than this one cannot open a file that uses offset 7 or higher.** The decision file records this for the release notes (point 8).
- **`WCS_SLOTS` is split (point 1).** It is now a crate-private `LEGACY_WCS_NAMES`, used only for legacy entity-name reservations and the pre-v52 and pre-v54 migrations. All of its word uses are gone.
- **`shared_word_problems` (point 7)** compares offset indexes and names the offset by the post's name.
- **UI and MCP** keep working through the app functions. The Setups combo still lists offsets 1-6, now named by the setup's post. MCP still accepts the words G54-G59. Slice 3 changes the combo and adds MCP's `index`.

## How tested

- Pinning tests in `crates/app/tests/wcs_index.rs`:
  - `offset_nine_on_a_six_offset_post_refuses_by_setup_name_and_never_posts_at_offset_one` (the no-fallback pin)
  - `the_command_refuses_an_offset_the_setups_post_cannot_express`
  - `the_setups_post_names_its_offsets`
  - `offset_seven_and_up_saves_as_its_number_and_reloads`
- Unit test: `project::wcs_pick::tests::legacy_words_and_numbers_round_trip`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green on 671ccd19: post suites, about 250 app suites including `wcs_index`, `setup_wcs`, `posting`, `probe_*`, `project_roundtrip` and `conformance`, the ui lib plus 11 ui suites. Wall time 9.6 min.
- I also ran 23 golden and post suites that the quick gate does not pick, including `golden_cl`, `carvera_post`, `heidenhain_*`, `tormach_post` and `lathe_post_*`. All pass, and no golden file changed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

## Not exercised

- No GUI hand check and no Hub run. The combo is unchanged apart from where its names come from.
- A user `.cps` file post with extended offsets was not tried by hand. It goes through the same cache path as the built-in posts.

Waits on #1101's Hub run. Like #1101, it merges at the next cut.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/931-wcs-index-app.md`.

Changelog: Work offsets are an index whose limit and names come from each setup's post. An offset the post cannot express is refused by setup name instead of posting at G54. Offsets 7 and up are saved as their number, and older builds cannot open those files. (#931)

title: fix(ui): the vise dialog says a setup needs its stock before a fit, and where the vise will land
body:
## What changed

The built-in vise dialog now tells the user what "Fit to the stock" needs before Place, and the no-stock refusals read in plain English. Per the maintainer's note on the issue, the wording says the vise grips the **stock** (the block the part is cut from), not the imported model.

- New app helper `vise_fit` (`fit` / `preview` / `has_stock` / `no_stock_message`): one derivation used by `InsertVise` and by the dialog's preview, so the two cannot disagree. The UI makes no world calls of its own beyond calling it.
- Dialog, setup with no stock body: notice + button "Open the Stock page" (same click path as the browser's Stock row), Fit greyed and off with a hover reason, position rows shown, Place by position works.
- Dialog, with a stock: one line that it grips the stock, plus where the vise lands and how far the jaws open (in the document unit); a stock wider than the vise's max opening is named up front. Place stays enabled (refusals stay refusals).
- New `CommandError::Needs(String)`, displayed as is. It is used only for the vise (no stock / stock too wide), mod vise pair and parallels refusals; `CommandError::Invalid` and every other command's text are unchanged.
- Browser: the Stock row's suffix reads `not set` while the setup's stock has no body.

## Texts (before / after)

- Vise: `vise not placed: invalid parameters: setup 'Setup1' has no stock to fit the vise to` -> `vise not placed: setup 'Setup1' has no stock yet, so there is nothing to fit the vise to - set the stock first (Stock page) - or place the vise by position instead`
- Mod vise: `... has no stock to fit the mod vise to` (with prefix) -> `the setup has no stock yet, so there is nothing to fit the mod vise to - set the stock first (Stock page)`
- Parallels: likewise `... nothing to fit the parallels under - set the stock first (Stock page)`
- Dialog notice: `This setup has no stock yet. A vise grips the stock - the block the part is cut from - not the imported model. Set the stock on the Stock page to fit the vise to it, or place the vise by position below.`
- With a stock: `Opens to 40.000 mm on the stock's Y width; the fixed jaw sits against the stock's +Y side (...), centred in X (...); the stock sits on the jaw floor (...).`

## Pinned by

- App: `vise_needs_stock` (`the_three_fits_name_the_missing_stock_and_the_stock_page`, `the_preview_is_the_commands_own_fit`, `a_stock_wider_than_the_vise_is_refused_up_front_and_by_the_command`).
- UI (structural, no pixels): `fixture_vise_stock_tests` (notice, greyed Fit, Stock page button and its target, position rows, Place by position, landing line with a stock, too-wide stock, queued refusal text, `Stock  not set` row).
- Removed `a_refused_vise_is_named_in_the_dialog` (its Place click now places by position); the refusal is covered by the queued-command test above.
- Also run green: builtin_vise, mod_vise, mod_vise_plate, builtin_accessory, mcp_vise, mcp_mod_vise, mcp_accessory, self_centering_vise, mcp_self_centering_vise, fixtures, ui `structural`, `setup_tree`; clippy -D warnings on camcraft-app and camcraft-ui.

## Not exercised

Not seen on screen - only the kittest harness was run (nothing launched). Layout, wrapping of the long notice and the greyed look are unverified by eye. Opening the Stock page for a dialog setup other than the active one activates it, as the browser row does. No snapshot PNG touched. Decisions: `docs/decisions/1105-vise-needs-stock.md`.

Changelog: The built-in vise dialog says a setup needs its stock before a fit and where the vise will land; the no-stock refusals read in plain English; the browser shows `Stock  not set` (#1105, PR #1111)

title: feat(post): work offsets ride the stream as a 1-based index; the post writes the word
body:
Slice 1 of 3 for #931: the post crate and scripts. Stacked on #945 (#934, Sinumerik G505/G506). Fork synced at v0.18.0. Effort: high.

**This changes the post interface** (what every script receives as `PARAM WorkOffset`), so it waits on a Hub run before it is flagged ready.

## What changed

- **The stream carries the index.** `dump` writes `PARAM WorkOffset` as the setup's 1-based offset number (`G55` -> `2`). App still hands the word and still caps at 6; slice 2 makes the `Dump` field an index.
- **New `workOffsetIndex` manifest flag** (`crates/post/src/post/work_offset.rs`, on the `coolantModes` pattern). It is read once at load with `workOffsetMax` (6 when unstated):
  - A flagged script receives the number. The engine refuses an offset above its maximum by setup name.
  - An unflagged (user) script receives the word `G54`..`G59` for 1-6, exactly as before. Any offset above 6 is refused by setup name, and an unflagged script cannot raise its own maximum.
  - The legacy words `G54`..`G59` in a stream still read as 1-6. Any other value (`G53`, 0, 2.5, `G54.1 P3`) is refused by setup name before a script sees it.
  - `work_offset::work_offsets(cps)` returns the maximum and the `workOffsetName(n)` names for slice 2's display. It never feeds the stream.
- **All 11 shipped scripts** declare the flag, `workOffsetMax` and `workOffsetName`, and map the index to their own word. No `slotOf` / `frameWord` / `frameOf` word parsing remains:
  - The Fanuc-family probe register reads `wcsIndex - 1`.
  - Sinumerik's `$P_UIFR[n]` uses the number directly.
  - Heidenhain maps offset n to preset row n.
- **Declared maxima:**
  - Tormach mill and Tormach lathe: **9** (`G59.1`..`G59.3`, cited to the LinuxCNC G-code reference: "G54-G59.3 Select Coordinate System (1 - 9)" and its G10 L2 table).
  - Every other dialect: **6**. Haas G154, Fanuc/Mazak/Doosan G54.1 P and further Sinumerik/Heidenhain frames or rows were not verified against a public manual, so none is written. Reasons and sources are in `docs/decisions/931-wcs-index-post.md`.
- **Docs.** `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` documents the 1-based `WorkOffset` beside the probe's 0-based `SetWorkOffset` (triage point 4). `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` describes the flag, the maximum and the name function.

## Tests

- New `crates/post/tests/work_offset_index.rs` (9 tests). Every shipped script runs on recorded streams at offsets 1, 6, 7, its maximum and one past it, checking the word it writes or the refusal by setup name. It also covers:
  - a recorded generator toolpath (`face_square_40x40.cl`) through Fanuc and Tormach;
  - legacy word streams posting byte-identically to their index;
  - invalid values;
  - an unflagged user script at 1-6 and at 7, and one that tries to raise its maximum;
  - a flagged script without a maximum or names;
  - the dump writing the index;
  - each script's name table.
- `sinumerik_work_offsets::sinumerik_refuses_a_work_offset_that_names_no_settable_frame` now expects the engine's refusal of `G53` (the engine refuses it before the script runs).
- Gate (local, worktree target, sccache), on head `2fe7afb7`:
  - `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: 75 passed, 0 failed.
  - 63 app suites, 431 passed, 0 failed. They cover every app suite that posts through the shipped scripts: conformance, golden_cl, posting, arc_planes, cli, the probe_* suites, sinumerik_*, heidenhain_*, fanuc_post, doosan_dnm_post, carvera_*, tormach_*, the lathe_post* suites, plasma_*, inverted_*, comment_escape, one_wcs, setups, setup_wcs, setup_defines_wcs, rotated_wcs, setup_mounts_post, setup_post_options, per_op_files, program_comments, smoothing, after_op, coolant*, post_unit_word, regression_models, wear_comp, control_comp and lathe_spindle_law. There are no separate mazak or haas suites; those scripts are covered by conformance, fanuc_post and the inverted_* suites.
  - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- 400-line law: the new manifest reading lives in its own module, `work_offset.rs`. `engine.rs` (511 -> 530 lines) and `js.rs` (409 -> 415) were already over 400 and grew only by the hook-up.

**Goldens:** no golden file changed. Offsets 1-6 post the same words as before.

**Not exercised:** the GUI and MCP (unchanged in this slice), a real control, and offsets above 6 end to end through app (app still caps at 6 until slice 2).

Changelog: Posts receive the work offset as a 1-based number and write their own word; the Tormach mill and lathe posts accept work offsets 7-9 (G59.1-G59.3), and a post that cannot express an offset refuses it by setup name (#931, slice 1)

title: feat(tools): .camtools carries the tool body; "Import tool holders" toggle
body:
## What changed

- **Format (`crates/app/src/tool_library.rs`)**: a `.camtools` tool's `definition` may carry `body`, the same `ToolBodyDto` a `.camproj` tool stores (a drawn holder profile, a placed mesh, or a lathe holder). The key is additive: `camcraft-tools/1` stays, files without it read unchanged, and older builds ignore it. Export writes the body of every tool that has one. On read, a body is checked the way the project loader checks one: `ToolBodyDto::to_body` re-derives it and `tool_body::fits` must accept it. If either refuses, the whole file is refused and the tool is named. The clean-room note stays as it was.
- **Command (`commands/tool_import.rs`)**: `ImportTools::with_holders(world, library, holders)` is still one undoable command. `ImportTools::new` is the same call with holders on. With holders on, each body is checked again at command creation. With holders off, every tool lands bare (holder cylinder only). The duplicate and rename rules are unchanged. The body counts toward "identical" only when one lands: a bare library tool matches the document's tool on its record alone, as before, and a tool that lands with a body must match the body too, otherwise it arrives as "Name (2)". `ImportReport` gains `holders` and `holders_left_out`, and both appear on the status line.
- **UI (Tool library page)**: an "Import tool holders" checkbox next to Import library, ticked by default. It is passed to the command as its `holders` parameter and remembered per user in the prefs file (`importToolHolders`, written only when off), the same way as #877. It is not project state and not on the history.
- **MCP**: `import_tool_library` takes an optional `holders` boolean (default true). The schema and description are updated, and the reply adds `holders` and `holders_left_out`. The script verb `cam.importTools(path)` keeps its arity (holders on).
- **Process**: the `import_tool_library` line in the camcraft-mcp skill is updated, so `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` goes 16 -> 17. Other open process PRs also claim 17-20; whichever merges later takes the next number when it merges main.

title: fix(thread): a matched thread mill verifies clean - the gouge laws read its major circle
body:
#1071: a Thread op's helix runs the thread depth H = 0.5413 x pitch past the declared hole, which is the thread's minor circle (what CAD draws of a tapped hole), by design (`machining2d::thread_mill`). The verify read that hole as a wall the cutter must keep `r` from, so every matched thread mill was blocked.

That covered the stock source too, which the issue thought was unaffected: the same thread from `SrcRef::Stock` had 52 gouges and 21 crossing pairs. `mill2d_c` never asserted the warnings, so no thread mill could post from any source.

Fork synced at v0.18.0, PROCESS_VERSION 29; merged with upstream main at 62a2c93a (head ea76d5df).

## What changed

Three laws convicted a matched thread, and each is fixed narrowly.

- **Law (b), the rim.** The Thread arm now moves each declared hole's rim out to the major circle (declared radius + H), after the region is built (`material_source::major_rims`). This covers every source and the area-controlled region. A loop that is the hole's minor rim (ours, or the model's own for a through hole) gives way to it; every other wall stays.
- **The containment solid law.** It read the model's minor wall, and the face the hole opens through, as part to keep. A new `sim::verify::thread_bore` (and `solid_hits_threaded`) excuses a hit only when both of these hold:
  - the facet is the thread's own material: the minor wall (near-vertical, every vertex on the declared circle within max(2 % r, 0.1 mm)), or a facet with a vertex on that circle lying wholly at or above the hole's entry (the mouth);
  - the swept cutter stays inside the major cylinder: the farther tip end's radius plus the atom's radius is at most the major radius plus the allowance.

  Floors, walls of another radius, other holes and any cut past the major circle still convict. `solid_hits` is unchanged: it calls the threaded form with no bores.

  **Since the review of f122474d:** the band only RECOGNISES the wall. The cap reads the hit facet's own radius about the axis (its nearest on-circle vertex) plus the thread depth plus the allowance, not the declared major circle. A hole declared wider than, or off the centre of, the model's hole by more than the allowance now convicts. `major_rims` likewise grows a through hole's major circle from the model's own rim loop when that stands nearer than the declared circle.
  **Since the review of 434a464a:** the wall is measured at the facet's (or rim loop's) nearest point to the axis, not its nearest vertex. A chord between two on-circle vertices dips inside the circle.
  - That nearest point must itself be on the band, so a D-bore's flat, a coarse polygon's side, or a step reaching inside the mouth is never the thread's material.
  - The wall stands at that point, credited at most `CHORD_CREDIT` (the sim's `DEV_TOL`, 0.01 mm) toward its nearest vertex. That is tessellation of a round hole: the STEP importer meshes at half of it.
  - `major_rims` reads the same way. It moved with `thread_bores` into `operation/thread_rims.rs`, so `material_source.rs` stays at main's 350 lines.
- **Law (a), crossings.** The retract runs the ride backwards at feed. The reversed arcs put their chord joints a last bit off their twins, and `proper_cross` excused a touch only at an exactly zero orientation. So each shared joint, and each collinear overlap, read as a crossing.

  Now chords that only touch (an endpoint within 1 nm of the other chord's line) are no crossing. A real crossing keeps every endpoint off the other line. This is the one change that reaches every operation's verify, so the whole batch tier was run (below). A parallel-only guard was tried first: it removed 5 of the 21 pairs, and the rest were the joint touches.
- Two functions now take eight arguments (`SolidIndex::hits`, `contain_into`). They carry `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` with a reason, as ten others in `sim` already do.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1071-thread-mill-rim.md`.

## How it was tested

New pinning tests:
- `crates/app/tests/thread_mill_rim.rs` (a 6 mm Tap-form thread mill, pitch 1, model-sourced unless named):
  - `a_matched_thread_mill_in_air_verifies_clean`: the issue's cavity fixture (#1073's block). Before the fix: 52 gouges and 21 crossing pairs.
  - `a_matched_thread_mill_in_a_drilled_hole_verifies_clean`: a block with a real r 5 blind hole, 96-gon. Before the fix: the gouges came back from the solid law at the wall and the mouth.
  - `a_stock_sourced_thread_mill_verifies_clean_too`.
  - `a_thread_whose_major_circle_reaches_a_wall_convicts`: the major circle is 0.24 mm into the cavity wall; the minor circle is clear of it.
  - `a_thread_declared_wider_than_the_models_hole_convicts`: the model drilled r 4.5, declared r 5.
  - `a_thread_taken_below_the_models_hole_floor_convicts`: floor declared at Z 9, model floor at Z 10.
  - `a_declared_hole_wider_than_the_models_by_a_hair_convicts` (review round): r 5.05 / 5.1 on r 5, r 15.25 on r 15, and a through hole. It failed on f122474d.
  - `a_declared_hole_off_the_models_centre_by_a_hair_convicts` (review round): centres 0.05 / 0.1 / 0.28 mm off, blind and through. It failed on f122474d.
  - `a_matched_thread_stays_clean_at_other_sizes_and_through` (review round): matched r 15, a matched through hole, and a 5 um off-centre declaration.
  - `a_flat_whose_corners_stand_on_the_circle_convicts` (third review): a D-bore (flat from (3, 4) to (-3, 4)), an octagon and a 16-gon on r 5, and a through octagon. The D-bore verified with no warning on 434a464a, which was checked.
  - `a_fine_polygon_bore_still_verifies_clean` (third review): 48 and 96 sides on r 5.
