title: feat(mcp): rename_operation and reorder_operation (closes #45)
body:
Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a).

## What changed

#45's GUI scope had already landed in earlier PRs: rename, saved order and drag and drop within a setup (PR #58, v0.12.0), the Setups ribbon cell and the always-present Setups browser row (#322, `fb957ec`), and each setup's operations grouped under its own browser node (#343). What was still owed was the agent surface: `RenameOperation` and `ReorderOperation` had no MCP tool (AGENTS.md "Commands ship with an MCP tool"). This PR adds them, which closes #45.

- `crates/app/src/mcp/order_tools.rs` (new):
  - `rename_operation {name, new_name}`: changes the display name only. The stable key and the program position stay the same, and renaming back to the key clears the label.
  - `reorder_operation {name, target, place: "before"|"after"}`: the drag and drop's own model. It moves an operation next to another one in the same setup, refuses a move to another setup, and answers with that setup's new order.
  - Both resolve operations by key or display name (`edit::find_op`) and run the existing undoable commands through the session History, so each is one undo step. Every construction-time refusal (a taken name, shadowing another op's key, another setup, already in place) comes back as a tool error.
- `crates/app/src/mcp/{mod,tools}.rs`: the module is registered and its table is chained into `tools::all()`.
- `docs/decisions/45-op-order-mcp.md`: the shape choices and what was dropped.

Posting, simulation and rest-machining order semantics do not change. The tools write the same `OperationMeta.order` the browser drag writes, and `setup::operation_order` still ranks setups first. There are no project-file or post-output changes.

## How tested

Pinning tests in the new binary `crates/app/tests/mcp_order.rs`:
- `rename_and_reorder_are_listed_with_their_schemas`
- `reorder_moves_within_its_setup_one_undo_step_and_refuses_another_setup`: two setups. A move within Setup1 keeps Setup2's op last, each move is one undo/redo step, and a cross-setup move, a no-op, a bad `place` and an unknown name are each refused with the order left as it was.
- `rename_keeps_the_key_and_the_order_and_round_trips`: the key and order are unchanged, other tools find the op by its new name, a duplicate label, another op's key and a blank name are refused, save -> open in a fresh session keeps the label and order, and undo restores the key as the name.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: green - 19 app suites + lib (all `app::mcp` gate-mapped suites incl. the new `mcp_order`), 0 failed, 0.4 min; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib --test mcp_order -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- Pause / Home program entries (#155) can't be addressed by these tools, because the MCP surface does not expose entries yet.
- The camcraft-mcp skill's tool table is not updated. It is a process file and would bump PROCESS_VERSION in a feature PR; its SKILL.md names `tools::list()` as the live registry.
- No GUI change, so there are no UI or snapshot changes.

Changelog: MCP gains `rename_operation` and `reorder_operation`: rename an operation's display name and move it within its setup, each one undo step, over the same commands as the browser (#45)

Effort: high (not escalated)

Fixes #45

title: fix(sim): judge and draw a necked tool at its drawn neck
body:
## What changed

A necked tool was judged as its full shank cylinder by every stack law, so reach and fixture checks refused or warned about cuts the real tool makes. The drawn cutter outline (`ToolCutter`, #93 slice 2) now feeds the shank band of the stack laws and the simulated tool, **only where it is narrower than the stated shank, never wider**.

- **tools**: new `neck` module. `neck::neck_bands(tool, spun)` reads the outline's own conservative bands (`SpunProfile::bands`) over the shank span (flute top to stickout). Each band is capped at the stated shank radius, any gap is filled at that radius, and the bands are merged to `MAX_BANDS` (merging only grows a band). The result is empty when the outline no longer `agrees` with the numbers or narrows nowhere. `HolderStack` gains a `neck` field. `HolderStack::shank_bands(g)` returns the exact old `(flute_len, shank_len, shank_radius)` band unless a neck fits `g`: contiguous, finite, never wider than the shank, at most `MAX_BANDS` bands. Each neck band is widened to any holder-body band beside it.
- **sim**: the shank band in laws c/c3 (`reach`), c2 (`laws`), d2 (`stack_span::upper_bands`), the posed sweep (`posed_steel`), the mesh law (`mesh_steel::steel_stack`) and the solid law's atoms (`Cutter::atoms`) now comes from `shank_bands`. `Cutter` carries the neck as `NeckBands` (fixed capacity, so it stays `Copy`). `Cutter::judged` drops a neck that no longer fits the geometry.
- **app**: `tool_cutter::neck_of` computes the neck against the stored tool record. It feeds `tool_body::stack(..).with_neck(..)` at the three existing seams: generation (`GenJob.neck`), the post gate's `fixture_struck::op_hits`, and `sim_tool_body::for_operation`. The simulation's cutter meridian is drawn from those same bands. A drawn neck now enters the op stamp (`tool_cutter::digest`, which writes bytes only when a neck exists, so no other stamp moves). The doc comments and the MCP `set_tool_cutter_profile` description no longer call the drawn cutter "display only".

## Readings and safety

- A tool with no drawn cutter, or a drawn cutter with no neck, judges and draws bit-identically: the very same band tuple is produced.
- If a neck is absent, fails `agrees`, or is degenerate, the stated cylinder is used. The tool is never judged narrower than its drawn outline or a body standing beside the shank.
- Drill reach (`operation::drill_reach`, which reads the holder face, not the shank radius), the probe stylus (`probe_op::stylus_cutter`, its own single body band) and multi-axis tilt avoidance (`motion::multiaxis::avoid`, generator side) do not share this seam. They stay on the stated cylinder, which is conservative, and are left to #842.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/app/tests/tool_neck_laws.rs` (new):
  - `a_necked_tool_clears_steel_its_shank_cylinder_strikes`: post gate fixture law, Ø8 neck vs Ø10 shank, 4.5 mm off; undo brings the strike back.
  - `a_drawn_cutter_with_no_neck_judges_bit_identically`: fixture verdicts and sim outline unchanged.
  - `the_reach_laws_cutter_carries_the_neck_and_no_neck_reads_the_cylinder`: `Cutter` used by laws c/c3 and the solid law; a misfitting neck is dropped.
  - `the_simulation_draws_the_neck`
- `crates/tools/src/neck_tests.rs` (new, 6 unit tests): neck bands, catalog tools carry no neck, a disagreeing outline is dropped, cylinder bit-for-bit, misfits fall back, a body beside the neck widens it.
- `tool_cutter_profile::a_drawn_cutter_lands_undoes_and_moves_the_stamp_only_by_its_neck`: renamed and updated. A drawn neck now moves the stamp; a drawn cutter with no neck still does not.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): green - tools, sim, motion, app and ui suites all ok (13.9 min wall); `cargo clippy -p camcraft-tools -p camcraft-sim -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean.

## Not exercised

- No end-to-end generation test in which law (c) against rest material acquits a deep necked cut. The reach law reads the `Cutter` seam, which is pinned directly.
- No UI snapshot changes. The tool editor already draws the drawn outline; the simulation mesh change is covered structurally by `the_simulation_draws_the_neck`.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/852-necked-tool-envelope.md`.

Changelog: The collision/reach checks and the simulated tool now read a tool's drawn neck where it is narrower than the stated shank, so a necked tool is no longer refused for steel its neck clears (no drawn neck: unchanged).

Effort: high (no escalation). Fork synced at v0.17.0.

Fixes #852

title: fix(motion): adaptive growth overload fallback compares whole revolutions
body:
Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a).

## What changed

`Planner::step_search` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/adaptive/grow.rs`): when no growth step holds the load, the fallback used to pick the least overload from the tries' readings. Those readings stop at the first point past the bound (`walk_until`). Where the overload comes before the step-dependent front, every try reads the same, the first and largest step wins the tie, and that step is then walked whole far past the reading it was picked on (#7 round 10, island NE corner: picked at 59.5 deg, cut at 125 deg).

Now the fallback keeps each overloaded try's ring and revolution, but drops its partial stock. `least_whole` walks each revolution whole again from the planner's stock, largest step first. A smaller step replaces the kept one only when its whole reading is more than 2 % lower (`SLACK`, the tie tolerance the old fallback already used). Each re-walk stops early once it can no longer win. The kept revolution reuses the stock and reading from its whole walk, so it is not walked a third time.

**#13 growth budget:** the re-walks are not charged as growth work, and `WORK_MAX`, `GEOM_MAX` and `GEOM_LEN` are unchanged. Each trial already charges its revolution's whole length (`add_len`) before its walk is cut short. The re-walk adds no new revolution and rebuilds no geometry: it reads revolutions already paid for in full, at most once each and usually only part way. The held fix e4039ef0 called the trial again instead, which rebuilt the offsets and charged length and vertices a second time; that is part of why its island run reached 61,971 r. The full reasoning is in `docs/decisions/845-adaptive-overload-fallback.md`.

## Readings

Release `hsm_one` over all six `adaptive_hsm` fixtures, run with this fix and with upstream's `grow.rs`:

| fixture | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| bore R12.5, rectangle 60x40, L-pocket, narrow slot 14x60, channel 22x60 | - | identical report lines (max deg, breaks, cut/air lengths, move counts, notes) |
| island 60x40, 12x12 | HSM refused by law 3 after 109 revolutions (~600.0 k vertices, ~9.4 k r); Offset rings | HSM refused by law 3 after 118 revolutions (~606.4 k vertices, ~9.5 k r); Offset rings - identical posted path |

On the island, the smaller steps now kept in the overloaded corners mean more revolutions before the existing geometry law refuses the plan (118 instead of 109). The refusal and the Offset-rings path it falls back to do not change. No other fixture's output moves.

**Goldens moved: none.** No committed CL/NC golden comes from the adaptive planner (`crates/app/tests/golden/` has no HSM/adaptive file), and no snapshot PNG is touched.

## How tested

- Pinning test: `machining2d::adaptive::grow::tests::the_overload_fallback_keeps_the_least_whole_reading_not_a_truncated_tie` (camcraft-motion lib). Two overloaded revolutions share a 3 mm side-cut start past the bound. Walked to the bound, their readings are exactly equal (the old tie, which the larger step won). Walked whole, the larger step turns into fresh stock and reads much more, so the test asserts the smaller step is kept with its whole reading. Plus `a_near_tie_keeps_the_larger_step_and_nothing_tried_keeps_nothing`.
- Quick gate `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: motion lib + adaptive_band + adaptive_hsm + pocket3d_hsm, all green (33 s).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Release heavy lanes: `adaptive_hsm --ignored` (full-resolution report, island refused in seconds, channel trochoid fallback, small-helix rectangle) and the lib's `budget::fixtures::the_fixtures_that_grow_today_stay_under_the_geometry_budget`: green.
- Debug camcraft-app adaptive suites (pocket3d_hsm, roughing2d, shoulder_adaptive, pocket_overhead, whole_model_pocket): all green (18 passed; 1 was already ignored).

## Not exercised

- The island fixture with the budget lifted (the issue's evidence run): the island is still refused by law 3 before its NE corner is grown, so the 125 deg corner overload no longer shows up in any posted path on main. The pinning test covers the mechanism directly.
- The batch and release tiers.

Changelog: Adaptive clearing's growth spiral, where no step holds the load, now cuts the step whose whole revolution overloads least, not the largest step on a tie read before the overload (#845)

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #845

title: fix(post): cap a feed that turns a rotary at the machine's stated rates
body:
**Changes posted G-code: waits on a Hub run before it is flagged ready.**

Fork synced at v0.17.0 (branch cut from upstream/main f490458a). Effort: high (safety floor: posted G-code; no escalation).

## What changed
- **One shared rule** - `crates/post/src/post/rotary_cap.rs` (new, appended to the prelude every `.cps` sees): `rotaryRate(letter)` (stated feed speed, else rapid, deg/min), `rotaryFeedCap(f, lin, turns, mode)`, `rotaryFeed(p, prev, letters, mode, arc)` and `rotaryFeedWord(v)`. It caps F so no rotary runs past its stated rate and no linear part past `feedRateMax`, read the way the control reads F:
  - **path** - `fanuc.cps` and `doosan-dnm.cps` under G43.4. F is the tool tip's speed relative to the work, with the rotaries carried along (FANUC 30i-B operator's manual, tool center point control): F <= rate x tip / |d|. With the tip still, F <= the rate.
  - **composite** - `doosan-dnm.cps` on a 4th axis without TCP, and `fanuc-lathe.cps` C-axis live tooling (#860). The control times the block over sqrt(lin^2 + sum d^2), counting degrees as mm (FANUC 0i-F operator's manual, feedrate for rotation axes). `fanuc-lathe.cps` `liveMove` now calls the shared rule instead of its own copy.
  - **Arcs** that turn a rotary use the path rule over the chord in the arc's plane. That chord is never longer than any reading of an arc's F, so the cap is never too loose.
- A capped F is floored to 0.1 mm/min. A cap under 0.1 mm/min is refused by name.
- The post now tracks the angles the control holds (`rotAt`), taken only from the A/B/C words it actually wrote. If a feed turns a rotary from an angle the post never wrote, and that rotary states a rate, the post refuses it by name: `a feed that turns A from an angle the post does not know - the stated A rate cannot be held`. Each rate refusal is counted once per program.
- An unstated rate caps nothing (the unstated-limit law).
- `tormach.cps` needs no cap: it writes A only on a G0 index and refuses an A that changes inside an operation (#785). haas, mazak, sinumerik, heidenhain and carvera refuse every tilted record.
- The decisions are recorded in `docs/decisions/885-rotary-feed-cap.md`.

## How tested
New pinning suite `crates/app/tests/rotary_feed_cap.rs`. It reads every posted motion block back, keeps the axes modal, and checks every feed block that turns A against the stated rates under that dialect's reading:
- `fanuc_tcp_feed_holds_the_stated_a_rate` (pins `A30 F3.3`, `A60 F1000` and the uncapped `A61 F2000`)
- `doosan_tcp_feed_holds_the_stated_a_rate`
- `doosan_fourth_axis_composite_feed_holds_the_stated_a_rate` (also pins the refusal when no A word was ever written)
- `an_unstated_rate_caps_nothing`
- `a_feed_turning_from_an_unknown_angle_is_refused_by_name`

The lathe stays pinned by `c_axis_unwind::a_lower_stated_rate_posts_a_lower_feed` and its golden, which did not change.

Gate (local, macOS, debug):
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post`: all suites green.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` plus the 44 post-touching binaries: all green, 377 tests. The binaries are arc_planes, c_axis_live, c_axis_unwind, comment_escape, conformance, control_comp, coolant_followups, doosan_dnm_post, drill_prior, drill_rplane, fanuc_post, fourth_axis_pose, heidenhain_cycles, inverted_equivalence/post/probe, lathe_*, machine_library, plasma_*, post_unit_word, probe_*, program_comments, program_entry, rotary_feed_cap, turning_face_approach, vertical_arc_entry, wear_comp, tilt, rotary_verify, tormach_fourth_axis, microarc_test_part, tormach_machines and posting.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Goldens moved
**None.** No committed golden states a rotary rate on a tilted feed. The lathe's C-axis goldens (`c_axis_unwind.nc`, `c_axis_helix.nc`) are byte-identical through the shared rule.

## Test fixture changed
`fourth_axis_pose.rs` `tilted()` now opens with a rapid at the pose before its two feeds. Under the new refusal, its feeds would otherwise turn the shipped DNM 5700's rated A from an angle the post never placed. The tests' own assertions are unchanged.

## Not exercised
- No Hub run or machine cut yet.
- G93 inverse time is not implemented (see the decision file).
- Under G43.4 the machine's linear axes also make a compensating move that depends on the pivot length. No machine file states that length, so the control's own per-axis clamp covers it. The post caps the tip at `feedRateMax`.

Found while working this: #950 (P0). doosan-dnm without TCP assumes A0 at program start and after a tool change, so an A0 section after an A30 section posts no A word. This PR does not fix that output. With a rated A, it now refuses such a feed by name.

Changelog: Posts cap the feed of a block that turns a rotary at the machine's stated rotary rate and linear feed (fanuc, doosan-dnm, fanuc-lathe through one shared rule), refusing by name when the starting angle is unknown (#885)

Fixes #885

title: fix(post): Sinumerik writes work offsets 5/6 as G505/G506
body:
## What changed

`assets/posts/sinumerik.cps` wrote the engine's generic work-offset word verbatim, so a setup on offset 5 or 6 opened each section with `G58` / `G59`. On the 840D those are axial programmable offsets, not settable frames (Siemens 840D sl Fundamentals: settable zero offsets `G54`..`G57`, then `G505`..`G599`) - the program would run in the wrong frame or alarm.

- New `frameWord` in the script maps the setup's word to the control's: `G54`..`G57` unchanged, `G58` -> `G505`, `G59` -> `G506`. A word naming no settable frame is refused by name (counted warning, blocks the post).
- The probing result that sets an offset goes through the same mapping, so a probe asked to set offset 6 now writes `$P_UIFR[6,..]` and re-selects `G506` (it was refused before, since the script knew `G59` was no frame). An offset past six never reaches the post: the stream parser already refuses `FOUND SET` past G59.
- The setup stays the one source of truth (`setup::wcs_slot`); only the word this post writes changes. No other post, no golden changes (no golden covered offsets 5/6 on this post).
- Decision (write G505/G506 rather than refuse): `docs/decisions/934-sinumerik-g505.md`.

## How tested

Pinning tests:
- `sinumerik_work_offsets::sinumerik_posts_offsets_one_to_six_as_their_settable_frames` - posts sections on all six `WCS_SLOTS` words; asserts `G54 G55 G56 G57 G505 G506` in the opening blocks and no `G58`/`G59` word anywhere.
- `sinumerik_work_offsets::sinumerik_refuses_a_work_offset_that_names_no_settable_frame`
- `probe_dialects::sinumerik_sets_the_sixth_offset_as_frame_g506` (replaces `sinumerik_refuses_setting_g59_by_name`, whose behaviour this fix deliberately changes)

Gate: quick on head 26e8610e green - `app probe_dialects (1 fn)` ok, `app sinumerik_work_offsets (2 fn)` ok. Batch on the first commit (d9cd719c): geometry, tools, post, sim, motion suites and clippy -D warnings green; app suites failed only on a probe pin I then dropped (unreachable - the stream parser refuses a slot past G59 first); two failures not from this diff: ui `theme_files` (known main-side) and cl `headless_bin::cl_bin_prints_move_stats` (expects `arcs 30`, reads `arcs 33` on `contour_disc_hole.cl`; crates/cl is untouched here).

## Not exercised

Not run on a real 840D or a simulator. **This changes posted G-code, so it waits on a Hub run before it is flagged ready.** The posted word is pinned at the script seam (engine + `sinumerik.cps`), not through a full setup post with the Sinumerik machine selected.

Effort: high (no escalation)
fork synced at v0.17.0 (branched from upstream/main)

Changelog: Siemens 840D post writes work offsets 5 and 6 as the settable frames G505 / G506 instead of G58 / G59 (programmable offsets on that control); a probe can now set offset 6

Fixes #934

title: feat(kernel): STEP import through solidcore-step behind the seam, benched against truck
body:
M12.1 stage 4 (#916): a STEP importer on the solidcore side of the kernel seam, and the dual-importer bench against truck-stepio. **Bench only** - `crates/app` still imports STEP through truck; truck and ruststep stay. Everything is inside `crates/kernel`; no other workspace crate gains a dependency.

## What changed

- **Pin.** `crates/kernel` takes `solidcore`, `solidcore-step` and `solidcore-convert` from `https://github.com/NeoTech/solidcore` at `rev = "55d0e7638b9e1ebbf91ab8c10657e595c114ecda"` (the fork's tag `camcraft-pin-2026-11-11`) in place of crates.io `solidcore = "=1.0.1"`. `solidcore-ops` and `solidcore-record` come with them; `solidcore-tess` at the same rev is a dev-dependency. `Cargo.lock`: 6 git packages (`solidcore`, `-convert`, `-ops`, `-record`, `-step`, `-tess`) replace the 1 registry package (552 -> 557), no new crates.io package (an earlier version of this text said 5 and 556: counted before the dev-dependency was added). The lock diff touches only those packages and camcraft-kernel's own dependency list.
- **Against 1.0.1** (the pin is 2973 commits past the `solidcore-v1.0.1` tag; the seam's library code compiled unchanged): `Brep` is no longer `Clone` (two test helpers now copy with `brep_copy` or measure in place); the port now refuses a NaN offset distance; the native reader now refuses blank, foreign, noise and header-only files itself. Five pinned port verdicts re-triaged - all were findings against the port, now closed by it.
- **Importer** (`camcraft_kernel::solidcore_step`): `read_step` (every solid item, refused ones with stage and reason, the file's length units, notes) and `import_step` (a model only when every solid item came through). 64 MiB size bound; the caller's `CancelToken` is the time bound (new `KernelError::TimedOut`), polled by the parser, between solids and inside the kernel's loops; panics caught. The stage-3 laws apply unchanged (integrity, closed manifold solid, vertex gap <= 1e-3 mm). A length unit the reader cannot convert is refused by the seam (the reader alone reads it as millimetres, silently).
- **Bench** (`tests/step_agreement.rs`): every `.step` under `testdata/models` through both importers; verdicts pinned; a fixture with no row fails.
- **Corrupt corpus** (`tests/step_import.rs`): 19 files made from box.step through both importers, each under a 60 s bound that cancels the import.

## Readings

| File | Unit (mm) | Importers | solidcore-tess mesh |
|---|---|---|---|
| box.step, empty_list.step (#887), tool_csys_box_iso13399.step | 1 | agree | watertight, within tolerance |
| sample_ap214.step (metre, 3 solids) | 1000 | agree | watertight, within tolerance |
| Milling-test.step, Milling-test-inch.step | 1 / 25.4 | **disagree: bounding box** | watertight, within tolerance |
| tool_csys_none / _iso13399 / _degenerate (no solid) | 1 | both refuse by name | - |

The disagreement: the port's "tight" box of Milling-test is Y -30..30; the part is a disc with a flat at Y = 19.719 (file vertices, truck's mesh and solidcore's own mesh all agree). Volume and area agree to 1.2e-4. solidcore is the wrong side - filed as #939.

Corrupt corpus: no panic, no hang. solidcore refuses 17 of 19 by name and imports 2 that are whole. truck-stepio, as the bench reads it, refuses the 10 that break the Part 21 syntax and answers `Ok` for the other 9, five of them with an open mesh.

Tessellation (point 4): `solidcore-tess` at the app's 0.005 mm chord has 0 open triangle sides on every fixture (truck: 854 on Milling-test, 3196 on sample_ap214) and is closer to the exact volume (5.6e-5 against 1.2e-4 relative on Milling-test), with more triangles (6228 against 952). What a machining mesh still owes is #940.

wasm32 (point 5): `cargo check -p camcraft-kernel --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` passes.

## How tested

Run in release, `cargo test --release -p camcraft-kernel --no-fail-fast`: 25 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored (heavy lane); the 2 heavy-lane tests also pass with `--ignored`. `cargo clippy --release -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

Pinning tests (new): `step_files_agree_or_refuse_by_name`, `importer_hands_out_closed_forms_and_units`, `corrupt_step_files_never_panic_or_hang`, `importer_keeps_its_size_and_time_bounds`. Re-pinned: `port_degenerate_inputs_never_panic_and_match_pinned_verdicts`, `corrupt_native_files_never_panic_or_hang`.

## Gate results after the first push

**Batch gate on head 10fabe16 merged with an older main** (run by the main session, not by the author): all green except one UI theme test that was red on main itself at the time (fixed on main since); `cargo test --release -p camcraft-kernel` passed there too (25 passed).

**This round - head ef65c32e, which is 10fabe16 + `git merge origin/main` (e0cb0049, v0.18.0) + a one-line count correction in the decision file.** The merge had no conflict; `Cargo.lock` merged by itself and `cargo metadata --locked` accepts it. Against main's lock, package by package: the registry `solidcore` 1.0.1 is replaced by the git one, five `solidcore-*` git packages are added, and `camcraft-kernel`'s dependency list gains them plus `ruststep` and `truck-stepio` (dev-dependencies, already locked). No other package differs; `flecs_ecs`, `flecs_ecs_sys` and the `ruststep` git source are identical to main's.

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test --release -p camcraft-kernel --no-fail-fast` | 25 passed, 0 failed, 2 ignored (heavy lane) |
| `cargo test --release -p camcraft-kernel --test agreement -- --ignored` | 2 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |
| `cargo check -p camcraft-kernel --target wasm32-unknown-unknown` | ok |
| `cargo check -p camcraft-app` | ok |

The tests and the checks ran on the merged tree before the count correction was committed; that commit changes only `docs/decisions/916-solidcore-step-bench.md`.

## What was not exercised

- `cargo xtask gate quick` was not run by the author: its plan falls back to the batch tier because `Cargo.lock` changed. The batch tier was run by the main session instead (below). App's and ui's suites were not re-run on the head merged with v0.18.0 main; `cargo check -p camcraft-app` was.
- The largest mesh-to-surface distance is not measured; the mesh is judged on volume, area, box and watertightness (#940).
- No wasm32 test run, only the check; `solidcore-tess` was not checked for wasm32.
- No STEP file larger than 100 KB and no third-party corpus: the fixtures are the repo's nine.
- The time bound cannot stop the reader's topology pass (no hook upstream, #939); it is bounded by caps.

Follow-ups filed: #939 (bounding box and two smaller port findings), #940 (machining mesh). Both gate #917.

Decisions: `docs/decisions/916-solidcore-step-bench.md`. Notices: `assets/ui/LICENSES.md`.

Changelog: The kernel seam can import STEP through solidcore's reader (bench only; the app still imports through truck), with a pinned agreement bench against truck over every STEP fixture; solidcore moves from crates.io 1.0.1 to a pinned commit of the owner's fork.

Effort: max (not escalated)

Fixes #916

title: feat(post): Synthetos TinyG post processor (3-axis mill)
body:
Adds a Synthetos TinyG post and a generic 3-axis router/mill so CamCraft can produce TinyG programs with manual tool changes, expanded drilling and explicit refusals for unsupported operations.

Stacked on #715 (grblHAL), integrated through `c9822758`; main integrated through `37482923`. The original branch includes release tag `v0.16.0`.

The compatibility update stops spindle and coolant before manual changes, restores a safe Z height after M0, refuses feeds that would format as F0, splits XY arcs into at most half turns, and linearizes non-XY arcs within a 0.005 mm bound including rounding. An optional script-level spindle dwell follows M3; smoothing requests produce one explanatory comment without inventing a controller tolerance word.

The merge keeps main's post/machine registrations and Heidenhain stream behavior. Contour lead goldens were regenerated for main's CAM geometry changes. The latest #715 parent already contains the corresponding grblHAL golden updates.

Evidence and validation:

- Final commit `572c6ed884546befcd6693e2a7681b006844b735` matches the tested working tree. TinyG-focused checks: **88 tests passed**, and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test tinyg_post --test coolant --test conformance`: TinyG 18/18, coolant 7/7 and conformance 6/6 passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test script_tinyg --test comp`: script cases 11/11 and compensation cases 9/9 passed.
- Final affected app suites: conformance 6, control compensation 5, coolant follow-ups 7, Fanuc cross-post checks 12, inverted-post checks 15, TinyG 18, wear compensation 5; plus the 20 post-script/compensation tests above.
- The repository-wide quick gate is **not claimed green**: it found the inherited grblHAL post is missing its required recorded suite (`recorded_streams::every_shipped_post_script_has_its_suite`). That broader run was stopped. This TinyG revision does not add grblHAL tests or fixes; the parent-suite gap remains separately identified.
- Regression coverage includes `feeds_that_round_to_zero_are_refused_in_each_machine_unit`, `full_xy_circles_and_helices_split_without_losing_direction_or_depth`, `vertical_arcs_are_chords_within_five_microns`, `first_cut_after_a_tool_change_seats_at_a_safe_start_height`, and `spindle_delay_is_optional_validated_and_rounds_up_in_seconds`.
- Final 13 conformance TinyG goldens replayed through the existing edge-next host executable: 759 lines, 1,566 planner blocks; zero failures, refusals, alarms or findings. The executable records dirty firmware source at `998c02eb`; CPS SHA-256 `99905fc06fb604b7ddbb3d119f60cdc50bdfe52bd6190500bb12752168c2ae4c`. The six runnable script-suite goldens also pass: 254 lines and 369 blocks; five named-refusal snapshots are not controller programs. Combined: 19 programs, 1,013 lines and 1,935 blocks, all clean.
- Independent mocked geometry screen: 32 non-XY helical-arc cases across mm/inch, XZ/YZ, CW/CCW and radii 0.01/1/10/100 mm; maximum sampled chord radial deviation 0.004871692 mm. This is a mathematical screen, not a stock-clearance or hardware proof.
- Behavior basis: public TinyG documentation and a user-supplied behavior review of master 440.21 and edge-next 450.x. No GPL firmware source was consulted by the CamCraft implementation agents.
- Master runtime verification was attempted, but the existing host adapters are incompatible with that revision. No independent master replay or physical-board verification is claimed.
- Host replay does not simulate operator jogging, physical stepping, spindle acceleration, serial flow, or real feedhold timing. Senders must hold streaming at M0 when the operator changes offsets. Short-segment simplification and a Setup UI for the script-level spindle-wait option are outside this PR.

Changelog: Add a TinyG 3-axis post with manual tool changes, expanded drilling, bounded arc output, feed-rounding refusals and an optional script-level spindle-start dwell.

Fixes #836

title: fix(app): generator refusals speak the document's unit (#740)
body:
An inch document's refusals still read millimeters: a bore 25 mm too deep was refused as `25.000 mm deep`, a `Ø14 shank in a Ø12 hole` quoted bare millimeters - while every dialog around it spoke inches (#740).

## The change

The refusal sentences are built deep in the generator, off the worker threads, world-free - that's why they never saw the document's unit. The fix carries the unit to them rather than reaching for the world:

- `GenJob` grows a `unit: Unit` field; `collect_job` fills it from `crate::units::of(world)` while the world is still in hand, and it rides into every refusal builder as one added argument (`too_deep`, `shank_fits`, `axial_reach`, the cross-reach family in `cross_spindle`/`cross_stock`/`cross_holder`, `circle_of_region`, `pocket_region_on_part`/`around_part`, `offset_run`). `AreaCtx` carries it the same way.
- The lens itself: `units::len(v_mm, unit, prec)` prints `{:.prec}` byte-identically in millimeters and the converted value at `prec + 2` in inches; `Unit::suffix()` gives the word. Every pinned number is `{:.3}` in mm, so inch refusals read five decimals. Where the sentence had a literal `" mm"` it now ends `units::len(..) + unit.suffix()`; bare numbers (mouth coordinates, `shank dia. {:.3}`, `Z {:.3}`) become suffixless `units::len(..)`.
- `GenError::At`'s location stays millimeters - the lens is for the sentence, not the geometry marker. Tests pin this.
- Two `#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]` attrs (`axial_reach`, `shank_fits`), following the existing convention in `generate.rs`/`plunge_solid.rs`.

Millimeter documents change not one byte: the existing suite, which pins these sentences verbatim, passes untouched.

## Pins (red on main, green with the fix)

`crates/app/tests/units_in_refusals.rs` runs five operations twice each, mm then inch, asserting the mm sentence byte-for-byte and the inch sentence converted:

- `an_axial_reach_refusal_speaks_the_document_unit` - through-hole `too_deep`: depth, flute, fix depth cross the lens, ` mm` becomes ` in`.
- `a_cross_reach_refusal_speaks_the_document_unit` - raw-bar cross hole: mouth coords `(10.000, 0.000, 0.000)` -> `(0.39370, 0.00000, 0.00000)`; the `At` location is pinned to stay `(10, 0, 0)` mm.
- `a_shank_fit_refusal_speaks_the_document_unit` - the BR-1000 shank refusal: depth/flute lensed, bare `shank dia. 14.000` -> `0.55118`; location pinned mm.
- `a_circle_fit_refusal_speaks_the_document_unit` - circular-fit deviation and centre point.
- `a_part_fills_the_selection_refusal_speaks_the_document_unit` - the plane named in the area refusal: ` at Z 7.000` -> ` at Z 0.27559`.

title: feat(ops): one machining-frame seam - OpFrame composes part_alignment and TiltedFrame
body:
## What changed

Phase 1 of #763: **`OpFrame`** — the one machining-frame seam in
`crates/app/src/operation/frame.rs` — composes the two existing frame
mechanisms (the setup's `part_alignment` from #326 and the op's 3+2
`Tilt` from M5.1 B) behind one door, and `collect_job` reads through it:

- `OpFrame::of(op)` built once per generation; material and heights
  resolve through it; the tilt frame comes from
  `OpFrame::checked_frame` — one construction site, the refusal keeping
  its exact words and its exact precedence (after the heights resolve,
  the job's error-order law).
- The contract is stated once in the module header: D / S / L frames,
  right-to-left composition `p_L = T(A(p_D))`, the CL wrapping back via
  `TiltedFrame::world_path` (identity clone without a tilt), and the
  furniture law (stock / WCS / fixtures live in S: never aligned, but
  read local by the tilt).
- Heights and bounds in L ship correct from day one
  (`aabb_local_of`, `height_z_local`): they resolve against FULLY
  TRANSFORMED geometry, never a `z − origin.z` shift of the S box —
  the shift is only correct while the tool axis is the world Z.

**No refusal lifted, no post change, no generator change.** The four
verified kinds, picks, area controls and tilt-in-aligned-setups keep
their refusals; the later phases lift them one by one, each with its
numeric pin.

## How tested

- New `crates/app/tests/opframe_seam.rs` (8 tests) + the seam's inline
  unit tests (6): identity passthrough; zero-tilt index reproduces the
  prismatic path EXACTLY move-for-move (the identity-bits law); a
  tilted face runs in its own plane (every endpoint maps back into the
  L1-folded height band over the local silhouette, tool axis =
  hand-computed Rx(45)); 90-degree alignment turns the solid and its
  TopOfModel height (15, not 10); 180-degree alignment mirrors the
  facets by hand math; alignment × tilt composition pinned against
  hand-composed transforms; local heights/boxes read fully transformed
  geometry (and provably NOT the z-shift); picks stay refused by name
  while the door Phase 2 will read through is already aligned.
- Capability gates: unchanged by design; the tilted-move refusal keeps
  its existing verbatim pin in `tests/inverted_post.rs`.
- The four kinds' aligned generation keeps its pins in the #326 suites
  (`plane_align`, `axis_align`, `rest_across_setups`, …), run by the
  same gate.

## What was not exercised

- The L-frame height/AABB resolve methods are pinned by tests only —
  no production call site switches onto them until Phase 2+ lifts the
  matching refusals (deliberate: the seam lands behavior-identical).
- The boundary/region builders (`boundary_ctx`, `material_region`,
  `boundary_picks`) still build their own frames from `op.params.tilt()`
  — they move onto the seam in the later phases.

title: feat(wcs): anchor the WCS on a picked circle's centre; tidy the WCS page
body:
## What changed

**Shared pick primitive** - `crates/app/src/pick/circle.rs` (next to the #692 pick graph): `circle_centre(world, &GeoSel)`, `circle_of_edge(graph, edge)`, `circle_of_run(features, run)` return a `Circle { centre, axis, radius, closed }` or a named `CircleRefusal` (`Straight`, `TooShort`, `NotCircular`, `NotAnEdge`, `Gone`). The edge pick resolves to its **run** (one straight stretch or one arc), so an arc of a filleted rim works too. The fit reuses `feature_arc::fit_arc` and its tolerances, and checks every vertex. A non-circular edge is refused, never guessed. The axis sign is canonical, so a hole in a top face reads +Z. The centre is in the active setup's view frame (#326), the frame the WCS is set in.

**Command + MCP** - `SetWcsAtCircleCentre` (`crates/app/src/commands/wcs_circle.rs`) resolves the circle when the command is created and wraps `SetWcsOrigin` at the centre: one undo step, and undo restores the previous origin. The MCP tool `set_wcs_circle_centre { edge: {model, id}, rotation? }` (`crates/app/src/mcp/wcs_circle.rs`) runs the same command and returns the circle's centre, axis and diameter. The camcraft-mcp skill doc lists the tool. No MCP follow-up is needed.

**WCS page** (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page.rs`, split out of the 1894-line `pages.rs`):
- Three collapsible sections: *Origin and orientation*, *Quarter turns* and *Anchor on*.
- The six value fields sit in a two-column grid, label and field on one row, with the fields in one column.
- The quarter turns are two rows of three equal buttons ([X+ Y+ Z+] / [X- Y- Z-]), plus *Level* and *Set Origin* as two equal halves. Every row spans the pane's width.
- The anchor grid is a 3x3 compass of equal cells (up to 72 x 30), placed exactly and centred.
- *Anchor on* has a third choice, **Circle centre**. It shows a "Pick a circular edge" toggle and then the result, e.g. "Circle Ø 20.00 mm, centre (0.00, 0.00, 10.00)", or "Not anchored: <reason>". While the toggle is armed, a viewport click takes feature edges only, one run per click, and hover highlights what a click would take. A landed pick disarms the toggle. Choosing Circle centre disarms the box markers, and the other way round.
- The Bottom/Middle/Top radios are now a plain "Z level" row. Beside the 120 px label column they widened the section past a narrow pane.

**Plumbing** - `CommandKind::SetWcsCircle`, and a new `state_wcs.rs` that also takes over the existing `SetWcs` arm (`state.rs` shrinks). The viewport routes clicks through `wcs_pick.rs` (anchor markers + circle pick), which shortens `interact.rs`. `feature_click::ask` returns the circle ask while armed.

## How tested

- `crates/app/tests/circle_centre.rs` (new, 5 tests) uses a plate with a drilled 8 mm hole (32 chords), off-centre at (5, -3):
  - `a_drilled_hole_rim_gives_its_true_centre_axis_and_radius`: centre within 1e-6, Ø 8, axis +Z, through a real ray pick, and again with the part moved.
  - `a_straight_edge_is_refused_by_name`.
  - `an_elliptical_rim_and_a_face_are_refused_never_guessed`: ellipse gives `NotCircular`, face gives `NotAnEdge`, stale id gives `Gone`.
  - `the_anchor_command_places_the_origin_and_undo_restores_the_previous_one`: undo, redo, and a refusal never builds a command.
  - `mcp_set_wcs_circle_centre_anchors_on_a_rim_and_refuses_a_straight_edge`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_page_tests.rs` (structural, no pixels):
  - `the_page_has_three_sections_and_one_row_fields_in_one_column`
  - `quarter_turns_are_equal_buttons_filling_the_pane`
  - `the_anchor_points_are_a_centred_compass_of_equal_cells`
  - It also holds the three `turn_wcs` tests, moved verbatim from `pages.rs`. The test count is unchanged.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/wcs_circle_tests.rs`:
  - `a_rim_click_anchors_the_origin_on_its_centre_and_undo_restores_it`: combo, then the pick button, then a viewport click on a boss rim, then G54 at the centre. The page states the circle, and Undo restores (1, 2, 3).
  - `a_face_is_refused_by_name_and_lands_nothing`
- Gate (macOS, worktree target):
  - Ran green: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `camcraft-app --lib`, the full `camcraft-ui` lib and integration suites (459 lib tests), and these app suites: circle_centre, feature_pick, feature_pick_wire, mcp, mcp_setup, mcp_pick, mcp_live, one_wcs, setup_wcs, commands_undo, wcs_align, wcs_view_pose, face_origin, vertex_pick, pick.
  - Not run: `cargo xtask gate quick` itself. Its dry run fell back to every crate, which is batch-sized.

## Not exercised

- Nobody has looked at the page in the real app (hand check below). No snapshot PNG changed. The release-lane `egui_shell_snapshot` was not run; the WCS page is not in that frame.
- A circle on a rotated or aligned setup is covered by the view-pose transform, and the app test covers a translated part. No rotated-setup test was added.

## Hand check

1. Open the WCS node and check the three sections. Each field should sit on one row with its label. Narrow the properties pane: the turn buttons should stretch evenly, and the compass should stay centred with equal cells.
2. Set *Anchor on: Circle centre*, then press *Pick a circular edge*. Hovering a hole rim or boss edge should highlight it. A click should move the WCS origin to the circle centre at the rim's height and show "Circle Ø … , centre (…)". Ctrl+Z should restore the previous origin.
3. With the pick armed, click a straight edge: the status line and the page should say it is straight, and the origin should stay put.
4. Switch back to Stock box: the compass and "Pick markers in viewport" should work as before.

title: fix(ui,app): setup alignment composes on the current pose, one flow, readable picks (#738)
body:
## What changed (#738, maintainer-reported, P1)

1. **Moves compose on the current pose.** Laying on a face or on three points now computes the lay in the setup's current alignment and composes it onto that alignment, through new `pick::lay_on_plane_in` / `lay_on_points_in` and `setup_turn::held_centre`. Before, each move went back to the import pose first. Axes already composed. Each move is still one `AlignPartToSetup`, and one undo returns to the previous pose exactly. Re-applying the same pick is a zero step and is refused as "already holds the part that way".
2. **One flow.** The top row now reads "Part alignment - each move starts from where the part sits now", and its tooltip describes the flow.
   - "Start from a preset" presets turn the part from where it sits, and so does the typed "Turn by", through the new `CommandKind::TurnPart` → `AlignPartToSetup::turn_by`.
   - "As modelled" is the one reset.
   - The pickers' Apply tooltips say a move starts from the current pose and is one undo step.
3. **Readable status.** It now reads "1 face selected", "2 points selected" or "1 edge selected" (`pick_words`).
   - Points show where they are: "Point 2: on 'part' (x, y, z) mm".
   - Internal ids ("Face 0xccc7c…") never show; app refusals on the page are stripped of " 0x…".
4. **Picks you can see.** `align_pick_viz::paint`:
   - picked faces are filled with the pick violet (alpha 96);
   - picked points are 6 px filled discs;
   - picked edges are 4 px strokes.

**Splits, so no large file grows:**
- `commands/align_stock.rs` comes out of `setup_align.rs` (422 → 298 lines).
- `state_align.rs` comes out of `state.rs` (4116 → 4062 lines).
- No snapshot PNG changed.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/738-align-flow.md`.

## Pinned by
- `align_compose` (new, 3 tests):
  - axes then face;
  - face then three points;
  - turn-by after a lay, for both pivots, plus the zero and NaN refusals.

  Each checks that the second move composes on the first, and that undo, undo and redo step back exactly.
- `setup_align_tests::a_preset_after_a_face_lay_composes_and_as_modelled_is_the_one_reset` (real clicks, Ctrl+Z).
- `setup_plane_tests::the_pick_status_counts_the_face_and_never_shows_an_id` and `setup_points_tests::the_pick_status_counts_the_points_and_never_shows_an_id`.
- `plane_face_pick::picked_faces_fill_points_are_discs_and_edges_are_bold` (paint assertions on the rendered shell).
- `pick_words` unit tests.

## Tested
- **app suites:** all green. lib 107, `align_compose` 3, `plane_align` 9, `plane_align_edges` 5, `points_align` 8, `axis_align` 10, `setup_align` 9, `turn_pivot` 5, `commands_undo` 32, `project_roundtrip` 71, `wcs_align` 5, `mcp_setup` 6, `fixture_locate` 11, `winding_align` 9, `setup_carry` 9, `setup_relative` 9, `setup_stock_source` 6, `fixture_locate_stock` 3, `wcs_view_pose` 3.
- **ui suites:** all green, lib 447.
- **clippy `-D warnings`:** ui lib+tests and the app lib are clean.

## Not exercised / for the hand check
- The look of the fill, discs and bold edges on a real part, including a tilted face.
- How the new wording reads in the narrow properties pane.
- Pressing "Turn by" Apply twice turns the part twice; this is intended.
- **Behaviour change:** MCP `lay_part_on_points` / `lay_part_on_plane` now also compose, since they share the command.

**Stays a draft until the maintainer or user hand-checks it** (binary: `~/camcraft-builds/camcraft-ui-738`).

title: feat(post): grblHAL post processor (3-axis mill)
body:
Fork synced at v0.16.0.

## What changed

A new built-in post, **grblHAL** (`assets/posts/grblhal.cps`, 3-axis mill), and a generic machine, **grblHAL 3-axis** (`assets/machines/grblhal-3axis.mch`). The post is specced from the G-code list in grblHAL's public core README and the LinuxCNC G-code reference (behaviour only; grblHAL's GPL source was not read), structured after `tormach.cps`.

- Header `G21|G20 G17 G90 G91.1 G94 G40 G80`; no `%`, O word, N numbers or G64.
- **No tool length word** (no G43 / G43.1 / G49): on grblHAL the offset belongs to the controller's tool-change handling, and a G49 would discard a measured length. This departs from the issue's G43.1 default; reasoning in `docs/decisions/710-grblhal-post.md`.
- `G53 G0 Z<safe>` then `T<n> M6` **alone on its line**; no G28/G30.
- Canned cycles G73/G81/G82/G83/G86/G89 with G98, dwell P in seconds.
- Refused by name: control/wear compensation (G41/G42), tapping (G84), going home after an operation (G28/G30 positions are controller settings), tilted moves, and probing (the engine refuses it, since the post has no probe hooks).
- **Z lift without trusting an unhomed machine Z0.** With `$22=0` grblHAL takes its power-on position as machine zero, so `G53 G0 Z0` could rapid down. `G53 G0 Z<safe>` is written only when the machine file states `safe_retract` (= "it homes"). Otherwise the lift is `G0 Z<h>` in the work offset, where h is the section's `ClearancePlane` or a higher Z already commanded; it is refused by name when h is unknown or not above `StockZTop`. The generic machine states no `safe_retract`.

## How tested

- `conformance`: grblHAL in POSTS / REFUSED (`tap_plate`, "tapping") / EXTENSIONS. Goldens in `golden/nc/grblhal/` (12) and `golden/nc/synth_grblhal.nc`. The synth stream drops only the tap.
- New `grblhal_post.rs` (9 tests): registry and library, grbl program shape with no length/G64/G28/G30/G84 word, Z lift before a lone `T M6`, dwell P1.5 for 1500 ms, one named tap refusal, inch output, a homed machine lifting with G53, the work-offset lift without homing (clearance, a higher commanded Z, origin shift), and the named refusal of an unknown or buried lift height.
- Cross-post lists extended: `comment_escape`, `control_comp`, `wear_comp`, `post/tests/comp`, `fanuc_post` (non-RTCP; the tilt refusal is now looked for among all warnings, since grblHAL also refuses its lift on that bare stream), `inverted_post`, `after_op` (stops plus the home refusal), `coolant`, `coolant_followups`, `machine` (library expectations).

Quick gate (debug) on the final tree: 28 camcraft-app binaries, among them conformance 6 (goldens unchanged by the lift fix, their machine states safeRetractZ 0), grblhal_post 9, fanuc_post 11, after_op 10, coolant 7, machine 32 and posting 17, all green; camcraft-post `comp` 9/9; camcraft-ui lib `machines_pane` 6/6 and `post` 19/19; `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib -- -D warnings` clean. Whole-crate `clippy --tests` stops on the pre-existing `lathe_thread_travel.rs:83` compile error (missing field `hand`), which is on upstream main and not touched here.

## Review fix (smoothing, head 6129a904)

With per-operation smoothing (#616) on, the post writes one `(SMOOTHING NOT WRITTEN - GRBLHAL STATES NO SMOOTHING TOLERANCE)` note per program (grblHAL lists G61 only, no tolerance word) and resets the ask per section. Pinned by `smoothing::fanuc_and_mazak_name_the_ask_once_and_write_no_unbounded_word` (now covers grblHAL). Goldens unchanged (smoothing off).

## Not exercised

**Not yet run on a real grblHAL controller or its simulator - testers welcome.** Anyone with a grblHAL machine: please post a program with this post, dry-run it (no stock, Z raised, hand on feed hold), and report on #710, especially the Z lift before each tool change and at the end. The Setup pane's End-units row still appears only for Tormach, although the script reads `EndUnits`.

title: feat(app,ui): set the WCS from any set of feature picks (#701)
body:
You can select edges, vertices, faces and cylinder walls and say which axis each one sets (#701) - the WCS lands on the fitted frame, undoable like any other placement.

## The change

**App lane** - `pick::roles.rs`: `Role` (`Origin | X | Y | Z`) and `align_roles(world, picks) -> Result<Alignment, String>`, returning the same `Alignment` `pick::align`'s 3-2-1 fit already returns, so one fit law answers both. Frame law: among the axis picks present, read in the priority order Z, X, Y - first exact, second projected perpendicular, third derived to close the right-handed frame (a third axis pick is overridden wholesale, not blended). An origin pick anchors on the feature's natural centre; without one, the origin falls on the second axis pick's anchor (an edge's start, a face's centroid, a wall's centre), projected onto the first pick's plane when that pick is a face. Refusals come back as words, in order: too few picks, a duplicated role, fewer than two axes, an unresolvable datum, an unsupportable tilt, a stale feature id. Cylinder walls fit by covariance null-space (Jacobi) plus a Kasa circle, on the wall's local facets transformed by the feature's `setup_align::view_pose` - the same law the plane fit already uses.

**UI lane** - the Setups page grows a "Set WCS from features" row (`egui_app::wcs_pick_row.rs`) over a draft module (`wcs_pick.rs`): arming it keeps the toolbar's pick mode (faces, edges, corners and walls all feed the one draft), the role box says what the next pick sets, and each viewport pick is stamped into that role's slot - re-picking a role replaces its pick in place. One draft at a time: arming this row disarms the plane-pick and axis-pick drafts and vice versa, and the wcs draft pauses while its setup row is hidden (the #664 law). Apply is gated live by `align_roles` itself - the refusal words ride the row inline and on the disabled button, so the UI's why is the command's own words - and only answers on the ACTIVE setup's row: `SetWcs` places the active setup's WCS, so a greyed Apply on another setup's row says to make that row's setup active first. Apply queues the existing undoable `CommandKind::SetWcs`; the same command the WCS pane's anchor grid already sends. No new command kind, no world writes outside commands. Rationale in `docs/decisions/701-wcs-from-features.md`.

## Pins (red before the fix, green with it)

- `wcs_roles::z_face_x_edge_and_origin_corner_reproduce_the_3_2_1_frame` - a Z face, X edge and origin corner digit-for-digit reproduce `align_321`.
- `wcs_roles::the_third_axis_role_is_derived_right_handed_never_read` - three axis picks: the third is overridden wholesale and the frame is right-handed.
- `wcs_roles::the_origin_projects_onto_a_z_face_and_anchors_on_its_centroid` - an origin vertex pick anchors on the face's centroid, projected onto its plane.
- `wcs_roles::a_tilted_bore_wall_fits_its_real_axis_and_centre` / `a_bore_wall_picked_as_z_stands_upright_with_a_pinned_sign` - the wall fit, both flat and tilted, sign pinned by the axis role.
- `wcs_roles::every_degenerate_role_set_is_refused_by_name` - each refusal sentence, pinned.
- `wcs_roles::an_edge_as_the_first_axis_reads_unit_on_a_part_tipped_off_the_table` - the first-axis edge is normalised right after reading: unit length and square axes on a tipped part, origin on the block.
- `egui_app::wcs_pick_tests::*` - five kittest tests on the live row: arming keeps the pick mode and stops the other drafts; an incomplete set greys Apply and shows the app's own words; role picks land in the draft (never in the open operation) and Apply queues one undoable `SetWcs` that undo/redo round-trips; re-picking replaces only that role's pick; and with two setups, the row on the inactive one greys Apply, queues nothing, says to make that setup active, and once active the same frame moves that setup's own WCS while the other setup's work zero stays put.
- `wcs_pick::tests::*` - three draft-module tests: role default and mutual disarm, replace-in-place, a paused draft takes nothing.

## Tested

- The pin commit alone is red: at `35f399d1` the `wcs_roles` binary does not compile (no `pick::Role`/`align_roles` on main) and the ui lib does not compile (no `crate::wcs_pick`, row unwired) - the API and surface the pins demand did not exist.
- Green at head `d2663a3f`, merged with current `origin/main` (`f490458a`): `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test wcs_roles` - 7 passed. `cargo test -p camcraft-app --lib` - 110 passed. Full `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` (state.rs and interact.rs touched) - 538 passed, 5 ignored. `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` - clean.

## Follow-ups

- MCP parity: the agent surface still takes only an absolute origin/quaternion (`set_wcs`); filed as #937 to add a feature-pick version over the same `align_roles` law.
- Arc/circle centre picks (#705/#692) as the Origin role, now that `feature_arc` has landed - not wired here (`PickKinds.centres: false` in the wcs mode).
- A wall picked as an axis takes its sign from the hemisphere rule, not from the origin pick as an edge does (review round 3): deterministic, but siding it by the origin pick would match what a user expects.

Changelog: the Setups page can set the WCS from feature picks - click faces, edges, corners and walls in the viewport, say what each one sets, and Apply places the work zero on the fitted frame, undo and redo included (#701)

Fixes #701

title: feat(ui): viewport origin gizmos wear their names (#727)
body:
With several setups on screen, every origin triad looks alike - nothing in the viewport says whose zero is whose (#727).

## The change

Every origin gizmo now labels itself at its origin. Each work-offset triad draws the entity name the Setup pane already uses (`G54` for the first setup, `Setup2/WCS` for the second) in bright triad blue at the ordinary overlay-label size; the dimmed world axes draw `World` in neutral gray dimmed by `WORLD_DIM`, like the lines under them. `Gizmo` (`interact.rs`) grows one `name` field, filled in `gizmos()` - which already honors the Models pane's eye (`hidden_offsets`) and the `show_world_axes` gate, so a hidden offset loses its name with its lines for free. `overlay_labels` places each name just below the projected origin (`NAME_DROP_UV = 0.02`, same currency as `axis_note::NOTE_DROP_UV`), emitted before the gizmo's `X`/`Y`/`Z` tips. Only the letters keep the big `is_axis_label` font. Rationale in `docs/decisions/727-viewport-gizmo-labels.md`.

## The switch (#645)

On top of the names, the review on #645 asked for a user switch, so the browser pane grows a `Show origin names` checkbox next to `Show world origin axes`. It gates only the name rows: the big `X`/`Y`/`Z` letters and the triad's strokes ignore it. The choice is a per-user preference, not document state - nothing touches the world or the command history - and it persists in `view.json` in the OS config folder next to the recents file (`recent`'s resolver, #662, so `CAMCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR` overrides the folder), written at once on the flip and read back at startup. The default is ON, the #727 decision: shipping the switch changes no existing viewport. A missing, unreadable or corrupt file - or a foreign one, the `camcraft-view/1` format tag says - starts at the defaults with a logged reason, never a crash, and unknown keys stay ignored so newer builds keep working.

## Pins (red on main, green with the fix)

- `gizmo_tests::the_dimmed_world_axes_are_labelled_world` - the fresh world's set carries `World`, neutral gray (equal channels) and dimmed like the axes.
- `gizmo_tests::each_triad_is_labelled_with_its_own_offset_name` - two setups: both `G54` and `Setup2/WCS` label their own origins, bright against the letters.
- `gizmo_tests::an_offset_name_stands_at_its_origin_not_its_axis_tips` - the name rides the projected origin horizontally, a small uv drop below it, not crowded onto the tips.
- `gizmo_tests::a_hidden_work_offset_drops_its_name_with_its_gizmo` - the pane's eye and the label agree.
- `gizmo_tests::gizmo_names_are_not_the_big_axis_letters` - `is_axis_label` still answers only X/Y/Z.
- Re-pins: label counts 3→4 (fresh world), 6→8 (two gizmos), 3→4 (moved origin); `axis_note_tests`' fresh-world set pins exactly `["World", "X", "Y", "Z"]`, which fixes each gizmo's emission order name-first.
- `setup_chip_tests`' no-G54-on-Setup2's-op clause narrows to plane chips (`" · "`): the `G54` origin name is Setup1's own, legitimately - the law was about op chips, and it still holds there.
- `structural::origin_names_paint_on_and_quiet_off_letters_and_lines_always` - the re-review's both-states shell check: with the switch on the seeded document's `G54` name row paints inside the viewport (the properties pane also reads `G54`, so the probe sits between the pane anchors, as the view-cube check does); the checkbox click drops it from the painted frame while the `X`/`Y`/`Z` letters and the triad's strokes come through untouched. The test redirects `view_store` to a temp folder so the flip never writes the real user's `view.json`.
- `crates/app/tests/view_prefs.rs` (new integration suite) - the persistence law: a flipped choice round-trips through the file across a "restart", a missing file is a quiet default start, a corrupt or foreign-format file starts at the defaults with a reason and never crashes, unknown keys stay ignored, and a `CAMCRAFT_CONFIG_DIR` override is the folder the choice round-trips through (`recent::config_dir_for` with a fake getter, as `recent_files` does).

## Tested

- Red first: with only the pins committed, `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- gizmo_tests axis_note_tests` ran 8 failed / 7 passed, exactly the new and re-pinned label tests - e.g. the fresh world's labels were `["X", "Y", "Z"]` with no name.
- Green: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- gizmo_tests axis_note_tests setup_chip_tests` - 17 passed, 0 failed.
- Full lib: `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib` - 490 passed, 0 failed (5 ignored). An earlier run of the same command failed only on `structural::shell_structure_light`, a theme-sync test this change never touches; it passes in isolation and on re-run - pre-existing parallel global-theme-state flakiness, already noted on #638.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test view_prefs` - 5 passed, 0 failed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` - clean.
- Not exercised: the on-screen labels themselves - the producers are pinned instead.

Changelog: viewport origin gizmos now wear their names - each work-offset triad shows its Setup-pane name at its origin, the neutral world axes show World (#727) - and a persisted "Show origin names" checkbox in the browser pane turns the name rows on and off, kept in the per-user `view.json` (#645)

Fixes #727

title: feat(post): the document's program number and comment, per dialect (#258 part 2)
body:
Part 2 of #258's split: the program number and comment. Today every post hard-codes `O0001` followed by the machine name. Branched from upstream/main; the fork is synced at v0.15.0.

## What changed
- **Document field:** a new `ProgramInfo { number, comment }` singleton (schema.rs). Unset means every post writes exactly what it wrote before.
- **Command:** an undoable `SetProgramInfo`. At creation it refuses by name:
  - a number outside 1-9999;
  - a comment over 40 characters, non-printable or non-ASCII, or containing `( ) % ; *`.

  Chosen: refuse rather than sanitise. Heidenhain and SINUMERIK, which use the comment as the program name, check it against their name rules at post time.
- **UI:** "Program number" and "Program comment" fields on the Post page. They commit on Enter or when focus leaves.
- **MCP:** a new `set_program` tool.
- **Scripts:** they get a `program` global `{number, numbered, comment}` (`engine::run_program_with`); `programNumber` is kept. Documented in docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md and assets/posts/AGENTS.md.
- **Per-operation files:** one file per op counts up from the stated number and is refused past O9999. The old code silently clamped instead.
- **Project file v59:** an optional `program` key. This is a version step, not just an added key, because an older build would drop the key and post O0001, which could overwrite a different program on the control. v58 files load with nothing set.

**Per dialect.** Each rule is cited in its .cps. The manual section references were written from memory, so a maintainer may want to check them against the manuals.
- **Fanuc, Fanuc Lathe, Mazak:** `O####` (O0001-O9999), then `(<comment or machine name>)`.
- **Haas:** five-digit `O#####`, written only when a number is set.
- **Tormach PathPilot:** never an O-word, because LinuxCNC's O words are subroutine and flow-control words. A number goes in the header comment.
- **Heidenhain ISO:** the comment becomes the program name, `%<name> G71 *`, limited to file-name characters. If only a number is set, it is used as the name.
- **SINUMERIK:** the comment becomes `%_N_<NAME>_MPF` (letters, digits and `_`; the first two are letters or `_` plus a letter; at most 24 characters). A name that breaks these rules is refused, not renamed. The number goes in a `; PROGRAM n` comment.

Decision record: `docs/decisions/258-program-number.md`.

## How tested
- **New `program_info` tests (9):**
  - output is byte-identical in all 7 posts when nothing is set;
  - each dialect's header with a number and comment, and with a number alone;
  - post-time refusals;
  - command validation, undo and redo;
  - the typed-number parser (accepts `O0012`);
  - per-op numbering;
  - a live post writes `O0077 (Lid)`, and undo restores O0001;
  - round-trip: a v58 file loads with nothing set, and a corrupt value is refused.
- **Also new:** `mcp_setup::set_program_states_undoes_and_refuses_by_name`, and ui `program_info_tests` (typing into the fields, Ctrl+Z/Ctrl+Y, a refusal).
- **Gate:** 35 app test binaries (338 tests) pass, including conformance, golden_cl, posting, every post suite, project_roundtrip, commands_undo, mcp and mcp_setup. All camcraft-post tests pass. ui lib passes 378; the one failure is the headless-GPU test, which also fails on this machine without the change. Clippy (post/app/ui, `-D warnings`) is clean. **No golden changed.**

## Not exercised
A GUI hands-on check, and a run of a numbered program on a control or in the Hub. G-code changes only when a number or comment is set.

Changelog: The document states its program number and comment (Post page, MCP set_program); each post writes it in its own dialect - O-word (Fanuc, Fanuc Lathe, Mazak, Haas), Heidenhain program name, SINUMERIK %_N_..._MPF, PathPilot header comment; project v59 (#258)

Refs #258

title: feat(post): EDM condition table as user data in the .mch edm section
body:
**Stacked on #551** (EDM machine kinds). Its commits show here until #551 merges; this PR adds one commit on top.

## What changed

`edm.conditions[]` in the `.mch` `edm` section (#531, part of #290, design D4):
- Each condition is `{ id, name, gap, wire_diameter | undersize, role: rough|skim|finish, notes }`. It holds only the geometry a toolpath needs. Power and flushing stay the control's, selected by `id`.
- `id` is the control's own selector, required and unique; a numeric id reads as its word. Lengths scale with the file's unit. Gap and undersize may be 0; a wire diameter must be positive.
- A garbled entry refuses the file, naming its id, and `is_sane` restates the law for project files.
- `Edm::condition(machine, id, need)` is the door the first EDM op (#532) calls at command creation. A missing condition, or an unstated field the op needs (gap, wire diameter, undersize), is refused by name before any generator runs.
- No conditions ship. Tests use an explicitly synthetic table.

## How tested

- New `edm_conditions`, 6/6:

  - the lookup refuses a missing condition or field by name;

title: feat(turning): optional repeat pass at each threading depth
body:
**Replaces #437** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #433** (#417), which is on #432 (#416). Part of #363. The #418 work is bf3b0d58.

## What changed
- **The option:** `ThreadInfeed.repeat_each_depth`, off by default. Every pass above the root is followed by an identical copy: same tip depth, same lattice shift, same helix phase. So a repeat can never cut deeper or move. The finishing and spring passes at the root are not repeated.
- **Alternating infeed:** the side flips once per depth, not per cut, so a repeat keeps its flank.
- **G76 refuses it by name.** The record carries a `repeat_each_depth` flag, written to the stream as `REP 1` only when set, plus a `RepeatEachDepth` post property. `fanuc-lathe.cps` refuses with "repeat each roughing depth is not a G76 cycle (the cycle cuts each depth once)".
- **Defaults are byte-identical:** the stamp adds one byte only when the flag is on, and no project key or stream word is written when it's off. No version rung.
- **UI:** a "Repeat each depth" checkbox on the Passes tab, after Spring passes. Its tooltip says G32 only, that G76 refuses it, and that tooling makers recommend against routine spring passes.
- `docs/decisions/418-thread-repeat-pass.md`

## How tested
- motion `turning_thread_infeed`, 10/10, including two new tests:
  - every roughing depth is cut twice (0.4, 0.4, 0.8, 0.8, 1.1, 1.1, 1.2, 1.2) and the default is unchanged move for move;
  - a repeat is the same pass under every method × schedule, and the verdict stays silent.
- app:
  - `turning_thread_infeed` 5/5: the toggle goes stale and back to OK, takes 3 then 5 plunges, with undo and redo; round-trip writes the key only when set;

title: fix(post): G76 words state the thread passes that were verified
body:
**Replaces #433** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

**Stacked on #432 (#416).** Part of #363.

## What changed
**With the G76 cycle post option, the G76 words now describe the passes the verdict judged.**
- The record maps 1:1: `G76 P(m)(r)(a) Q(dmin) R(d)` / `G76 X Z P(k) Q(dd) F`, where:
  - dd = the first pass's depth;
  - dmin = the step (constant depth) or the plan's minimum (constant area);
  - d = the finishing pass's own depth;
  - m = 1 + spring passes;
  - a = twice the flank angle.
- **Control model** (GSK988TA, Fanuc-compatible G76):
  - each roughing pass goes to `max(dd·√n, previous + dmin)`, up to k − d;
  - the first finishing pass cuts d, and m − 1 more repeat at k;
  - each pass starts `depth·tan(a/2)` along Z.
- **Refused by name with G76 chosen:** alternating infeed (the CL carries a new `alternating` flag; `ALT 1` is written to the stream only when set), a doubled angle outside 0/29/30/55/60/80 (so 29.5° is refused), and a one-pass thread.

**⚠ This changes posted output for the default G76 thread: `R0` becomes `R0.4`.** The golden `fanuc-lathe/thread_g76.nc` changes on one line: `G76 P010000 Q400 R0` → `G76 P010000 Q400 R0.4`.
- Why: with `R0` the control roughs 0.4, 0.8 and 1.2, then cuts its finishing pass at the root again. That is a fourth full-depth pass the verdict never judged. It's not a gouge, but it isn't what was verified.
- With `R0.4` it roughs 0.4 and 0.8 and finishes at 1.2: exactly the three passes we judge.
- Making `R0` true instead would have meant changing G32 output and the judged passes.
- Note: the #363 research said Q = infeed made the control cut a decreasing ladder. That isn't so, because dmin = infeed clamps every step equal. The real gap was R.

`docs/decisions/417-g76-matches-verified.md`

## How tested
- New app `lathe_post_g76_schedule` (4 tests):
  - a new flank, constant-area golden `thread_g76_area.nc` (`G76 P020055 Q100 R0.05` / `G76 X9.6 Z14 P1200 Q400 F2`): the control's schedule computed from the posted words matches the laid depths and stations within 1 µm;
  - the default (`R0.4`) and a 0.5 step (`Q500 R0.2`) also match;
  - one refusal per unexpressible option;
  - `ALT` survives the stream and the project file.
- Existing post, cl, inverted_post, lathe_post, golden_cl, project_roundtrip, tool_law, tool_gate and commands_undo suites are green.
- `clippy --tests -D warnings` (cl, post, motion, app, ui) is clean.
- The gate escalated to batch (cl changed). It fails only on tests already red on main: headless GPU, #415, and `swarf_pose_continuity` (PR #351).

## Not exercised / not confirmed by sources (draft until a lathe sim or machine run)
1. Which way Fanuc shifts Z per pass for flank infeed. This follows LinuxCNC's sign; either sign is gouge-safe.
2. Whether the control also shifts each pass's end Z. If not, early passes end up to k·tan θ off at the runout, shallower than the root.
3. How the minimum-depth clamp applies (read as a per-pass minimum, per the manual's definition).
4. Micron rounding of the words: the control's ladder can differ by under 1 µm.

None of these moves the finished thread form.

title: feat(turning): threading infeed method and decreasing-depth pass schedule
body:
**Replaces #432** (opened from the old fork, which can no longer take pushes). Same head commit; nothing else changed.

Part of #363 (peck threading; the research comment there has the sources). Follow-up #417 (PR stacked on this one) makes the G76 output match these passes.

## What changed
**New threading op param `infeed_plan` (`turning::ThreadInfeed`).**
- **Infeed method:** radial, modified flank at an angle θ, or alternating flank.
- **Depth schedule:** constant depth, or constant area (first depth × √n).
- **Minimum depth per pass, finish allowance, and spring passes** (default 0, capped at 98).
- The existing `infeed` is the first-pass depth.
- It's shown as rows on the op's Passes tab (`thread_infeed_page.rs`).

**Kernel.** `crates/motion/src/turning/infeed.rs` lays the passes from the plan. `thread_in` calls `thread_planned_in` with the default plan.
- **Flank:** each pass starts shifted by −(tip − root)·tan θ along its travel. Finishing and spring passes sit on the pitch lattice, so lead and spindle phase never change.
- **Safety:** every pass stays inside the finished V exactly when θ ≤ half the insert's included angle. A larger angle is refused by name at the command (create, paste, edit, retype via `thread_gate`) and again at Generate.
- **Alternating:** flips the side each pass.

**The verdict judges the laid passes.** `the_verdict_reads_the_shifted_pass` pins a past-half-angle pass being convicted. `attach_cycle` moved to `thread_cycle.rs`.

**Defaults are byte-identical.** The default plan makes the same `blade::rungs(root, ref_top, infeed, 0)` call at the same stations.
- The op stamp includes the plan only when it isn't the default, so cached threads stay fresh.
- The project key is written only when non-default, so there's no version rung. An older build drops a non-default plan and cuts the radial ladder; that's not a gouge.
- No existing golden changed.

`docs/decisions/416-thread-infeed.md`

## How tested
- New motion `turning_thread_infeed` (8 tests):
  - √n depths with the minimum-depth clamp;
  - allowance plus spring-pass count;
  - flank shift, including the full 30°;
  - alternating flip;
  - verdict silent for every method × schedule on the thread fixture;
  - a shifted pass is convicted;
  - refusals by name.
- New app `turning_thread_infeed` (4/4, plus 1 after the merge): the plan runs in a document; refusals at create and edit; undo/redo (op goes stale); project round-trip with no key for the default plan.
- Existing suites unchanged and green: motion `turning_thread` and `turning_thread_cycle`; app `turning_thread`, `lathe_post_g76`, `lathe_field_tools` and `project_roundtrip`.
- `clippy --tests -D warnings` is clean.
- `scripts/gate.sh quick` passes except tests that already fail on main:
  - the headless-GPU ui tests;
  - `setup_stock_source::a_new_block_after_a_flip…` (#415);
  - `swarf_pose_continuity` (2 tests; red on main, fixed by PR #351).

## Not exercised (draft)
- GUI check of the new Passes-tab rows.
- **Posted G-code for non-default plans** (flank, constant area, allowance, spring passes) is new. It needs a lathe simulator or machine run before ready. Default plans post exactly as before.

Fixes #416

title: feat(turning): in-pass chip-break dips inside a continuous G32 chain
body:
**Stacked on #437** (#418), which is on #433 (#417) and #432 (#416). Until those merge, this diff includes their commits; the #419 work is 68bd14a5. Part of #363.

## The citation gate (the issue's precondition)
Before any code, the issue required a primary-source citation that chained Fanuc G32 blocks keep spindle synchronization. Found in *FANUC Series 0i-TD/0i Mate-TD USER'S MANUAL (For Lathe System)*, B-64304EN-1/01, Part II:
- **§3.4 "Continuous Threading", p.34:** consecutive threading blocks keep "the synchronism with the spindle" at "the joint between blocks wherever possible", so the lead and shape can change midway.
- **§3.2 "Constant Lead Threading (G32)", WARNING 6, p.32:** a threading block that follows a threading block starts "without waiting for detection of the one-spindle-rotation signal".
- **§3.2, pp.29-31:** G32 cuts tapers (`G32 X41.0 Z29.0 F3.5`). Up to 45° the lead F is taken along Z.

The manual was read from a public third-party mirror of Fanuc's PDF (https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/fanuc-0itd-users-manualpdf/259106078), for behaviour only. The Haas G32 reference (cited in #363) agrees. **LinuxCNC G33 stays unconfirmed:** its docs don't say whether a chained G33 waits for the index again, so no LinuxCNC post may declare the capability.

## What changed
- **Parameters.** The infeed plan gains `ThreadInfeed.dips` with interval, height and length. An interval of 0 means off, which is the default.
- **Shape of a dip.** A dip is a radial lift on **roughing passes only**. Each ramp stays under 45°, keeping the lead on Z.
  - **Never placed in:** the first or last lead, or the finishing, spring or #418 repeat passes.
  - **Height:** no more than every dipped pass's depth of cut.
- **New CL segment.** A dip is a variable-radius XY half-turn: the axial travel is still exactly half a lead, but the end radius differs from the start.
- **Marking.** The thread record carries `chip_break_dips`: `DIP 1` in the stream, `ChipBreakDips` as a post property, and a project cache key only when set. The section carries `PARAM ChipBreakDips`. If dips are on but the record can't be attached, the kernel refuses, so a dip is never laid unmarked.
- **Post capability flag.** The engine refuses dips by name for any script without `continuousThreading = true`. Only `fanuc-lathe.cps` declares it, with the citation in its header.
  - It writes each dip segment as `G32 X Z F`.
  - It refuses by name a segment that doesn't continue a G32 chain, is steeper than 45°, or goes deeper than its plunge.
  - **G76 refuses dips by name.**
- **Verdict.** `thread_warnings` checks every chain for phase (equal axial advance per half-turn), depth, slope and placement. Any breach is a Gouge, which blocks the post.
- **UI.** Three rows on the Passes tab.
- **Defaults are byte-identical.** With dips off there is no stamp byte, project key, stream word or PARAM.
- `docs/decisions/419-thread-dips.md`

## How tested
- **New motion `turning_thread_dips`** (8 tests):
  - dips off lay the plain path bit for bit;
  - a dip is never deeper than its pass;
  - the phase is unchanged across the chain;
  - placement and slope rules hold;
  - a repeated depth cuts whole;
  - the verdict is silent on laid dips;
  - the verdict convicts each broken law (first/last lead, finishing pass, deeper, phase shift, steep). Temporarily disabling the laws made this test fail.
  - refusals by name.
- **New app `lathe_post_thread_dips`** (6 tests):
  - the golden `thread_g32_dips.nc`;
  - the posted chain keeps the plain thread's Z words and lead;
  - G76 refuses;
  - a post without `continuousThreading` refuses;
  - the lathe script refuses a bent dip;
  - dips ride the command, the stream and the project file.
- **Existing suites green:** the turning thread, infeed and G76 suites, `inverted_post`, `lathe_post*`, `project_roundtrip`, `conformance`, and all cl and post tests. No existing golden changed.
- `clippy -D warnings --all-targets` on motion, post, cl, app and ui is clean.

## Not exercised (draft)
- **Machine check:** a run on a lathe simulator or machine.
- **GUI check:** the Passes-tab rows. The #416 test kit covers the neighbouring rows.

Changelog: Threading: optional in-pass chip-break dips on roughing passes, posted as continuous G32 X Z F segments by the Fanuc lathe post (#419)

Fixes #419
